text: “No, I don’t believe it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And I believe you don’t, and that you speak the truth. You look sincere and you speak sincerely. But not Ivan. Ivan’s supercilious.... I’d make an end of your monks, though, all the same. I’d take all that mystic stuff and suppress it, once for all, all over Russia, so as to bring all the fools to reason. And the gold and the silver that would flow into the mint!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But why suppress it?” asked Ivan.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That Truth may prevail. That’s why.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, if Truth were to prevail, you know, you’d be the first to be robbed and suppressed.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah! I dare say you’re right. Ah, I’m an ass!” burst out Fyodor Pavlovitch, striking himself lightly on the forehead.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, your monastery may stand then, Alyosha, if that’s how it is. And we clever people will sit snug and enjoy our brandy. You know, Ivan, it must have been so ordained by the Almighty Himself. Ivan, speak, is there a God or not? Stay, speak the truth, speak seriously. Why are you laughing again?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’m laughing that you should have made a clever remark just now about Smerdyakov’s belief in the existence of two saints who could move mountains.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, am I like him now, then?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Very much.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, that shows I’m a Russian, too, and I have a Russian characteristic. And you may be caught in the same way, though you are a philosopher. Shall I catch you? What do you bet that I’ll catch you to-morrow. Speak, all the same, is there a God, or not? Only, be serious. I want you to be serious now.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, there is no God.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alyosha, is there a God?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There is.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ivan, and is there immortality of some sort, just a little, just a tiny bit?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There is no immortality either.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “None at all?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “None at all.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There’s absolute nothingness then. Perhaps there is just something? Anything is better than nothing!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Absolute nothingness.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alyosha, is there immortality?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There is.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “God and immortality?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “God and immortality. In God is immortality.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “H’m! It’s more likely Ivan’s right. Good Lord! to think what faith, what force of all kinds, man has lavished for nothing, on that dream, and for how many thousand years. Who is it laughing at man? Ivan! For the last time, once for all, is there a God or not? I ask for the last time!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And for the last time there is not.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Who is laughing at mankind, Ivan?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It must be the devil,” said Ivan, smiling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And the devil? Does he exist?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, there’s no devil either.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s a pity. Damn it all, what wouldn’t I do to the man who first invented God! Hanging on a bitter aspen tree would be too good for him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There would have been no civilization if they hadn’t invented God.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Wouldn’t there have been? Without God?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No. And there would have been no brandy either. But I must take your brandy away from you, anyway.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Stop, stop, stop, dear boy, one more little glass. I’ve hurt Alyosha’s feelings. You’re not angry with me, Alyosha? My dear little Alexey!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, I am not angry. I know your thoughts. Your heart is better than your head.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “My heart better than my head, is it? Oh, Lord! And that from you. Ivan, do you love Alyosha?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You must love him” (Fyodor Pavlovitch was by this time very drunk).

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Listen, Alyosha, I was rude to your elder this morning. But I was excited. But there’s wit in that elder, don’t you think, Ivan?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Very likely.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There is, there is. Il y a du Piron là-dedans. He’s a Jesuit, a Russian one, that is. As he’s an honorable person there’s a hidden indignation boiling within him at having to pretend and affect holiness.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But, of course, he believes in God.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not a bit of it. Didn’t you know? Why, he tells every one so, himself. That is, not every one, but all the clever people who come to him. He said straight out to Governor Schultz not long ago: ‘Credo, but I don’t know in what.’”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Really?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He really did. But I respect him. There’s something of Mephistopheles about him, or rather of ‘The hero of our time’ ... Arbenin, or what’s his name?... You see, he’s a sensualist. He’s such a sensualist that I should be afraid for my daughter or my wife if she went to confess to him. You know, when he begins telling stories.... The year before last he invited us to tea, tea with liqueur (the ladies send him liqueur), and began telling us about old times till we nearly split our sides.... Especially how he once cured a paralyzed woman. ‘If my legs were not bad I know a dance I could dance you,’ he said. What do you say to that? ‘I’ve plenty of tricks in my time,’ said he. He did Dernidov, the merchant, out of sixty thousand.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What, he stole it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He brought him the money as a man he could trust, saying, ‘Take care of it for me, friend, there’ll be a police search at my place to-morrow. And he kept it. ‘You have given it to the Church,’ he declared. I said to him: ‘You’re a scoundrel,’ I said. ‘No,’ said he, ‘I’m not a scoundrel, but I’m broad-minded. But that wasn’t he, that was some one else. I’ve muddled him with some one else ... without noticing it. Come, another glass and that’s enough. Take away the bottle, Ivan. I’ve been telling lies. Why didn’t you stop me, Ivan, and tell me I was lying?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I knew you’d stop of yourself.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s a lie. You did it from spite, from simple spite against me. You despise me. You have come to me and despised me in my own house.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, I’m going away. You’ve had too much brandy.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve begged you for Christ’s sake to go to Tchermashnya for a day or two, and you don’t go.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ll go to-morrow if you’re so set upon it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You won’t go. You want to keep an eye on me. That’s what you want, spiteful fellow. That’s why you won’t go.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The old man persisted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had reached that state of drunkenness when the drunkard who has till then been inoffensive tries to pick a quarrel and to assert himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why are you looking at me? Why do you look like that? Your eyes look at me and say, ‘You ugly drunkard! Your eyes are mistrustful. They’re contemptuous.... You’ve come here with some design. Alyosha, here, looks at me and his eyes shine. Alyosha doesn’t despise me. Alexey, you mustn’t love Ivan.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t be ill-tempered with my brother. Leave off attacking him,” Alyosha said emphatically.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, all right. Ugh, my head aches. Take away the brandy, Ivan. It’s the third time I’ve told you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He mused, and suddenly a slow, cunning grin spread over his face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t be angry with a feeble old man, Ivan. I know you don’t love me, but don’t be angry all the same. You’ve nothing to love me for. You go to Tchermashnya. I’ll come to you myself and bring you a present. I’ll show you a little wench there. I’ve had my eye on her a long time. She’s still running about bare-foot. Don’t be afraid of bare-footed wenches—don’t despise them—they’re pearls!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And he kissed his hand with a smack.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “To my thinking,” he revived at once, seeming to grow sober the instant he touched on his favorite topic.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “To my thinking ... Ah, you boys! You children, little sucking-pigs, to my thinking ... I never thought a woman ugly in my life—that’s been my rule! Can you understand that? How could you understand it? You’ve milk in your veins, not blood. You’re not out of your shells yet. My rule has been that you can always find something devilishly interesting in every woman that you wouldn’t find in any other. Only, one must know how to find it, that’s the point! That’s a talent! To my mind there are no ugly women. The very fact that she is a woman is half the battle ... but how could you understand that? Even in vieilles filles, even in them you may discover something that makes you simply wonder that men have been such fools as to let them grow old without noticing them. Bare-footed girls or unattractive ones, you must take by surprise. Didn’t you know that? You must astound them till they’re fascinated, upset, ashamed that such a gentleman should fall in love with such a little slut. It’s a jolly good thing that there always are and will be masters and slaves in the world, so there always will be a little maid-of-all-work and her master, and you know, that’s all that’s needed for happiness. Stay ... listen, Alyosha, I always used to surprise your mother, but in a different way. I paid no attention to her at all, but all at once, when the minute came, I’d be all devotion to her, crawl on my knees, kiss her feet, and I always, always—I remember it as though it were to-day—reduced her to that tinkling, quiet, nervous, queer little laugh. It was peculiar to her. I knew her attacks always used to begin like that. The next day she would begin shrieking hysterically, and this little laugh was not a sign of delight, though it made a very good counterfeit. That’s the great thing, to know how to take every one. Once Belyavsky—he was a handsome fellow, and rich—used to like to come here and hang about her—suddenly gave me a slap in the face in her presence. And she—such a mild sheep—why, I thought she would have knocked me down for that blow. How she set on me! ‘You’re beaten, beaten now,’ she said. ‘You’ve taken a blow from him. You have been trying to sell me to him,’ she said.... ‘And how dared he strike you in my presence! Don’t dare come near me again, never, never! Run at once, challenge him to a duel!’... I took her to the monastery then to bring her to her senses. The holy Fathers prayed her back to reason. But I swear, by God, Alyosha, I never insulted the poor crazy girl! Only once, perhaps, in the first year; then she was very fond of praying. She used to keep the feasts of Our Lady particularly and used to turn me out of her room then. I’ll knock that mysticism out of her, thought I! ‘Here,’ said I, ‘you see your holy image. Here it is. Here I take it down. You believe it’s miraculous, but here, I’ll spit on it directly and nothing will happen to me for it!’... When she saw it, good Lord! I thought she would kill me. But she only jumped up, wrung her hands, then suddenly hid her face in them, began trembling all over and fell on the floor ... fell all of a heap. Alyosha, Alyosha, what’s the matter?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The old man jumped up in alarm.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: From the time he had begun speaking about his mother, a change had gradually come over Alyosha’s face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He flushed crimson, his eyes glowed, his lips quivered.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The old sot had gone spluttering on, noticing nothing, till the moment when something very strange happened to Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Precisely what he was describing in the crazy woman was suddenly repeated with Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He jumped up from his seat exactly as his mother was said to have done, wrung his hands, hid his face in them, and fell back in his chair, shaking all over in an hysterical paroxysm of sudden violent, silent weeping.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His extraordinary resemblance to his mother particularly impressed the old man.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ivan, Ivan! Water, quickly! It’s like her, exactly as she used to be then, his mother. Spurt some water on him from your mouth, that’s what I used to do to her. He’s upset about his mother, his mother,” he muttered to Ivan.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But she was my mother, too, I believe, his mother. Was she not?” said Ivan, with uncontrolled anger and contempt.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The old man shrank before his flashing eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But something very strange had happened, though only for a second; it seemed really to have escaped the old man’s mind that Alyosha’s mother actually was the mother of Ivan too.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Your mother?” he muttered, not understanding.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What do you mean?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What mother are you talking about?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Was she?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why, damn it! of course she was yours too!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Damn it!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: My mind has never been so darkened before.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Excuse me, why, I was thinking, Ivan....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He he he!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He stopped.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A broad, drunken, half-senseless grin overspread his face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At that moment a fearful noise and clamor was heard in the hall, there were violent shouts, the door was flung open, and Dmitri burst into the room.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The old man rushed to Ivan in terror.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’ll kill me! He’ll kill me! Don’t let him get at me!” he screamed, clinging to the skirt of Ivan’s coat.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grigory and Smerdyakov ran into the room after Dmitri.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They had been struggling with him in the passage, refusing to admit him, acting on instructions given them by Fyodor Pavlovitch some days before.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Taking advantage of the fact that Dmitri stopped a moment on entering the room to look about him, Grigory ran round the table, closed the double doors on the opposite side of the room leading to the inner apartments, and stood before the closed doors, stretching wide his arms, prepared to defend the entrance, so to speak, with the last drop of his blood.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Seeing this, Dmitri uttered a scream rather than a shout and rushed at Grigory.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Then she’s there! She’s hidden there! Out of the way, scoundrel!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He tried to pull Grigory away, but the old servant pushed him back.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Beside himself with fury, Dmitri struck out, and hit Grigory with all his might.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The old man fell like a log, and Dmitri, leaping over him, broke in the door.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Smerdyakov remained pale and trembling at the other end of the room, huddling close to Fyodor Pavlovitch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “She’s here!” shouted Dmitri.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I saw her turn towards the house just now, but I couldn’t catch her. Where is she? Where is she?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That shout, “She’s here!” produced an indescribable effect on Fyodor Pavlovitch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All his terror left him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Hold him! Hold him!” he cried, and dashed after Dmitri.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Meanwhile Grigory had got up from the floor, but still seemed stunned.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ivan and Alyosha ran after their father.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In the third room something was heard to fall on the floor with a ringing crash: it was a large glass vase—not an expensive one—on a marble pedestal which Dmitri had upset as he ran past it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “At him!” shouted the old man.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Help!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ivan and Alyosha caught the old man and were forcibly bringing him back.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why do you run after him? He’ll murder you outright,” Ivan cried wrathfully at his father.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ivan! Alyosha! She must be here. Grushenka’s here. He said he saw her himself, running.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was choking.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was not expecting Grushenka at the time, and the sudden news that she was here made him beside himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was trembling all over.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He seemed frantic.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But you’ve seen for yourself that she hasn’t come,” cried Ivan.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But she may have come by that other entrance.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You know that entrance is locked, and you have the key.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Dmitri suddenly reappeared in the drawing-room.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had, of course, found the other entrance locked, and the key actually was in Fyodor Pavlovitch’s pocket.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The windows of all the rooms were also closed, so Grushenka could not have come in anywhere nor have run out anywhere.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Hold him!” shrieked Fyodor Pavlovitch, as soon as he saw him again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’s been stealing money in my bedroom.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And tearing himself from Ivan he rushed again at Dmitri.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Dmitri threw up both hands and suddenly clutched the old man by the two tufts of hair that remained on his temples, tugged at them, and flung him with a crash on the floor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He kicked him two or three times with his heel in the face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The old man moaned shrilly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ivan, though not so strong as Dmitri, threw his arms round him, and with all his might pulled him away.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha helped him with his slender strength, holding Dmitri in front.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Madman! You’ve killed him!” cried Ivan.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Serve him right!” shouted Dmitri breathlessly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “If I haven’t killed him, I’ll come again and kill him. You can’t protect him!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Dmitri! Go away at once!” cried Alyosha commandingly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alexey! You tell me. It’s only you I can believe; was she here just now, or not? I saw her myself creeping this way by the fence from the lane. I shouted, she ran away.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I swear she’s not been here, and no one expected her.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But I saw her.... So she must ... I’ll find out at once where she is.... Good-by, Alexey! Not a word to Æsop about the money now. But go to Katerina Ivanovna at once and be sure to say, ‘He sends his compliments to you! Compliments, his compliments! Just compliments and farewell! Describe the scene to her.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Meanwhile Ivan and Grigory had raised the old man and seated him in an arm-chair.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His face was covered with blood, but he was conscious and listened greedily to Dmitri’s cries.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was still fancying that Grushenka really was somewhere in the house.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Dmitri looked at him with hatred as he went out.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t repent shedding your blood!” he cried.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Beware, old man, beware of your dream, for I have my dream, too. I curse you, and disown you altogether.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He ran out of the room.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “She’s here. She must be here. Smerdyakov! Smerdyakov!” the old man wheezed, scarcely audibly, beckoning to him with his finger.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, she’s not here, you old lunatic! Ivan shouted at him angrily. “Here, he’s fainting! Water! A towel! Make haste, Smerdyakov!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Smerdyakov ran for water.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At last they got the old man undressed, and put him to bed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They wrapped a wet towel round his head.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Exhausted by the brandy, by his violent emotion, and the blows he had received, he shut his eyes and fell asleep as soon as his head touched the pillow.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ivan and Alyosha went back to the drawing-room.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Smerdyakov removed the fragments of the broken vase, while Grigory stood by the table looking gloomily at the floor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Shouldn’t you put a wet bandage on your head and go to bed, too? Alyosha said to him. “We’ll look after him. My brother gave you a terrible blow—on the head.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’s insulted me!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grigory articulated gloomily and distinctly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’s ‘insulted’ his father, not only you,” observed Ivan with a forced smile.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I used to wash him in his tub. He’s insulted me,” repeated Grigory.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Damn it all, if I hadn’t pulled him away perhaps he’d have murdered him. It wouldn’t take much to do for Æsop, would it?” whispered Ivan to Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “God forbid!” cried Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why should He forbid? Ivan went on in the same whisper, with a malignant grimace. “One reptile will devour the other. And serve them both right, too.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha shuddered.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Of course I won’t let him be murdered as I didn’t just now. Stay here, Alyosha, I’ll go for a turn in the yard. My head’s begun to ache.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha went to his father’s bedroom and sat by his bedside behind the screen for about an hour.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The old man suddenly opened his eyes and gazed for a long while at Alyosha, evidently remembering and meditating.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All at once his face betrayed extraordinary excitement.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alyosha,” he whispered apprehensively, “where’s Ivan?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “In the yard. He’s got a headache. He’s on the watch.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Give me that looking-glass. It stands over there. Give it me.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha gave him a little round folding looking-glass which stood on the chest of drawers.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The old man looked at himself in it; his nose was considerably swollen, and on the left side of his forehead there was a rather large crimson bruise.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What does Ivan say? Alyosha, my dear, my only son, I’m afraid of Ivan. I’m more afraid of Ivan than the other. You’re the only one I’m not afraid of....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t be afraid of Ivan either. He is angry, but he’ll defend you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alyosha, and what of the other? He’s run to Grushenka. My angel, tell me the truth, was she here just now or not?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No one has seen her. It was a mistake. She has not been here.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You know Mitya wants to marry her, to marry her.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “She won’t marry him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “She won’t. She won’t. She won’t. She won’t on any account!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The old man fairly fluttered with joy, as though nothing more comforting could have been said to him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In his delight he seized Alyosha’s hand and pressed it warmly to his heart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Tears positively glittered in his eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That image of the Mother of God of which I was telling you just now,” he said.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Take it home and keep it for yourself. And I’ll let you go back to the monastery.... I was joking this morning, don’t be angry with me. My head aches, Alyosha.... Alyosha, comfort my heart. Be an angel and tell me the truth!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’re still asking whether she has been here or not?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha said sorrowfully.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, no, no. I believe you. I’ll tell you what it is: you go to Grushenka yourself, or see her somehow; make haste and ask her; see for yourself, which she means to choose, him or me. Eh? What? Can you?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “If I see her I’ll ask her,” Alyosha muttered, embarrassed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, she won’t tell you,” the old man interrupted, “she’s a rogue. She’ll begin kissing you and say that it’s you she wants. She’s a deceitful, shameless hussy. You mustn’t go to her, you mustn’t!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, father, and it wouldn’t be suitable, it wouldn’t be right at all.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Where was he sending you just now? He shouted ‘Go’ as he ran away.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “To Katerina Ivanovna.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “For money? To ask her for money?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No. Not for money.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’s no money; not a farthing. I’ll settle down for the night, and think things over, and you can go. Perhaps you’ll meet her.... Only be sure to come to me to-morrow in the morning. Be sure to. I have a word to say to you to-morrow. Will you come?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

What a sweet hand—what a sweet hand you have! You sweet young lady, you incredible beauty!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She slowly raised the hands to her lips, with the strange object indeed of “being even” with her in kisses.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Katerina Ivanovna did not take her hand away.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She listened with timid hope to the last words, though Grushenka’s promise to do her bidding like a slave was very strangely expressed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She looked intently into her eyes; she still saw in those eyes the same simple-hearted, confiding expression, the same bright gayety.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “She’s perhaps too naïve,” thought Katerina Ivanovna, with a gleam of hope.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka meanwhile seemed enthusiastic over the “sweet hand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She raised it deliberately to her lips.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But she held it for two or three minutes near her lips, as though reconsidering something.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do you know, angel lady,” she suddenly drawled in an even more soft and sugary voice, “do you know, after all, I think I won’t kiss your hand?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And she laughed a little merry laugh.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “As you please. What’s the matter with you?” said Katerina Ivanovna, starting suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So that you may be left to remember that you kissed my hand, but I didn’t kiss yours.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was a sudden gleam in her eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She looked with awful intentness at Katerina Ivanovna.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Insolent creature!” cried Katerina Ivanovna, as though suddenly grasping something.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She flushed all over and leapt up from her seat.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka too got up, but without haste.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So I shall tell Mitya how you kissed my hand, but I didn’t kiss yours at all. And how he will laugh!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Vile slut! Go away!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah, for shame, young lady! Ah, for shame! That’s unbecoming for you, dear young lady, a word like that.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Go away! You’re a creature for sale!” screamed Katerina Ivanovna.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Every feature was working in her utterly distorted face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “For sale indeed! You used to visit gentlemen in the dusk for money once; you brought your beauty for sale. You see, I know.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Katerina Ivanovna shrieked, and would have rushed at her, but Alyosha held her with all his strength.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not a step, not a word! Don’t speak, don’t answer her. She’ll go away—she’ll go at once.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At that instant Katerina Ivanovna’s two aunts ran in at her cry, and with them a maid-servant.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All hurried to her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I will go away,” said Grushenka, taking up her mantle from the sofa.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alyosha, darling, see me home!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Go away—go away, make haste!” cried Alyosha, clasping his hands imploringly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Dear little Alyosha, see me home! I’ve got a pretty little story to tell you on the way. I got up this scene for your benefit, Alyosha. See me home, dear, you’ll be glad of it afterwards.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha turned away, wringing his hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka ran out of the house, laughing musically.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Katerina Ivanovna went into a fit of hysterics.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She sobbed, and was shaken with convulsions.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Every one fussed round her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I warned you,” said the elder of her aunts.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I tried to prevent your doing this. You’re too impulsive. How could you do such a thing? You don’t know these creatures, and they say she’s worse than any of them. You are too self-willed.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “She’s a tigress!” yelled Katerina Ivanovna.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why did you hold me, Alexey Fyodorovitch? I’d have beaten her—beaten her!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She could not control herself before Alyosha; perhaps she did not care to, indeed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “She ought to be flogged in public on a scaffold!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha withdrew towards the door.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But, my God!” cried Katerina Ivanovna, clasping her hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He! He! He could be so dishonorable, so inhuman! Why, he told that creature what happened on that fatal, accursed day! ‘You brought your beauty for sale, dear young lady. She knows it! Your brother’s a scoundrel, Alexey Fyodorovitch.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha wanted to say something, but he couldn’t find a word.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His heart ached.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Go away, Alexey Fyodorovitch! It’s shameful, it’s awful for me! To-morrow, I beg you on my knees, come to-morrow. Don’t condemn me. Forgive me. I don’t know what I shall do with myself now!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha walked out into the street reeling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He could have wept as she did.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Suddenly he was overtaken by the maid.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The young lady forgot to give you this letter from Madame Hohlakov; it’s been left with us since dinner-time.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha took the little pink envelope mechanically and put it, almost unconsciously, into his pocket.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was not much more than three-quarters of a mile from the town to the monastery.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha walked quickly along the road, at that hour deserted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was almost night, and too dark to see anything clearly at thirty paces ahead.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There were cross-roads half-way.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A figure came into sight under a solitary willow at the cross-roads.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As soon as Alyosha reached the cross-roads the figure moved out and rushed at him, shouting savagely:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Your money or your life!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So it’s you, Mitya,” cried Alyosha, in surprise, violently startled however.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ha ha ha! You didn’t expect me? I wondered where to wait for you. By her house? There are three ways from it, and I might have missed you. At last I thought of waiting here, for you had to pass here, there’s no other way to the monastery. Come, tell me the truth. Crush me like a beetle. But what’s the matter?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nothing, brother—it’s the fright you gave me. Oh, Dmitri! Father’s blood just now.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: (Alyosha began to cry, he had been on the verge of tears for a long time, and now something seemed to snap in his soul.)

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You almost killed him—cursed him—and now—here—you’re making jokes—‘Your money or your life!’”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, what of that? It’s not seemly—is that it? Not suitable in my position?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No—I only—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Stay. Look at the night. You see what a dark night, what clouds, what a wind has risen. I hid here under the willow waiting for you. And as God’s above, I suddenly thought, why go on in misery any longer, what is there to wait for? Here I have a willow, a handkerchief, a shirt, I can twist them into a rope in a minute, and braces besides, and why go on burdening the earth, dishonoring it with my vile presence? And then I heard you coming—Heavens, it was as though something flew down to me suddenly. So there is a man, then, whom I love. Here he is, that man, my dear little brother, whom I love more than any one in the world, the only one I love in the world. And I loved you so much, so much at that moment that I thought, ‘I’ll fall on his neck at once. Then a stupid idea struck me, to have a joke with you and scare you. I shouted, like a fool, ‘Your money! Forgive my foolery—it was only nonsense, and there’s nothing unseemly in my soul.... Damn it all, tell me what’s happened. What did she say? Strike me, crush me, don’t spare me! Was she furious?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, not that.... There was nothing like that, Mitya. There—I found them both there.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Both? Whom?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Grushenka at Katerina Ivanovna’s.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Dmitri was struck dumb.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Impossible!” he cried.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’re raving! Grushenka with her?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha described all that had happened from the moment he went in to Katerina Ivanovna’s.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was ten minutes telling his story.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He can’t be said to have told it fluently and consecutively, but he seemed to make it clear, not omitting any word or action of significance, and vividly describing, often in one word, his own sensations.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Dmitri listened in silence, gazing at him with a terrible fixed stare, but it was clear to Alyosha that he understood it all, and had grasped every point.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But as the story went on, his face became not merely gloomy, but menacing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He scowled, he clenched his teeth, and his fixed stare became still more rigid, more concentrated, more terrible, when suddenly, with incredible rapidity, his wrathful, savage face changed, his tightly compressed lips parted, and Dmitri Fyodorovitch broke into uncontrolled, spontaneous laughter.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He literally shook with laughter.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For a long time he could not speak.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So she wouldn’t kiss her hand! So she didn’t kiss it; so she ran away!” he kept exclaiming with hysterical delight; insolent delight it might have been called, if it had not been so spontaneous.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So the other one called her tigress! And a tigress she is! So she ought to be flogged on a scaffold? Yes, yes, so she ought. That’s just what I think; she ought to have been long ago. It’s like this, brother, let her be punished, but I must get better first. I understand the queen of impudence. That’s her all over! You saw her all over in that hand-kissing, the she-devil! She’s magnificent in her own line! So she ran home? I’ll go—ah—I’ll run to her! Alyosha, don’t blame me, I agree that hanging is too good for her.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But Katerina Ivanovna!” exclaimed Alyosha sorrowfully.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I see her, too! I see right through her, as I’ve never done before! It’s a regular discovery of the four continents of the world, that is, of the five! What a thing to do! That’s just like Katya, who was not afraid to face a coarse, unmannerly officer and risk a deadly insult on a generous impulse to save her father! But the pride, the recklessness, the defiance of fate, the unbounded defiance! You say that aunt tried to stop her? That aunt, you know, is overbearing, herself. She’s the sister of the general’s widow in Moscow, and even more stuck-up than she. But her husband was caught stealing government money. He lost everything, his estate and all, and the proud wife had to lower her colors, and hasn’t raised them since. So she tried to prevent Katya, but she wouldn’t listen to her! She thinks she can overcome everything, that everything will give way to her. She thought she could bewitch Grushenka if she liked, and she believed it herself: she plays a part to herself, and whose fault is it? Do you think she kissed Grushenka’s hand first, on purpose, with a motive? No, she really was fascinated by Grushenka, that’s to say, not by Grushenka, but by her own dream, her own delusion—because it was her dream, her delusion! Alyosha, darling, how did you escape from them, those women? Did you pick up your cassock and run? Ha ha ha!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Brother, you don’t seem to have noticed how you’ve insulted Katerina Ivanovna by telling Grushenka about that day. And she flung it in her face just now that she had gone to gentlemen in secret to sell her beauty! Brother, what could be worse than that insult?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What worried Alyosha more than anything was that, incredible as it seemed, his brother appeared pleased at Katerina Ivanovna’s humiliation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Bah! Dmitri frowned fiercely, and struck his forehead with his hand. He only now realized it, though Alyosha had just told him of the insult, and Katerina Ivanovna’s cry: “Your brother is a scoundrel!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, perhaps, I really did tell Grushenka about that ‘fatal day,’ as Katya calls it. Yes, I did tell her, I remember! It was that time at Mokroe. I was drunk, the gypsies were singing.... But I was sobbing. I was sobbing then, kneeling and praying to Katya’s image, and Grushenka understood it. She understood it all then. I remember, she cried herself.... Damn it all! But it’s bound to be so now.... Then she cried, but now ‘the dagger in the heart’! That’s how women are.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He looked down and sank into thought.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, I am a scoundrel, a thorough scoundrel!” he said suddenly, in a gloomy voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It doesn’t matter whether I cried or not, I’m a scoundrel! Tell her I accept the name, if that’s any comfort. Come, that’s enough. Good-by. It’s no use talking! It’s not amusing. You go your way and I mine. And I don’t want to see you again except as a last resource. Good-by, Alexey!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He warmly pressed Alyosha’s hand, and still looking down, without raising his head, as though tearing himself away, turned rapidly towards the town.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha looked after him, unable to believe he would go away so abruptly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Stay, Alexey, one more confession to you alone!” cried Dmitri, suddenly turning back.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Look at me. Look at me well. You see here, here—there’s terrible disgrace in store for me.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: (As he said “here,” Dmitri struck his chest with his fist with a strange air, as though the dishonor lay precisely on his chest, in some spot, in a pocket, perhaps, or hanging round his neck.)

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You know me now, a scoundrel, an avowed scoundrel, but let me tell you that I’ve never done anything before and never shall again, anything that can compare in baseness with the dishonor which I bear now at this very minute on my breast, here, here, which will come to pass, though I’m perfectly free to stop it. I can stop it or carry it through, note that. Well, let me tell you, I shall carry it through. I shan’t stop it. I told you everything just now, but I didn’t tell you this, because even I had not brass enough for it. I can still pull up; if I do, I can give back the full half of my lost honor to-morrow. But I shan’t pull up. I shall carry out my base plan, and you can bear witness that I told you so beforehand. Darkness and destruction! No need to explain. You’ll find out in due time. The filthy back-alley and the she-devil. Good-by. Don’t pray for me, I’m not worth it. And there’s no need, no need at all.... I don’t need it! Away!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And he suddenly retreated, this time finally.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha went towards the monastery.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What? I shall never see him again! What is he saying?” he wondered wildly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, I shall certainly see him to-morrow. I shall look him up. I shall make a point of it. What does he mean?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He went round the monastery, and crossed the pine-wood to the hermitage.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The door was opened to him, though no one was admitted at that hour.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was a tremor in his heart as he went into Father Zossima’s cell.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, why, had he gone forth? Why had he sent him into the world? Here was peace. Here was holiness. But there was confusion, there was darkness in which one lost one’s way and went astray at once....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In the cell he found the novice Porfiry and Father Païssy, who came every hour to inquire after Father Zossima.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha learnt with alarm that he was getting worse and worse.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Even his usual discourse with the brothers could not take place that day.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As a rule every evening after service the monks flocked into Father Zossima’s cell, and all confessed aloud their sins of the day, their sinful thoughts and temptations; even their disputes, if there had been any.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Some confessed kneeling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The elder absolved, reconciled, exhorted, imposed penance, blessed, and dismissed them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was against this general “confession” that the opponents of “elders” protested, maintaining that it was a profanation of the sacrament of confession, almost a sacrilege, though this was quite a different thing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They even represented to the diocesan authorities that such confessions attained no good object, but actually to a large extent led to sin and temptation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Many of the brothers disliked going to the elder, and went against their own will because every one went, and for fear they should be accused of pride and rebellious ideas.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: People said that some of the monks agreed beforehand, saying, “I’ll confess I lost my temper with you this morning, and you confirm it,” simply in order to have something to say.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha knew that this actually happened sometimes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He knew, too, that there were among the monks some who deeply resented the fact that letters from relations were habitually taken to the elder, to be opened and read by him before those to whom they were addressed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was assumed, of course, that all this was done freely, and in good faith, by way of voluntary submission and salutary guidance.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But, in fact, there was sometimes no little insincerity, and much that was false and strained in this practice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yet the older and more experienced of the monks adhered to their opinion, arguing that “for those who have come within these walls sincerely seeking salvation, such obedience and sacrifice will certainly be salutary and of great benefit; those, on the other hand, who find it irksome, and repine, are no true monks, and have made a mistake in entering the monastery—their proper place is in the world. Even in the temple one cannot be safe from sin and the devil. So it was no good taking it too much into account.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He is weaker, a drowsiness has come over him,” Father Païssy whispered to Alyosha, as he blessed him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s difficult to rouse him. And he must not be roused. He waked up for five minutes, sent his blessing to the brothers, and begged their prayers for him at night. He intends to take the sacrament again in the morning. He remembered you, Alexey. He asked whether you had gone away, and was told that you were in the town. ‘I blessed him for that work,’ he said, ‘his place is there, not here, for awhile. Those were his words about you. He remembered you lovingly, with anxiety; do you understand how he honored you? But how is it that he has decided that you shall spend some time in the world? He must have foreseen something in your destiny! Understand, Alexey, that if you return to the world, it must be to do the duty laid upon you by your elder, and not for frivolous vanity and worldly pleasures.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Païssy went out.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha had no doubt that Father Zossima was dying, though he might live another day or two.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha firmly and ardently resolved that in spite of his promises to his father, the Hohlakovs, and Katerina Ivanovna, he would not leave the monastery next day, but would remain with his elder to the end.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His heart glowed with love, and he reproached himself bitterly for having been able for one instant to forget him whom he had left in the monastery on his deathbed, and whom he honored above every one in the world.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He went into Father Zossima’s bedroom, knelt down, and bowed to the ground before the elder, who slept quietly without stirring, with regular, hardly audible breathing and a peaceful face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha returned to the other room, where Father Zossima had received his guests in the morning.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Taking off his boots, he lay down on the hard, narrow, leathern sofa, which he had long used as a bed, bringing nothing but a pillow.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The mattress, about which his father had shouted to him that morning, he had long forgotten to lie on.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He took off his cassock, which he used as a covering.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But before going to bed, he fell on his knees and prayed a long time.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In his fervent prayer he did not beseech God to lighten his darkness but only thirsted for the joyous emotion, which always visited his soul after the praise and adoration, of which his evening prayer usually consisted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That joy always brought him light untroubled sleep.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As he was praying, he suddenly felt in his pocket the little pink note the servant had handed him as he left Katerina Ivanovna’s.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was disturbed, but finished his prayer.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Then, after some hesitation, he opened the envelope.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In it was a letter to him, signed by Lise, the young daughter of Madame Hohlakov, who had laughed at him before the elder in the morning.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alexey Fyodorovitch,” she wrote, “I am writing to you without any one’s knowledge, even mamma’s, and I know how wrong it is.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But I cannot live without telling you the feeling that has sprung up in my heart, and this no one but us two must know for a time.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But how am I to say what I want so much to tell you?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Paper, they say, does not blush, but I assure you it’s not true and that it’s blushing just as I am now, all over.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Dear Alyosha, I love you, I’ve loved you from my childhood, since our Moscow days, when you were very different from what you are now, and I shall love you all my life.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: My heart has chosen you, to unite our lives, and pass them together till our old age.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Of course, on condition that you will leave the monastery.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As for our age we will wait for the time fixed by the law.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: By that time I shall certainly be quite strong, I shall be walking and dancing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There can be no doubt of that.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You see how I’ve thought of everything.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There’s only one thing I can’t imagine: what you’ll think of me when you read this.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I’m always laughing and being naughty.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I made you angry this morning, but I assure you before I took up my pen, I prayed before the Image of the Mother of God, and now I’m praying, and almost crying.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “My secret is in your hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: When you come to-morrow, I don’t know how I shall look at you.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ah, Alexey Fyodorovitch, what if I can’t restrain myself like a silly and laugh when I look at you as I did to-day.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: You’ll think I’m a nasty girl making fun of you, and you won’t believe my letter.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And so I beg you, dear one, if you’ve any pity for me, when you come to-morrow, don’t look me straight in the face, for if I meet your eyes, it will be sure to make me laugh, especially as you’ll be in that long gown.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I feel cold all over when I think of it, so when you come, don’t look at me at all for a time, look at mamma or at the window....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Here I’ve written you a love-letter.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh, dear, what have I done?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha, don’t despise me, and if I’ve done something very horrid and wounded you, forgive me.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Now the secret of my reputation, ruined perhaps for ever, is in your hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I shall certainly cry to-day.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Good-by till our meeting, our awful meeting.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: —LISE.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “P.S.—Alyosha! You must, must, must come!—LISE.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha read the note in amazement, read it through twice, thought a little, and suddenly laughed a soft, sweet laugh.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He started.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That laugh seemed to him sinful.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But a minute later he laughed again just as softly and happily.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He slowly replaced the note in the envelope, crossed himself and lay down.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The agitation in his heart passed at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “God, have mercy upon all of them, have all these unhappy and turbulent souls in Thy keeping, and set them in the right path.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All ways are Thine.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Save them according to Thy wisdom.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Thou art love.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Thou wilt send joy to all!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha murmured, crossing himself, and falling into peaceful sleep.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha was roused early, before daybreak.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Zossima woke up feeling very weak, though he wanted to get out of bed and sit up in a chair.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His mind was quite clear; his face looked very tired, yet bright and almost joyful.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It wore an expression of gayety, kindness and cordiality.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Maybe I shall not live through the coming day,” he said to Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Then he desired to confess and take the sacrament at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He always confessed to Father Païssy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: After taking the communion, the service of extreme unction followed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The monks assembled and the cell was gradually filled up by the inmates of the hermitage.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Meantime it was daylight.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: People began coming from the monastery.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: After the service was over the elder desired to kiss and take leave of every one.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As the cell was so small the earlier visitors withdrew to make room for others.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha stood beside the elder, who was seated again in his arm-chair.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He talked as much as he could.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though his voice was weak, it was fairly steady.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve been teaching you so many years, and therefore I’ve been talking aloud so many years, that I’ve got into the habit of talking, and so much so that it’s almost more difficult for me to hold my tongue than to talk, even now, in spite of my weakness, dear Fathers and brothers,” he jested, looking with emotion at the group round him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha remembered afterwards something of what he said to them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But though he spoke out distinctly and his voice was fairly steady, his speech was somewhat disconnected.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He spoke of many things, he seemed anxious before the moment of death to say everything he had not said in his life, and not simply for the sake of instructing them, but as though thirsting to share with all men and all creation his joy and ecstasy, and once more in his life to open his whole heart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Love one another, Fathers,” said Father Zossima, as far as Alyosha could remember afterwards.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Love God’s people. Because we have come here and shut ourselves within these walls, we are no holier than those that are outside, but on the contrary, from the very fact of coming here, each of us has confessed to himself that he is worse than others, than all men on earth.... And the longer the monk lives in his seclusion, the more keenly he must recognize that. Else he would have had no reason to come here. When he realizes that he is not only worse than others, but that he is responsible to all men for all and everything, for all human sins, national and individual, only then the aim of our seclusion is attained. For know, dear ones, that every one of us is undoubtedly responsible for all men and everything on earth, not merely through the general sinfulness of creation, but each one personally for all mankind and every individual man. This knowledge is the crown of life for the monk and for every man. For monks are not a special sort of men, but only what all men ought to be. Only through that knowledge, our heart grows soft with infinite, universal, inexhaustible love. Then every one of you will have the power to win over the whole world by love and to wash away the sins of the world with your tears.... Each of you keep watch over your heart and confess your sins to yourself unceasingly. Be not afraid of your sins, even when perceiving them, if only there be penitence, but make no conditions with God. Again I say, Be not proud. Be proud neither to the little nor to the great. Hate not those who reject you, who insult you, who abuse and slander you. Hate not the atheists, the teachers of evil, the materialists—and I mean not only the good ones—for there are many good ones among them, especially in our day—hate not even the wicked ones. Remember them in your prayers thus: Save, O Lord, all those who have none to pray for them, save too all those who will not pray. And add: it is not in pride that I make this prayer, O Lord, for I am lower than all men.... Love God’s people, let not strangers draw away the flock, for if you slumber in your slothfulness and disdainful pride, or worse still, in covetousness, they will come from all sides and draw away your flock. Expound the Gospel to the people unceasingly ... be not extortionate.... Do not love gold and silver, do not hoard them.... Have faith. Cling to the banner and raise it on high.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the elder spoke more disconnectedly than Alyosha reported his words afterwards.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Sometimes he broke off altogether, as though to take breath, and recover his strength, but he was in a sort of ecstasy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They heard him with emotion, though many wondered at his words and found them obscure....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Afterwards all remembered those words.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: When Alyosha happened for a moment to leave the cell, he was struck by the general excitement and suspense in the monks who were crowding about it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This anticipation showed itself in some by anxiety, in others by devout solemnity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All were expecting that some marvel would happen immediately after the elder’s death.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Their suspense was, from one point of view, almost frivolous, but even the most austere of the monks were affected by it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Païssy’s face looked the gravest of all.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha was mysteriously summoned by a monk to see Rakitin, who had arrived from town with a singular letter for him from Madame Hohlakov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In it she informed Alyosha of a strange and very opportune incident.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It appeared that among the women who had come on the previous day to receive Father Zossima’s blessing, there had been an old woman from the town, a sergeant’s widow, called Prohorovna.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She had inquired whether she might pray for the rest of the soul of her son, Vassenka, who had gone to Irkutsk, and had sent her no news for over a year.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: To which Father Zossima had answered sternly, forbidding her to do so, and saying that to pray for the living as though they were dead was a kind of sorcery.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He afterwards forgave her on account of her ignorance, and added, “as though reading the book of the future” (this was Madame Hohlakov’s expression), words of comfort: “that her son Vassya was certainly alive and he would either come himself very shortly or send a letter, and that she was to go home and expect him. And “Would you believe it?” exclaimed Madame Hohlakov enthusiastically, “the prophecy has been fulfilled literally indeed, and more than that. Scarcely had the old woman reached home when they gave her a letter from Siberia which had been awaiting her. But that was not all; in the letter written on the road from Ekaterinenburg, Vassya informed his mother that he was returning to Russia with an official, and that three weeks after her receiving the letter he hoped “to embrace his mother.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Madame Hohlakov warmly entreated Alyosha to report this new “miracle of prediction” to the Superior and all the brotherhood.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “All, all, ought to know of it!” she concluded.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The letter had been written in haste, the excitement of the writer was apparent in every line of it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Alyosha had no need to tell the monks, for all knew of it already.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Rakitin had commissioned the monk who brought his message “to inform most respectfully his reverence Father Païssy, that he, Rakitin, has a matter to speak of with him, of such gravity that he dare not defer it for a moment, and humbly begs forgiveness for his presumption.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As the monk had given the message to Father Païssy before that to Alyosha, the latter found after reading the letter, there was nothing left for him to do but to hand it to Father Païssy in confirmation of the story.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And even that austere and cautious man, though he frowned as he read the news of the “miracle,” could not completely restrain some inner emotion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His eyes gleamed, and a grave and solemn smile came into his lips.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We shall see greater things!” broke from him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We shall see greater things, greater things yet!” the monks around repeated.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Father Païssy, frowning again, begged all of them, at least for a time, not to speak of the matter “till it be more fully confirmed, seeing there is so much credulity among those of this world, and indeed this might well have chanced naturally,” he added, prudently, as it were to satisfy his conscience, though scarcely believing his own disavowal, a fact his listeners very clearly perceived.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Within the hour the “miracle” was of course known to the whole monastery, and many visitors who had come for the mass.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: No one seemed more impressed by it than the monk who had come the day before from St. Sylvester, from the little monastery of Obdorsk in the far North.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was he who had been standing near Madame Hohlakov the previous day and had asked Father Zossima earnestly, referring to the “healing” of the lady’s daughter, “How can you presume to do such things?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was now somewhat puzzled and did not know whom to believe.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The evening before he had visited Father Ferapont in his cell apart, behind the apiary, and had been greatly impressed and overawed by the visit.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This Father Ferapont was that aged monk so devout in fasting and observing silence who has been mentioned already, as antagonistic to Father Zossima and the whole institution of “elders,” which he regarded as a pernicious and frivolous innovation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was a very formidable opponent, although from his practice of silence he scarcely spoke a word to any one.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What made him formidable was that a number of monks fully shared his feeling, and many of the visitors looked upon him as a great saint and ascetic, although they had no doubt that he was crazy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But it was just his craziness attracted them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Ferapont never went to see the elder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though he lived in the hermitage they did not worry him to keep its regulations, and this too because he behaved as though he were crazy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was seventy-five or more, and he lived in a corner beyond the apiary in an old decaying wooden cell which had been built long ago for another great ascetic, Father Iona, who had lived to be a hundred and five, and of whose saintly doings many curious stories were still extant in the monastery and the neighborhood.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Ferapont had succeeded in getting himself installed in this same solitary cell seven years previously.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was simply a peasant’s hut, though it looked like a chapel, for it contained an extraordinary number of ikons with lamps perpetually burning before them—which men brought to the monastery as offerings to God.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Ferapont had been appointed to look after them and keep the lamps burning.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was said (and indeed it was true) that he ate only two pounds of bread in three days.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The beekeeper, who lived close by the apiary, used to bring him the bread every three days, and even to this man who waited upon him, Father Ferapont rarely uttered a word.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The four pounds of bread, together with the sacrament bread, regularly sent him on Sundays after the late mass by the Father Superior, made up his weekly rations.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The water in his jug was changed every day.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He rarely appeared at mass.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Visitors who came to do him homage saw him sometimes kneeling all day long at prayer without looking round.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If he addressed them, he was brief, abrupt, strange, and almost always rude.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: On very rare occasions, however, he would talk to visitors, but for the most part he would utter some one strange saying which was a complete riddle, and no entreaties would induce him to pronounce a word in explanation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was not a priest, but a simple monk.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was a strange belief, chiefly however among the most ignorant, that Father Ferapont had communication with heavenly spirits and would only converse with them, and so was silent with men.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The monk from Obdorsk, having been directed to the apiary by the beekeeper, who was also a very silent and surly monk, went to the corner where Father Ferapont’s cell stood.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Maybe he will speak as you are a stranger and maybe you’ll get nothing out of him,” the beekeeper had warned him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The monk, as he related afterwards, approached in the utmost apprehension.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was rather late in the evening.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Ferapont was sitting at the door of his cell on a low bench.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A huge old elm was lightly rustling overhead.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was an evening freshness in the air.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The monk from Obdorsk bowed down before the saint and asked his blessing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do you want me to bow down to you, monk?” said Father Ferapont.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Get up!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The monk got up.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Blessing, be blessed! Sit beside me. Where have you come from?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What most struck the poor monk was the fact that in spite of his strict fasting and great age, Father Ferapont still looked a vigorous old man.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was tall, held himself erect, and had a thin, but fresh and healthy face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was no doubt he still had considerable strength.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was of athletic build.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In spite of his great age he was not even quite gray, and still had very thick hair and a full beard, both of which had once been black.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His eyes were gray, large and luminous, but strikingly prominent.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He spoke with a broad accent.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was dressed in a peasant’s long reddish coat of coarse convict cloth (as it used to be called) and had a stout rope round his waist.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His throat and chest were bare.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Beneath his coat, his shirt of the coarsest linen showed almost black with dirt, not having been changed for months.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They said that he wore irons weighing thirty pounds under his coat.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His stockingless feet were thrust in old slippers almost dropping to pieces.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “From the little Obdorsk monastery, from St. Sylvester,” the monk answered humbly, whilst his keen and inquisitive, but rather frightened little eyes kept watch on the hermit.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I have been at your Sylvester’s. I used to stay there. Is Sylvester well?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The monk hesitated.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are a senseless lot! How do you keep the fasts?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Our dietary is according to the ancient conventual rules. During Lent there are no meals provided for Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. For Tuesday and Thursday we have white bread, stewed fruit with honey, wild berries, or salt cabbage and wholemeal stirabout. On Saturday white cabbage soup, noodles with peas, kasha, all with hemp oil. On weekdays we have dried fish and kasha with the cabbage soup. From Monday till Saturday evening, six whole days in Holy Week, nothing is cooked, and we have only bread and water, and that sparingly; if possible not taking food every day, just the same as is ordered for first week in Lent. On Good Friday nothing is eaten. In the same way on the Saturday we have to fast till three o’clock, and then take a little bread and water and drink a single cup of wine. On Holy Thursday we drink wine and have something cooked without oil or not cooked at all, inasmuch as the Laodicean council lays down for Holy Thursday: ‘It is unseemly by remitting the fast on the Holy Thursday to dishonor the whole of Lent! This is how we keep the fast. But what is that compared with you, holy Father,” added the monk, growing more confident, “for all the year round, even at Easter, you take nothing but bread and water, and what we should eat in two days lasts you full seven. It’s truly marvelous—your great abstinence.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And mushrooms?” asked Father Ferapont, suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mushrooms?” repeated the surprised monk.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes. I can give up their bread, not needing it at all, and go away into the forest and live there on the mushrooms or the berries, but they can’t give up their bread here, wherefore they are in bondage to the devil. Nowadays the unclean deny that there is need of such fasting. Haughty and unclean is their judgment.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Och, true,” sighed the monk.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And have you seen devils among them?” asked Ferapont.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Among them? Among whom?” asked the monk, timidly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I went to the Father Superior on Trinity Sunday last year, I haven’t been since. I saw a devil sitting on one man’s chest hiding under his cassock, only his horns poked out; another had one peeping out of his pocket with such sharp eyes, he was afraid of me; another settled in the unclean belly of one, another was hanging round a man’s neck, and so he was carrying him about without seeing him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You—can see spirits?” the monk inquired.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I tell you I can see, I can see through them. When I was coming out from the Superior’s I saw one hiding from me behind the door, and a big one, a yard and a half or more high, with a thick long gray tail, and the tip of his tail was in the crack of the door and I was quick and slammed the door, pinching his tail in it. He squealed and began to struggle, and I made the sign of the cross over him three times. And he died on the spot like a crushed spider. He must have rotted there in the corner and be stinking, but they don’t see, they don’t smell it. It’s a year since I have been there. I reveal it to you, as you are a stranger.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Your words are terrible! But, holy and blessed Father,” said the monk, growing bolder and bolder, “is it true, as they noise abroad even to distant lands about you, that you are in continual communication with the Holy Ghost?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He does fly down at times.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How does he fly down? In what form?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “As a bird.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The Holy Ghost in the form of a dove?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There’s the Holy Ghost and there’s the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit can appear as other birds—sometimes as a swallow, sometimes a goldfinch and sometimes as a blue-tit.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How do you know him from an ordinary tit?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He speaks.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How does he speak, in what language?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Human language.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And what does he tell you?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, to-day he told me that a fool would visit me and would ask me unseemly questions. You want to know too much, monk.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Terrible are your words, most holy and blessed Father,” the monk shook his head.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But there was a doubtful look in his frightened little eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do you see this tree?” asked Father Ferapont, after a pause.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I do, blessed Father.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You think it’s an elm, but for me it has another shape.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What sort of shape?” inquired the monk, after a pause of vain expectation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It happens at night. You see those two branches? In the night it is Christ holding out His arms to me and seeking me with those arms, I see it clearly and tremble. It’s terrible, terrible!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What is there terrible if it’s Christ Himself?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, He’ll snatch me up and carry me away.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alive?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “In the spirit and glory of Elijah, haven’t you heard? He will take me in His arms and bear me away.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though the monk returned to the cell he was sharing with one of the brothers, in considerable perplexity of mind, he still cherished at heart a greater reverence for Father Ferapont than for Father Zossima.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was strongly in favor of fasting, and it was not strange that one who kept so rigid a fast as Father Ferapont should “see marvels. His words seemed certainly queer, but God only could tell what was hidden in those words, and were not worse words and acts commonly seen in those who have sacrificed their intellects for the glory of God? The pinching of the devil’s tail he was ready and eager to believe, and not only in the figurative sense. Besides he had, before visiting the monastery, a strong prejudice against the institution of “elders,” which he only knew of by hearsay and believed to be a pernicious innovation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Before he had been long at the monastery, he had detected the secret murmurings of some shallow brothers who disliked the institution.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
