title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was a bright, clear day, and many of the visitors were thronging about the tombs, which were particularly numerous round the church and scattered here and there about the hermitage.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As he walked round the hermitage, Father Païssy remembered Alyosha and that he had not seen him for some time, not since the night.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And he had no sooner thought of him than he at once noticed him in the farthest corner of the hermitage garden, sitting on the tombstone of a monk who had been famous long ago for his saintliness.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He sat with his back to the hermitage and his face to the wall, and seemed to be hiding behind the tombstone.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Going up to him, Father Païssy saw that he was weeping quietly but bitterly, with his face hidden in his hands, and that his whole frame was shaking with sobs.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Païssy stood over him for a little.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Enough, dear son, enough, dear,” he pronounced with feeling at last.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why do you weep? Rejoice and weep not. Don’t you know that this is the greatest of his days? Think only where he is now, at this moment!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha glanced at him, uncovering his face, which was swollen with crying like a child’s, but turned away at once without uttering a word and hid his face in his hands again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Maybe it is well,” said Father Païssy thoughtfully; “weep if you must, Christ has sent you those tears.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Your touching tears are but a relief to your spirit and will serve to gladden your dear heart,” he added to himself, walking away from Alyosha, and thinking lovingly of him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He moved away quickly, however, for he felt that he too might weep looking at him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Meanwhile the time was passing; the monastery services and the requiems for the dead followed in their due course.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Païssy again took Father Iosif’s place by the coffin and began reading the Gospel.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But before three o’clock in the afternoon that something took place to which I alluded at the end of the last book, something so unexpected by all of us and so contrary to the general hope, that, I repeat, this trivial incident has been minutely remembered to this day in our town and all the surrounding neighborhood.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I may add here, for myself personally, that I feel it almost repulsive to recall that event which caused such frivolous agitation and was such a stumbling-block to many, though in reality it was the most natural and trivial matter.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I should, of course, have omitted all mention of it in my story, if it had not exerted a very strong influence on the heart and soul of the chief, though future, hero of my story, Alyosha, forming a crisis and turning-point in his spiritual development, giving a shock to his intellect, which finally strengthened it for the rest of his life and gave it a definite aim.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And so, to return to our story.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: When before dawn they laid Father Zossima’s body in the coffin and brought it into the front room, the question of opening the windows was raised among those who were around the coffin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But this suggestion made casually by some one was unanswered and almost unnoticed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Some of those present may perhaps have inwardly noticed it, only to reflect that the anticipation of decay and corruption from the body of such a saint was an actual absurdity, calling for compassion (if not a smile) for the lack of faith and the frivolity it implied.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For they expected something quite different.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And, behold, soon after midday there were signs of something, at first only observed in silence by those who came in and out and were evidently each afraid to communicate the thought in his mind.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But by three o’clock those signs had become so clear and unmistakable, that the news swiftly reached all the monks and visitors in the hermitage, promptly penetrated to the monastery, throwing all the monks into amazement, and finally, in the shortest possible time, spread to the town, exciting every one in it, believers and unbelievers alike.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The unbelievers rejoiced, and as for the believers some of them rejoiced even more than the unbelievers, for “men love the downfall and disgrace of the righteous,” as the deceased elder had said in one of his exhortations.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The fact is that a smell of decomposition began to come from the coffin, growing gradually more marked, and by three o’clock it was quite unmistakable.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In all the past history of our monastery, no such scandal could be recalled, and in no other circumstances could such a scandal have been possible, as showed itself in unseemly disorder immediately after this discovery among the very monks themselves.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Afterwards, even many years afterwards, some sensible monks were amazed and horrified, when they recalled that day, that the scandal could have reached such proportions.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For in the past, monks of very holy life had died, God-fearing old men, whose saintliness was acknowledged by all, yet from their humble coffins, too, the breath of corruption had come, naturally, as from all dead bodies, but that had caused no scandal nor even the slightest excitement.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Of course there had been, in former times, saints in the monastery whose memory was carefully preserved and whose relics, according to tradition, showed no signs of corruption.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This fact was regarded by the monks as touching and mysterious, and the tradition of it was cherished as something blessed and miraculous, and as a promise, by God’s grace, of still greater glory from their tombs in the future.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: One such, whose memory was particularly cherished, was an old monk, Job, who had died seventy years before at the age of a hundred and five.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had been a celebrated ascetic, rigid in fasting and silence, and his tomb was pointed out to all visitors on their arrival with peculiar respect and mysterious hints of great hopes connected with it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: (That was the very tomb on which Father Païssy had found Alyosha sitting in the morning.)

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Another memory cherished in the monastery was that of the famous Father Varsonofy, who was only recently dead and had preceded Father Zossima in the eldership.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was reverenced during his lifetime as a crazy saint by all the pilgrims to the monastery.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was a tradition that both of these had lain in their coffins as though alive, that they had shown no signs of decomposition when they were buried and that there had been a holy light in their faces.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And some people even insisted that a sweet fragrance came from their bodies.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yet, in spite of these edifying memories, it would be difficult to explain the frivolity, absurdity and malice that were manifested beside the coffin of Father Zossima.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It is my private opinion that several different causes were simultaneously at work, one of which was the deeply-rooted hostility to the institution of elders as a pernicious innovation, an antipathy hidden deep in the hearts of many of the monks.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Even more powerful was jealousy of the dead man’s saintliness, so firmly established during his lifetime that it was almost a forbidden thing to question it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For though the late elder had won over many hearts, more by love than by miracles, and had gathered round him a mass of loving adherents, none the less, in fact, rather the more on that account he had awakened jealousy and so had come to have bitter enemies, secret and open, not only in the monastery but in the world outside it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He did no one any harm, but “Why do they think him so saintly?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And that question alone, gradually repeated, gave rise at last to an intense, insatiable hatred of him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That, I believe, was why many people were extremely delighted at the smell of decomposition which came so quickly, for not a day had passed since his death.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At the same time there were some among those who had been hitherto reverently devoted to the elder, who were almost mortified and personally affronted by this incident.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This was how the thing happened.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As soon as signs of decomposition had begun to appear, the whole aspect of the monks betrayed their secret motives in entering the cell.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They went in, stayed a little while and hastened out to confirm the news to the crowd of other monks waiting outside.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Some of the latter shook their heads mournfully, but others did not even care to conceal the delight which gleamed unmistakably in their malignant eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And now no one reproached them for it, no one raised his voice in protest, which was strange, for the majority of the monks had been devoted to the dead elder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But it seemed as though God had in this case let the minority get the upper hand for a time.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Visitors from outside, particularly of the educated class, soon went into the cell, too, with the same spying intent.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Of the peasantry few went into the cell, though there were crowds of them at the gates of the hermitage.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: After three o’clock the rush of worldly visitors was greatly increased and this was no doubt owing to the shocking news.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: People were attracted who would not otherwise have come on that day and had not intended to come, and among them were some personages of high standing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But external decorum was still preserved and Father Païssy, with a stern face, continued firmly and distinctly reading aloud the Gospel, apparently not noticing what was taking place around him, though he had, in fact, observed something unusual long before.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But at last the murmurs, first subdued but gradually louder and more confident, reached even him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It shows God’s judgment is not as man’s,” Father Païssy heard suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The first to give utterance to this sentiment was a layman, an elderly official from the town, known to be a man of great piety.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But he only repeated aloud what the monks had long been whispering.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They had long before formulated this damning conclusion, and the worst of it was that a sort of triumphant satisfaction at that conclusion became more and more apparent every moment.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Soon they began to lay aside even external decorum and almost seemed to feel they had a sort of right to discard it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And for what reason can this have happened,” some of the monks said, at first with a show of regret; “he had a small frame and his flesh was dried up on his bones, what was there to decay?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It must be a sign from heaven,” others hastened to add, and their opinion was adopted at once without protest.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For it was pointed out, too, that if the decomposition had been natural, as in the case of every dead sinner, it would have been apparent later, after a lapse of at least twenty-four hours, but this premature corruption “was in excess of nature,” and so the finger of God was evident.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was meant for a sign.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This conclusion seemed irresistible.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Gentle Father Iosif, the librarian, a great favorite of the dead man’s, tried to reply to some of the evil speakers that “this is not held everywhere alike,” and that the incorruptibility of the bodies of the just was not a dogma of the Orthodox Church, but only an opinion, and that even in the most Orthodox regions, at Athos for instance, they were not greatly confounded by the smell of corruption, and there the chief sign of the glorification of the saved was not bodily incorruptibility, but the color of the bones when the bodies have lain many years in the earth and have decayed in it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And if the bones are yellow as wax, that is the great sign that the Lord has glorified the dead saint, if they are not yellow but black, it shows that God has not deemed him worthy of such glory—that is the belief in Athos, a great place, where the Orthodox doctrine has been preserved from of old, unbroken and in its greatest purity,” said Father Iosif in conclusion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the meek Father’s words had little effect and even provoked a mocking retort.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s all pedantry and innovation, no use listening to it,” the monks decided.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We stick to the old doctrine, there are all sorts of innovations nowadays, are we to follow them all?” added others.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We have had as many holy fathers as they had. There they are among the Turks, they have forgotten everything. Their doctrine has long been impure and they have no bells even,” the most sneering added.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Iosif walked away, grieving the more since he had put forward his own opinion with little confidence as though scarcely believing in it himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He foresaw with distress that something very unseemly was beginning and that there were positive signs of disobedience.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Little by little, all the sensible monks were reduced to silence like Father Iosif.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And so it came to pass that all who loved the elder and had accepted with devout obedience the institution of the eldership were all at once terribly cast down and glanced timidly in one another’s faces, when they met.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Those who were hostile to the institution of elders, as a novelty, held up their heads proudly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There was no smell of corruption from the late elder Varsonofy, but a sweet fragrance,” they recalled malignantly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But he gained that glory not because he was an elder, but because he was a holy man.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And this was followed by a shower of criticism and even blame of Father Zossima.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “His teaching was false; he taught that life is a great joy and not a vale of tears,” said some of the more unreasonable.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He followed the fashionable belief, he did not recognize material fire in hell,” others, still more unreasonable, added.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He was not strict in fasting, allowed himself sweet things, ate cherry jam with his tea, ladies used to send it to him. Is it for a monk of strict rule to drink tea?” could be heard among some of the envious.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He sat in pride,” the most malignant declared vindictively; “he considered himself a saint and he took it as his due when people knelt before him. “He abused the sacrament of confession,” the fiercest opponents of the institution of elders added in a malicious whisper.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And among these were some of the oldest monks, strictest in their devotion, genuine ascetics, who had kept silent during the life of the deceased elder, but now suddenly unsealed their lips.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And this was terrible, for their words had great influence on young monks who were not yet firm in their convictions.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The monk from Obdorsk heard all this attentively, heaving deep sighs and nodding his head.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, clearly Father Ferapont was right in his judgment yesterday,” and at that moment Father Ferapont himself made his appearance, as though on purpose to increase the confusion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I have mentioned already that he rarely left his wooden cell by the apiary.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was seldom even seen at church and they overlooked this neglect on the ground of his craziness, and did not keep him to the rules binding on all the rest.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But if the whole truth is to be told, they hardly had a choice about it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For it would have been discreditable to insist on burdening with the common regulations so great an ascetic, who prayed day and night (he even dropped asleep on his knees).

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If they had insisted, the monks would have said, “He is holier than all of us and he follows a rule harder than ours.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And if he does not go to church, it’s because he knows when he ought to; he has his own rule.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was to avoid the chance of these sinful murmurs that Father Ferapont was left in peace.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As every one was aware, Father Ferapont particularly disliked Father Zossima.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And now the news had reached him in his hut that “God’s judgment is not the same as man’s,” and that something had happened which was “in excess of nature.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It may well be supposed that among the first to run to him with the news was the monk from Obdorsk, who had visited him the evening before and left his cell terror-stricken.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I have mentioned above, that though Father Païssy, standing firm and immovable reading the Gospel over the coffin, could not hear nor see what was passing outside the cell, he gauged most of it correctly in his heart, for he knew the men surrounding him, well.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was not shaken by it, but awaited what would come next without fear, watching with penetration and insight for the outcome of the general excitement.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Suddenly an extraordinary uproar in the passage in open defiance of decorum burst on his ears.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The door was flung open and Father Ferapont appeared in the doorway.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Behind him there could be seen accompanying him a crowd of monks, together with many people from the town.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They did not, however, enter the cell, but stood at the bottom of the steps, waiting to see what Father Ferapont would say or do.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For they felt with a certain awe, in spite of their audacity, that he had not come for nothing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Standing in the doorway, Father Ferapont raised his arms, and under his right arm the keen inquisitive little eyes of the monk from Obdorsk peeped in.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He alone, in his intense curiosity, could not resist running up the steps after Father Ferapont.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The others, on the contrary, pressed farther back in sudden alarm when the door was noisily flung open.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Holding his hands aloft, Father Ferapont suddenly roared:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Casting out I cast out!” and, turning in all directions, he began at once making the sign of the cross at each of the four walls and four corners of the cell in succession.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All who accompanied Father Ferapont immediately understood his action.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For they knew he always did this wherever he went, and that he would not sit down or say a word, till he had driven out the evil spirits.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Satan, go hence! Satan, go hence!” he repeated at each sign of the cross.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Casting out I cast out,” he roared again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was wearing his coarse gown girt with a rope.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His bare chest, covered with gray hair, could be seen under his hempen shirt.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His feet were bare.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As soon as he began waving his arms, the cruel irons he wore under his gown could be heard clanking.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Païssy paused in his reading, stepped forward and stood before him waiting.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What have you come for, worthy Father? Why do you offend against good order? Why do you disturb the peace of the flock?” he said at last, looking sternly at him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What have I come for? You ask why? What is your faith?” shouted Father Ferapont crazily.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve come here to drive out your visitors, the unclean devils. I’ve come to see how many have gathered here while I have been away. I want to sweep them out with a birch broom.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You cast out the evil spirit, but perhaps you are serving him yourself,” Father Païssy went on fearlessly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And who can say of himself ‘I am holy’? Can you, Father?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I am unclean, not holy. I would not sit in an arm-chair and would not have them bow down to me as an idol,” thundered Father Ferapont.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nowadays folk destroy the true faith. The dead man, your saint,” he turned to the crowd, pointing with his finger to the coffin, “did not believe in devils. He gave medicine to keep off the devils. And so they have become as common as spiders in the corners. And now he has begun to stink himself. In that we see a great sign from God.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The incident he referred to was this.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: One of the monks was haunted in his dreams and, later on, in waking moments, by visions of evil spirits.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: When in the utmost terror he confided this to Father Zossima, the elder had advised continual prayer and rigid fasting.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But when that was of no use, he advised him, while persisting in prayer and fasting, to take a special medicine.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Many persons were shocked at the time and wagged their heads as they talked over it—and most of all Father Ferapont, to whom some of the censorious had hastened to report this “extraordinary” counsel on the part of the elder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Go away, Father!” said Father Païssy, in a commanding voice, “it’s not for man to judge but for God. Perhaps we see here a ‘sign’ which neither you, nor I, nor any one of us is able to comprehend. Go, Father, and do not trouble the flock!” he repeated impressively.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He did not keep the fasts according to the rule and therefore the sign has come. That is clear and it’s a sin to hide it,” the fanatic, carried away by a zeal that outstripped his reason, would not be quieted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He was seduced by sweetmeats, ladies brought them to him in their pockets, he sipped tea, he worshiped his belly, filling it with sweet things and his mind with haughty thoughts.... And for this he is put to shame....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You speak lightly, Father.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Païssy, too, raised his voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I admire your fasting and severities, but you speak lightly like some frivolous youth, fickle and childish.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Go away, Father, I command you!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Païssy thundered in conclusion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I will go,” said Ferapont, seeming somewhat taken aback, but still as bitter.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You learned men! You are so clever you look down upon my humbleness. I came hither with little learning and here I have forgotten what I did know, God Himself has preserved me in my weakness from your subtlety.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Païssy stood over him, waiting resolutely.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Ferapont paused and, suddenly leaning his cheek on his hand despondently, pronounced in a sing-song voice, looking at the coffin of the dead elder:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “To-morrow they will sing over him ‘Our Helper and Defender’—a splendid anthem—and over me when I die all they’ll sing will be ‘What earthly joy’—a little canticle,” he added with tearful regret.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are proud and puffed up, this is a vain place!” he shouted suddenly like a madman, and with a wave of his hand he turned quickly and quickly descended the steps.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The crowd awaiting him below wavered; some followed him at once and some lingered, for the cell was still open, and Father Païssy, following Father Ferapont on to the steps, stood watching him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the excited old fanatic was not completely silenced.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Walking twenty steps away, he suddenly turned towards the setting sun, raised both his arms and, as though some one had cut him down, fell to the ground with a loud scream.

text: A thick coil of her dark brown hair escaped from its lace covering and fell on her right shoulder, but she did not notice it and did not put it back till she had gazed at her visitors and recognized them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah, it’s you, Rakitin? You quite frightened me. Whom have you brought? Who is this with you? Good heavens, you have brought him!” she exclaimed, recognizing Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do send for candles!” said Rakitin, with the free-and-easy air of a most intimate friend, who is privileged to give orders in the house.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Candles ... of course, candles.... Fenya, fetch him a candle.... Well, you have chosen a moment to bring him!” she exclaimed again, nodding towards Alyosha, and turning to the looking-glass she began quickly fastening up her hair with both hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She seemed displeased.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Haven’t I managed to please you?” asked Rakitin, instantly almost offended.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You frightened me, Rakitin, that’s what it is. Grushenka turned with a smile to Alyosha. “Don’t be afraid of me, my dear Alyosha, you cannot think how glad I am to see you, my unexpected visitor. But you frightened me, Rakitin, I thought it was Mitya breaking in. You see, I deceived him just now, I made him promise to believe me and I told him a lie. I told him that I was going to spend the evening with my old man, Kuzma Kuzmitch, and should be there till late counting up his money. I always spend one whole evening a week with him making up his accounts. We lock ourselves in and he counts on the reckoning beads while I sit and put things down in the book. I am the only person he trusts. Mitya believes that I am there, but I came back and have been sitting locked in here, expecting some news. How was it Fenya let you in? Fenya, Fenya, run out to the gate, open it and look about whether the captain is to be seen! Perhaps he is hiding and spying, I am dreadfully frightened.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There’s no one there, Agrafena Alexandrovna, I’ve just looked out, I keep running to peep through the crack, I am in fear and trembling myself.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Are the shutters fastened, Fenya? And we must draw the curtains—that’s better! She drew the heavy curtains herself. “He’d rush in at once if he saw a light. I am afraid of your brother Mitya to-day, Alyosha.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka spoke aloud, and, though she was alarmed, she seemed very happy about something.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why are you so afraid of Mitya to-day?” inquired Rakitin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I should have thought you were not timid with him, you’d twist him round your little finger.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I tell you, I am expecting news, priceless news, so I don’t want Mitya at all. And he didn’t believe, I feel he didn’t, that I should stay at Kuzma Kuzmitch’s. He must be in his ambush now, behind Fyodor Pavlovitch’s, in the garden, watching for me. And if he’s there, he won’t come here, so much the better! But I really have been to Kuzma Kuzmitch’s, Mitya escorted me there. I told him I should stay there till midnight, and I asked him to be sure to come at midnight to fetch me home. He went away and I sat ten minutes with Kuzma Kuzmitch and came back here again. Ugh, I was afraid, I ran for fear of meeting him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And why are you so dressed up? What a curious cap you’ve got on!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How curious you are yourself, Rakitin! I tell you, I am expecting a message. If the message comes, I shall fly, I shall gallop away and you will see no more of me. That’s why I am dressed up, so as to be ready.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And where are you flying to?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “If you know too much, you’ll get old too soon.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Upon my word!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: You are highly delighted ...

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I’ve never seen you like this before.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: You are dressed up as if you were going to a ball.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Rakitin looked her up and down.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Much you know about balls.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And do you know much about them?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I have seen a ball. The year before last, Kuzma Kuzmitch’s son was married and I looked on from the gallery. Do you suppose I want to be talking to you, Rakitin, while a prince like this is standing here. Such a visitor! Alyosha, my dear boy, I gaze at you and can’t believe my eyes. Good heavens, can you have come here to see me! To tell you the truth, I never had a thought of seeing you and I didn’t think that you would ever come and see me. Though this is not the moment now, I am awfully glad to see you. Sit down on the sofa, here, that’s right, my bright young moon. I really can’t take it in even now.... Eh, Rakitin, if only you had brought him yesterday or the day before! But I am glad as it is! Perhaps it’s better he has come now, at such a moment, and not the day before yesterday.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She gayly sat down beside Alyosha on the sofa, looking at him with positive delight.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And she really was glad, she was not lying when she said so.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Her eyes glowed, her lips laughed, but it was a good-hearted merry laugh.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha had not expected to see such a kind expression in her face....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had hardly met her till the day before, he had formed an alarming idea of her, and had been horribly distressed the day before by the spiteful and treacherous trick she had played on Katerina Ivanovna.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was greatly surprised to find her now altogether different from what he had expected.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And, crushed as he was by his own sorrow, his eyes involuntarily rested on her with attention.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Her whole manner seemed changed for the better since yesterday, there was scarcely any trace of that mawkish sweetness in her speech, of that voluptuous softness in her movements.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Everything was simple and good-natured, her gestures were rapid, direct, confiding, but she was greatly excited.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Dear me, how everything comes together to-day!” she chattered on again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And why I am so glad to see you, Alyosha, I couldn’t say myself! If you ask me, I couldn’t tell you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Come, don’t you know why you’re glad?” said Rakitin, grinning.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You used to be always pestering me to bring him, you’d some object, I suppose.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I had a different object once, but now that’s over, this is not the moment. I say, I want you to have something nice. I am so good-natured now. You sit down, too, Rakitin; why are you standing? You’ve sat down already? There’s no fear of Rakitin’s forgetting to look after himself. Look, Alyosha, he’s sitting there opposite us, so offended that I didn’t ask him to sit down before you. Ugh, Rakitin is such a one to take offense!” laughed Grushenka.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t be angry, Rakitin, I’m kind to-day.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why are you so depressed, Alyosha?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Are you afraid of me?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She peeped into his eyes with merry mockery.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’s sad. The promotion has not been given,” boomed Rakitin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What promotion?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “His elder stinks.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What? You are talking some nonsense, you want to say something nasty. Be quiet, you stupid! Let me sit on your knee, Alyosha, like this. She suddenly skipped forward and jumped, laughing, on his knee, like a nestling kitten, with her right arm about his neck. “I’ll cheer you up, my pious boy. Yes, really, will you let me sit on your knee? You won’t be angry? If you tell me, I’ll get off?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha did not speak.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He sat afraid to move, he heard her words, “If you tell me, I’ll get off,” but he did not answer.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But there was nothing in his heart such as Rakitin, for instance, watching him malignantly from his corner, might have expected or fancied.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The great grief in his heart swallowed up every sensation that might have been aroused, and, if only he could have thought clearly at that moment, he would have realized that he had now the strongest armor to protect him from every lust and temptation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yet in spite of the vague irresponsiveness of his spiritual condition and the sorrow that overwhelmed him, he could not help wondering at a new and strange sensation in his heart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This woman, this “dreadful” woman, had no terror for him now, none of that terror that had stirred in his soul at any passing thought of woman.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: On the contrary, this woman, dreaded above all women, sitting now on his knee, holding him in her arms, aroused in him now a quite different, unexpected, peculiar feeling, a feeling of the intensest and purest interest without a trace of fear, of his former terror.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That was what instinctively surprised him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’ve talked nonsense enough,” cried Rakitin, “you’d much better give us some champagne. You owe it me, you know you do!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, I really do. Do you know, Alyosha, I promised him champagne on the top of everything, if he’d bring you? I’ll have some too! Fenya, Fenya, bring us the bottle Mitya left! Look sharp! Though I am so stingy, I’ll stand a bottle, not for you, Rakitin, you’re a toadstool, but he is a falcon! And though my heart is full of something very different, so be it, I’ll drink with you. I long for some dissipation.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But what is the matter with you?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And what is this message, may I ask, or is it a secret?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Rakitin put in inquisitively, doing his best to pretend not to notice the snubs that were being continually aimed at him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ech, it’s not a secret, and you know it, too,” Grushenka said, in a voice suddenly anxious, turning her head towards Rakitin, and drawing a little away from Alyosha, though she still sat on his knee with her arm round his neck.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “My officer is coming, Rakitin, my officer is coming.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I heard he was coming, but is he so near?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He is at Mokroe now; he’ll send a messenger from there, so he wrote; I got a letter from him to-day. I am expecting the messenger every minute.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You don’t say so! Why at Mokroe?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s a long story, I’ve told you enough.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mitya’ll be up to something now—I say! Does he know or doesn’t he?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He know! Of course he doesn’t. If he knew, there would be murder. But I am not afraid of that now, I am not afraid of his knife. Be quiet, Rakitin, don’t remind me of Dmitri Fyodorovitch, he has bruised my heart. And I don’t want to think of that at this moment. I can think of Alyosha here, I can look at Alyosha ... smile at me, dear, cheer up, smile at my foolishness, at my pleasure.... Ah, he’s smiling, he’s smiling! How kindly he looks at me! And you know, Alyosha, I’ve been thinking all this time you were angry with me, because of the day before yesterday, because of that young lady. I was a cur, that’s the truth.... But it’s a good thing it happened so. It was a horrid thing, but a good thing too. Grushenka smiled dreamily and a little cruel line showed in her smile. “Mitya told me that she screamed out that I ‘ought to be flogged. I did insult her dreadfully. She sent for me, she wanted to make a conquest of me, to win me over with her chocolate.... No, it’s a good thing it did end like that. She smiled again. “But I am still afraid of your being angry.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, that’s really true,” Rakitin put in suddenly with genuine surprise.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alyosha, she is really afraid of a chicken like you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He is a chicken to you, Rakitin ... because you’ve no conscience, that’s what it is! You see, I love him with all my soul, that’s how it is! Alyosha, do you believe I love you with all my soul?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah, you shameless woman! She is making you a declaration, Alexey!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, what of it, I love him!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And what about your officer? And the priceless message from Mokroe?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That is quite different.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s a woman’s way of looking at it!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t you make me angry, Rakitin. Grushenka caught him up hotly. “This is quite different. I love Alyosha in a different way. It’s true, Alyosha, I had sly designs on you before. For I am a horrid, violent creature. But at other times I’ve looked upon you, Alyosha, as my conscience. I’ve kept thinking ‘how any one like that must despise a nasty thing like me. I thought that the day before yesterday, as I ran home from the young lady’s. I have thought of you a long time in that way, Alyosha, and Mitya knows, I’ve talked to him about it. Mitya understands. Would you believe it, I sometimes look at you and feel ashamed, utterly ashamed of myself.... And how, and since when, I began to think about you like that, I can’t say, I don’t remember....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Fenya came in and put a tray with an uncorked bottle and three glasses of champagne on the table.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Here’s the champagne!” cried Rakitin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’re excited, Agrafena Alexandrovna, and not yourself. When you’ve had a glass of champagne, you’ll be ready to dance. Eh, they can’t even do that properly,” he added, looking at the bottle.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The old woman’s poured it out in the kitchen and the bottle’s been brought in warm and without a cork. Well, let me have some, anyway.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He went up to the table, took a glass, emptied it at one gulp and poured himself out another.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “One doesn’t often stumble upon champagne,” he said, licking his lips.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Now, Alyosha, take a glass, show what you can do! What shall we drink to? The gates of paradise? Take a glass, Grushenka, you drink to the gates of paradise, too.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What gates of paradise?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She took a glass, Alyosha took his, tasted it and put it back.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, I’d better not,” he smiled gently.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And you bragged!” cried Rakitin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, if so, I won’t either,” chimed in Grushenka, “I really don’t want any. You can drink the whole bottle alone, Rakitin. If Alyosha has some, I will.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What touching sentimentality!” said Rakitin tauntingly; “and she’s sitting on his knee, too! He’s got something to grieve over, but what’s the matter with you? He is rebelling against his God and ready to eat sausage....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How so?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “His elder died to-day, Father Zossima, the saint.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So Father Zossima is dead,” cried Grushenka.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Good God, I did not know!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She crossed herself devoutly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Goodness, what have I been doing, sitting on his knee like this at such a moment!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She started up as though in dismay, instantly slipped off his knee and sat down on the sofa.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha bent a long wondering look upon her and a light seemed to dawn in his face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Rakitin,” he said suddenly, in a firm and loud voice; “don’t taunt me with having rebelled against God. I don’t want to feel angry with you, so you must be kinder, too, I’ve lost a treasure such as you have never had, and you cannot judge me now. You had much better look at her—do you see how she has pity on me? I came here to find a wicked soul—I felt drawn to evil because I was base and evil myself, and I’ve found a true sister, I have found a treasure—a loving heart. She had pity on me just now.... Agrafena Alexandrovna, I am speaking of you. You’ve raised my soul from the depths.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha’s lips were quivering and he caught his breath.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “She has saved you, it seems,” laughed Rakitin spitefully.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And she meant to get you in her clutches, do you realize that?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Stay, Rakitin. Grushenka jumped up. “Hush, both of you. Now I’ll tell you all about it. Hush, Alyosha, your words make me ashamed, for I am bad and not good—that’s what I am. And you hush, Rakitin, because you are telling lies. I had the low idea of trying to get him in my clutches, but now you are lying, now it’s all different. And don’t let me hear anything more from you, Rakitin.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All this Grushenka said with extreme emotion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “They are both crazy,” said Rakitin, looking at them with amazement.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I feel as though I were in a madhouse. They’re both getting so feeble they’ll begin crying in a minute.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I shall begin to cry, I shall,” repeated Grushenka.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He called me his sister and I shall never forget that. Only let me tell you, Rakitin, though I am bad, I did give away an onion.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “An onion? Hang it all, you really are crazy.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Rakitin wondered at their enthusiasm.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was aggrieved and annoyed, though he might have reflected that each of them was just passing through a spiritual crisis such as does not come often in a lifetime.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But though Rakitin was very sensitive about everything that concerned himself, he was very obtuse as regards the feelings and sensations of others—partly from his youth and inexperience, partly from his intense egoism.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You see, Alyosha,” Grushenka turned to him with a nervous laugh.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I was boasting when I told Rakitin I had given away an onion, but it’s not to boast I tell you about it. It’s only a story, but it’s a nice story. I used to hear it when I was a child from Matryona, my cook, who is still with me. It’s like this. Once upon a time there was a peasant woman and a very wicked woman she was. And she died and did not leave a single good deed behind. The devils caught her and plunged her into the lake of fire. So her guardian angel stood and wondered what good deed of hers he could remember to tell to God; ‘She once pulled up an onion in her garden,’ said he, ‘and gave it to a beggar woman. And God answered: ‘You take that onion then, hold it out to her in the lake, and let her take hold and be pulled out. And if you can pull her out of the lake, let her come to Paradise, but if the onion breaks, then the woman must stay where she is. The angel ran to the woman and held out the onion to her. ‘Come,’ said he, ‘catch hold and I’ll pull you out. And he began cautiously pulling her out. He had just pulled her right out, when the other sinners in the lake, seeing how she was being drawn out, began catching hold of her so as to be pulled out with her. But she was a very wicked woman and she began kicking them. ‘I’m to be pulled out, not you. It’s my onion, not yours. As soon as she said that, the onion broke. And the woman fell into the lake and she is burning there to this day. So the angel wept and went away. So that’s the story, Alyosha; I know it by heart, for I am that wicked woman myself. I boasted to Rakitin that I had given away an onion, but to you I’ll say: ‘I’ve done nothing but give away one onion all my life, that’s the only good deed I’ve done. So don’t praise me, Alyosha, don’t think me good, I am bad, I am a wicked woman and you make me ashamed if you praise me. Eh, I must confess everything. Listen, Alyosha. I was so anxious to get hold of you that I promised Rakitin twenty-five roubles if he would bring you to me. Stay, Rakitin, wait!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She went with rapid steps to the table, opened a drawer, pulled out a purse and took from it a twenty-five rouble note.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What nonsense! What nonsense!” cried Rakitin, disconcerted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Take it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Rakitin, I owe it you, there’s no fear of your refusing it, you asked for it yourself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And she threw the note to him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Likely I should refuse it,” boomed Rakitin, obviously abashed, but carrying off his confusion with a swagger.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That will come in very handy; fools are made for wise men’s profit.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And now hold your tongue, Rakitin, what I am going to say now is not for your ears. Sit down in that corner and keep quiet. You don’t like us, so hold your tongue.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What should I like you for?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Rakitin snarled, not concealing his ill-humor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He put the twenty-five rouble note in his pocket and he felt ashamed at Alyosha’s seeing it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had reckoned on receiving his payment later, without Alyosha’s knowing of it, and now, feeling ashamed, he lost his temper.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Till that moment he had thought it discreet not to contradict Grushenka too flatly in spite of her snubbing, since he had something to get out of her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But now he, too, was angry:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “One loves people for some reason, but what have either of you done for me?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You should love people without a reason, as Alyosha does.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How does he love you? How has he shown it, that you make such a fuss about it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka was standing in the middle of the room; she spoke with heat and there were hysterical notes in her voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Hush, Rakitin, you know nothing about us! And don’t dare to speak to me like that again. How dare you be so familiar! Sit in that corner and be quiet, as though you were my footman! And now, Alyosha, I’ll tell you the whole truth, that you may see what a wretch I am! I am not talking to Rakitin, but to you. I wanted to ruin you, Alyosha, that’s the holy truth; I quite meant to. I wanted to so much, that I bribed Rakitin to bring you. And why did I want to do such a thing? You knew nothing about it, Alyosha, you turned away from me; if you passed me, you dropped your eyes. And I’ve looked at you a hundred times before to-day; I began asking every one about you. Your face haunted my heart. ‘He despises me,’ I thought; ‘he won’t even look at me. And I felt it so much at last that I wondered at myself for being so frightened of a boy. I’ll get him in my clutches and laugh at him. I was full of spite and anger. Would you believe it, nobody here dares talk or think of coming to Agrafena Alexandrovna with any evil purpose. Old Kuzma is the only man I have anything to do with here; I was bound and sold to him; Satan brought us together, but there has been no one else. But looking at you, I thought, I’ll get him in my clutches and laugh at him. You see what a spiteful cur I am, and you called me your sister! And now that man who wronged me has come; I sit here waiting for a message from him. And do you know what that man has been to me? Five years ago, when Kuzma brought me here, I used to shut myself up, that no one might have sight or sound of me. I was a silly slip of a girl; I used to sit here sobbing; I used to lie awake all night, thinking: ‘Where is he now, the man who wronged me? He is laughing at me with another woman, most likely. If only I could see him, if I could meet him again, I’d pay him out, I’d pay him out! At night I used to lie sobbing into my pillow in the dark, and I used to brood over it; I used to tear my heart on purpose and gloat over my anger. ‘I’ll pay him out, I’ll pay him out! That’s what I used to cry out in the dark. And when I suddenly thought that I should really do nothing to him, and that he was laughing at me then, or perhaps had utterly forgotten me, I would fling myself on the floor, melt into helpless tears, and lie there shaking till dawn. In the morning I would get up more spiteful than a dog, ready to tear the whole world to pieces. And then what do you think? I began saving money, I became hard-hearted, grew stout—grew wiser, would you say? No, no one in the whole world sees it, no one knows it, but when night comes on, I sometimes lie as I did five years ago, when I was a silly girl, clenching my teeth and crying all night, thinking, ‘I’ll pay him out, I’ll pay him out! Do you hear? Well then, now you understand me. A month ago a letter came to me—he was coming, he was a widower, he wanted to see me. It took my breath away; then I suddenly thought: ‘If he comes and whistles to call me, I shall creep back to him like a beaten dog. I couldn’t believe myself. Am I so abject? Shall I run to him or not? And I’ve been in such a rage with myself all this month that I am worse than I was five years ago. Do you see now, Alyosha, what a violent, vindictive creature I am? I have shown you the whole truth! I played with Mitya to keep me from running to that other. Hush, Rakitin, it’s not for you to judge me, I am not speaking to you. Before you came in, I was lying here waiting, brooding, deciding my whole future life, and you can never know what was in my heart. Yes, Alyosha, tell your young lady not to be angry with me for what happened the day before yesterday.... Nobody in the whole world knows what I am going through now, and no one ever can know.... For perhaps I shall take a knife with me to-day, I can’t make up my mind ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And at this “tragic” phrase Grushenka broke down, hid her face in her hands, flung herself on the sofa pillows, and sobbed like a little child.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha got up and went to Rakitin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Misha,” he said, “don’t be angry. She wounded you, but don’t be angry. You heard what she said just now? You mustn’t ask too much of human endurance, one must be merciful.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha said this at the instinctive prompting of his heart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He felt obliged to speak and he turned to Rakitin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If Rakitin had not been there, he would have spoken to the air.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Rakitin looked at him ironically and Alyosha stopped short.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You were so primed up with your elder’s teaching last night that now you have to let it off on me, Alexey, man of God!” said Rakitin, with a smile of hatred.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t laugh, Rakitin, don’t smile, don’t talk of the dead—he was better than any one in the world!” cried Alyosha, with tears in his voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I didn’t speak to you as a judge but as the lowest of the judged. What am I beside her? I came here seeking my ruin, and said to myself, ‘What does it matter?’ in my cowardliness, but she, after five years in torment, as soon as any one says a word from the heart to her—it makes her forget everything, forgive everything, in her tears! The man who has wronged her has come back, he sends for her and she forgives him everything, and hastens joyfully to meet him and she won’t take a knife with her. She won’t! No, I am not like that. I don’t know whether you are, Misha, but I am not like that. It’s a lesson to me.... She is more loving than we.... Have you heard her speak before of what she has just told us? No, you haven’t; if you had, you’d have understood her long ago ... and the person insulted the day before yesterday must forgive her, too! She will, when she knows ... and she shall know.... This soul is not yet at peace with itself, one must be tender with it ... there may be a treasure in that soul....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha stopped, because he caught his breath.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In spite of his ill-humor Rakitin looked at him with astonishment.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had never expected such a tirade from the gentle Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “She’s found some one to plead her cause! Why, are you in love with her? Agrafena Alexandrovna, our monk’s really in love with you, you’ve made a conquest!” he cried, with a coarse laugh.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka lifted her head from the pillow and looked at Alyosha with a tender smile shining on her tear-stained face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Let him alone, Alyosha, my cherub; you see what he is, he is not a person for you to speak to. Mihail Osipovitch,” she turned to Rakitin, “I meant to beg your pardon for being rude to you, but now I don’t want to. Alyosha, come to me, sit down here. She beckoned to him with a happy smile. “That’s right, sit here. Tell me,” she shook him by the hand and peeped into his face, smiling, “tell me, do I love that man or not? the man who wronged me, do I love him or not? Before you came, I lay here in the dark, asking my heart whether I loved him. Decide for me, Alyosha, the time has come, it shall be as you say. Am I to forgive him or not?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But you have forgiven him already,” said Alyosha, smiling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, I really have forgiven him,” Grushenka murmured thoughtfully.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What an abject heart!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: To my abject heart!

text: She snatched up a glass from the table, emptied it at a gulp, lifted it in the air and flung it on the floor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The glass broke with a crash.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A little cruel line came into her smile.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Perhaps I haven’t forgiven him, though,” she said, with a sort of menace in her voice, and she dropped her eyes to the ground as though she were talking to herself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Perhaps my heart is only getting ready to forgive. I shall struggle with my heart. You see, Alyosha, I’ve grown to love my tears in these five years.... Perhaps I only love my resentment, not him ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, I shouldn’t care to be in his shoes,” hissed Rakitin.

text: “Well, you won’t be, Rakitin, you’ll never be in his shoes. You shall black my shoes, Rakitin, that’s the place you are fit for. You’ll never get a woman like me ... and he won’t either, perhaps ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Won’t he? Then why are you dressed up like that?” said Rakitin, with a venomous sneer.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t taunt me with dressing up, Rakitin, you don’t know all that is in my heart! If I choose to tear off my finery, I’ll tear it off at once, this minute,” she cried in a resonant voice.

text: “You don’t know what that finery is for, Rakitin! Perhaps I shall see him and say: ‘Have you ever seen me look like this before? He left me a thin, consumptive cry-baby of seventeen. That may be what the finery is for, Rakitin. Grushenka finished with a malicious laugh. “I’m violent and resentful, Alyosha, I’ll tear off my finery, I’ll destroy my beauty, I’ll scorch my face, slash it with a knife, and turn beggar. If I choose, I won’t go anywhere now to see any one. If I choose, I’ll send Kuzma back all he has ever given me, to-morrow, and all his money and I’ll go out charing for the rest of my life. You think I wouldn’t do it, Rakitin, that I would not dare to do it? I would, I would, I could do it directly, only don’t exasperate me ... and I’ll send him about his business, I’ll snap my fingers in his face, he shall never see me again!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She uttered the last words in an hysterical scream, but broke down again, hid her face in her hands, buried it in the pillow and shook with sobs.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Rakitin got up.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s time we were off,” he said, “it’s late, we shall be shut out of the monastery.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka leapt up from her place.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Surely you don’t want to go, Alyosha!” she cried, in mournful surprise.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What are you doing to me? You’ve stirred up my feeling, tortured me, and now you’ll leave me to face this night alone!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He can hardly spend the night with you! Though if he wants to, let him! I’ll go alone,” Rakitin scoffed jeeringly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Hush, evil tongue! Grushenka cried angrily at him; “you never said such words to me as he has come to say.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What has he said to you so special?” asked Rakitin irritably.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I can’t say, I don’t know. I don’t know what he said to me, it went straight to my heart; he has wrung my heart.... He is the first, the only one who has pitied me, that’s what it is. Why did you not come before, you angel? She fell on her knees before him as though in a sudden frenzy. “I’ve been waiting all my life for some one like you, I knew that some one like you would come and forgive me. I believed that, nasty as I am, some one would really love me, not only with a shameful love!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What have I done to you?” answered Alyosha, bending over her with a tender smile, and gently taking her by the hands; “I only gave you an onion, nothing but a tiny little onion, that was all!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was moved to tears himself as he said it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At that moment there was a sudden noise in the passage, some one came into the hall.

text: Grushenka jumped up, seeming greatly alarmed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Fenya ran noisily into the room, crying out:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mistress, mistress darling, a messenger has galloped up,” she cried, breathless and joyful.

text: “A carriage from Mokroe for you, Timofey the driver, with three horses, they are just putting in fresh horses.... A letter, here’s the letter, mistress.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A letter was in her hand and she waved it in the air all the while she talked.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka snatched the letter from her and carried it to the candle.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was only a note, a few lines.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She read it in one instant.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He has sent for me,” she cried, her face white and distorted, with a wan smile; “he whistles! Crawl back, little dog!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But only for one instant she stood as though hesitating; suddenly the blood rushed to her head and sent a glow to her cheeks.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I will go,” she cried; “five years of my life! Good-by! Good-by, Alyosha, my fate is sealed. Go, go, leave me all of you, don’t let me see you again! Grushenka is flying to a new life.... Don’t you remember evil against me either, Rakitin. I may be going to my death! Ugh! I feel as though I were drunk!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She suddenly left them and ran into her bedroom.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, she has no thoughts for us now!” grumbled Rakitin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Let’s go, or we may hear that feminine shriek again. I am sick of all these tears and cries.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha mechanically let himself be led out.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In the yard stood a covered cart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Horses were being taken out of the shafts, men were running to and fro with a lantern.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Three fresh horses were being led in at the open gate.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But when Alyosha and Rakitin reached the bottom of the steps, Grushenka’s bedroom window was suddenly opened and she called in a ringing voice after Alyosha:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alyosha, give my greetings to your brother Mitya and tell him not to remember evil against me, though I have brought him misery. And tell him, too, in my words: ‘Grushenka has fallen to a scoundrel, and not to you, noble heart. And add, too, that Grushenka loved him only one hour, only one short hour she loved him—so let him remember that hour all his life—say, ‘Grushenka tells you to!’”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She ended in a voice full of sobs.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The window was shut with a slam.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “H’m, h’m!” growled Rakitin, laughing, “she murders your brother Mitya and then tells him to remember it all his life! What ferocity!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha made no reply, he seemed not to have heard.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He walked fast beside Rakitin as though in a terrible hurry.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was lost in thought and moved mechanically.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Rakitin felt a sudden twinge as though he had been touched on an open wound.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had expected something quite different by bringing Grushenka and Alyosha together.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Something very different from what he had hoped for had happened.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He is a Pole, that officer of hers,” he began again, restraining himself; “and indeed he is not an officer at all now. He served in the customs in Siberia, somewhere on the Chinese frontier, some puny little beggar of a Pole, I expect. Lost his job, they say. He’s heard now that Grushenka’s saved a little money, so he’s turned up again—that’s the explanation of the mystery.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Again Alyosha seemed not to hear.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Rakitin could not control himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, so you’ve saved the sinner?” he laughed spitefully.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Have you turned the Magdalene into the true path? Driven out the seven devils, eh? So you see the miracles you were looking out for just now have come to pass!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Hush, Rakitin,” Alyosha answered with an aching heart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So you despise me now for those twenty-five roubles? I’ve sold my friend, you think. But you are not Christ, you know, and I am not Judas.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, Rakitin, I assure you I’d forgotten about it,” cried Alyosha, “you remind me of it yourself....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But this was the last straw for Rakitin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Damnation take you all and each of you!” he cried suddenly, “why the devil did I take you up? I don’t want to know you from this time forward. Go alone, there’s your road!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And he turned abruptly into another street, leaving Alyosha alone in the dark.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha came out of the town and walked across the fields to the monastery.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was very late, according to the monastery ideas, when Alyosha returned to the hermitage; the door-keeper let him in by a special entrance.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It had struck nine o’clock—the hour of rest and repose after a day of such agitation for all.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha timidly opened the door and went into the elder’s cell where his coffin was now standing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was no one in the cell but Father Païssy, reading the Gospel in solitude over the coffin, and the young novice Porfiry, who, exhausted by the previous night’s conversation and the disturbing incidents of the day, was sleeping the deep sound sleep of youth on the floor of the other room.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though Father Païssy heard Alyosha come in, he did not even look in his direction.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha turned to the right from the door to the corner, fell on his knees and began to pray.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His soul was overflowing but with mingled feelings; no single sensation stood out distinctly; on the contrary, one drove out another in a slow, continual rotation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But there was a sweetness in his heart and, strange to say, Alyosha was not surprised at it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Again he saw that coffin before him, the hidden dead figure so precious to him, but the weeping and poignant grief of the morning was no longer aching in his soul.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As soon as he came in, he fell down before the coffin as before a holy shrine, but joy, joy was glowing in his mind and in his heart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The one window of the cell was open, the air was fresh and cool.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So the smell must have become stronger, if they opened the window,” thought Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But even this thought of the smell of corruption, which had seemed to him so awful and humiliating a few hours before, no longer made him feel miserable or indignant.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He began quietly praying, but he soon felt that he was praying almost mechanically.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Fragments of thought floated through his soul, flashed like stars and went out again at once, to be succeeded by others.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But yet there was reigning in his soul a sense of the wholeness of things—something steadfast and comforting—and he was aware of it himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Sometimes he began praying ardently, he longed to pour out his thankfulness and love....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But when he had begun to pray, he passed suddenly to something else, and sank into thought, forgetting both the prayer and what had interrupted it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He began listening to what Father Païssy was reading, but worn out with exhaustion he gradually began to doze.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee;” read Father Païssy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And the mother of Jesus was there; And both Jesus was called, and his disciples, to the marriage.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Marriage? What’s that?... A marriage!” floated whirling through Alyosha’s mind.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There is happiness for her, too.... She has gone to the feast.... No, she has not taken the knife.... That was only a tragic phrase.... Well ... tragic phrases should be forgiven, they must be. Tragic phrases comfort the heart.... Without them, sorrow would be too heavy for men to bear. Rakitin has gone off to the back alley. As long as Rakitin broods over his wrongs, he will always go off to the back alley.... But the high road ... The road is wide and straight and bright as crystal, and the sun is at the end of it.... Ah!... What’s being read?”...

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And when they wanted wine, the mother of Jesus saith unto him, They have no wine” ...

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha heard.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah, yes, I was missing that, and I didn’t want to miss it, I love that passage: it’s Cana of Galilee, the first miracle.... Ah, that miracle! Ah, that sweet miracle! It was not men’s grief, but their joy Christ visited, He worked His first miracle to help men’s gladness.... ‘He who loves men loves their gladness, too’ ... He was always repeating that, it was one of his leading ideas.... ‘There’s no living without joy,’ Mitya says.... Yes, Mitya.... ‘Everything that is true and good is always full of forgiveness,’ he used to say that, too” ...

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what has it to do with thee or me?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mine hour is not yet come.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it” ...

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do it.... Gladness, the gladness of some poor, very poor, people.... Of course they were poor, since they hadn’t wine enough even at a wedding.... The historians write that, in those days, the people living about the Lake of Gennesaret were the poorest that can possibly be imagined ... and another great heart, that other great being, His Mother, knew that He had come not only to make His great terrible sacrifice. She knew that His heart was open even to the simple, artless merrymaking of some obscure and unlearned people, who had warmly bidden Him to their poor wedding. ‘Mine hour is not yet come,’ He said, with a soft smile (He must have smiled gently to her). And, indeed, was it to make wine abundant at poor weddings He had come down to earth? And yet He went and did as she asked Him.... Ah, he is reading again”....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water.

text: And they filled them up to the brim.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And he saith unto them, Draw out now and bear unto the governor of the feast.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But what’s this, what’s this? Why is the room growing wider?... Ah, yes ... It’s the marriage, the wedding ... yes, of course.
