Who is getting up there from the great table? What!... He here, too? But he’s in the coffin ... but he’s here, too. He has stood up, he sees me, he is coming here.... God!”...

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yes, he came up to him, to him, he, the little, thin old man, with tiny wrinkles on his face, joyful and laughing softly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was no coffin now, and he was in the same dress as he had worn yesterday sitting with them, when the visitors had gathered about him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His face was uncovered, his eyes were shining.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: How was this, then?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He, too, had been called to the feast.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He, too, at the marriage of Cana in Galilee....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, my dear, I am called, too, called and bidden,” he heard a soft voice saying over him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why have you hidden yourself here, out of sight? You come and join us too.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was his voice, the voice of Father Zossima.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And it must be he, since he called him!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The elder raised Alyosha by the hand and he rose from his knees.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We are rejoicing,” the little, thin old man went on.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We are drinking the new wine, the wine of new, great gladness; do you see how many guests? Here are the bride and bridegroom, here is the wise governor of the feast, he is tasting the new wine. Why do you wonder at me? I gave an onion to a beggar, so I, too, am here. And many here have given only an onion each—only one little onion.... What are all our deeds? And you, my gentle one, you, my kind boy, you too have known how to give a famished woman an onion to-day. Begin your work, dear one, begin it, gentle one!... Do you see our Sun, do you see Him?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I am afraid ... I dare not look,” whispered Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do not fear Him. He is terrible in His greatness, awful in His sublimity, but infinitely merciful. He has made Himself like unto us from love and rejoices with us. He is changing the water into wine that the gladness of the guests may not be cut short. He is expecting new guests, He is calling new ones unceasingly for ever and ever.... There they are bringing new wine. Do you see they are bringing the vessels....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Something glowed in Alyosha’s heart, something filled it till it ached, tears of rapture rose from his soul....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He stretched out his hands, uttered a cry and waked up.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Again the coffin, the open window, and the soft, solemn, distinct reading of the Gospel.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Alyosha did not listen to the reading.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was strange, he had fallen asleep on his knees, but now he was on his feet, and suddenly, as though thrown forward, with three firm rapid steps he went right up to the coffin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His shoulder brushed against Father Païssy without his noticing it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Païssy raised his eyes for an instant from his book, but looked away again at once, seeing that something strange was happening to the boy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha gazed for half a minute at the coffin, at the covered, motionless dead man that lay in the coffin, with the ikon on his breast and the peaked cap with the octangular cross, on his head.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had only just been hearing his voice, and that voice was still ringing in his ears.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was listening, still expecting other words, but suddenly he turned sharply and went out of the cell.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He did not stop on the steps either, but went quickly down; his soul, overflowing with rapture, yearned for freedom, space, openness.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The vault of heaven, full of soft, shining stars, stretched vast and fathomless above him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The Milky Way ran in two pale streams from the zenith to the horizon.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The fresh, motionless, still night enfolded the earth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The white towers and golden domes of the cathedral gleamed out against the sapphire sky.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The gorgeous autumn flowers, in the beds round the house, were slumbering till morning.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The silence of earth seemed to melt into the silence of the heavens.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The mystery of earth was one with the mystery of the stars....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha stood, gazed, and suddenly threw himself down on the earth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He did not know why he embraced it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He could not have told why he longed so irresistibly to kiss it, to kiss it all.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But he kissed it weeping, sobbing and watering it with his tears, and vowed passionately to love it, to love it for ever and ever.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Water the earth with the tears of your joy and love those tears,” echoed in his soul.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What was he weeping over?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh! in his rapture he was weeping even over those stars, which were shining to him from the abyss of space, and “he was not ashamed of that ecstasy. There seemed to be threads from all those innumerable worlds of God, linking his soul to them, and it was trembling all over “in contact with other worlds. He longed to forgive every one and for everything, and to beg forgiveness. Oh, not for himself, but for all men, for all and for everything. “And others are praying for me too,” echoed again in his soul.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But with every instant he felt clearly and, as it were, tangibly, that something firm and unshakable as that vault of heaven had entered into his soul.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was as though some idea had seized the sovereignty of his mind—and it was for all his life and for ever and ever.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had fallen on the earth a weak boy, but he rose up a resolute champion, and he knew and felt it suddenly at the very moment of his ecstasy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And never, never, all his life long, could Alyosha forget that minute.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Some one visited my soul in that hour,” he used to say afterwards, with implicit faith in his words.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Within three days he left the monastery in accordance with the words of his elder, who had bidden him “sojourn in the world.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Dmitri, to whom Grushenka, flying away to a new life, had left her last greetings, bidding him remember the hour of her love for ever, knew nothing of what had happened to her, and was at that moment in a condition of feverish agitation and activity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For the last two days he had been in such an inconceivable state of mind that he might easily have fallen ill with brain fever, as he said himself afterwards.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha had not been able to find him the morning before, and Ivan had not succeeded in meeting him at the tavern on the same day.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The people at his lodgings, by his orders, concealed his movements.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had spent those two days literally rushing in all directions, “struggling with his destiny and trying to save himself,” as he expressed it himself afterwards, and for some hours he even made a dash out of the town on urgent business, terrible as it was to him to lose sight of Grushenka for a moment.

text: He pulled the bundle of notes out of his pocket again, picked out three hundred roubles, threw them on the counter, and ran hurriedly out of the shop.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Every one followed him out, bowing and wishing him good luck.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Andrey, coughing from the brandy he had just swallowed, jumped up on the box.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Mitya was only just taking his seat when suddenly to his surprise he saw Fenya before him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She ran up panting, clasped her hands before him with a cry, and plumped down at his feet.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Dmitri Fyodorovitch, dear good Dmitri Fyodorovitch, don’t harm my mistress. And it was I told you all about it.... And don’t murder him, he came first, he’s hers! He’ll marry Agrafena Alexandrovna now. That’s why he’s come back from Siberia. Dmitri Fyodorovitch, dear, don’t take a fellow creature’s life!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Tut—tut—tut! That’s it, is it? So you’re off there to make trouble!” muttered Pyotr Ilyitch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Now, it’s all clear, as clear as daylight. Dmitri Fyodorovitch, give me your pistols at once if you mean to behave like a man,” he shouted aloud to Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do you hear, Dmitri?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The pistols? Wait a bit, brother, I’ll throw them into the pool on the road,” answered Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Fenya, get up, don’t kneel to me. Mitya won’t hurt any one, the silly fool won’t hurt any one again. But I say, Fenya,” he shouted, after having taken his seat.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I hurt you just now, so forgive me and have pity on me, forgive a scoundrel.... But it doesn’t matter if you don’t. It’s all the same now. Now then, Andrey, look alive, fly along full speed!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Andrey whipped up the horses, and the bells began ringing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Good-by, Pyotr Ilyitch! My last tear is for you!...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’s not drunk, but he keeps babbling like a lunatic,” Pyotr Ilyitch thought as he watched him go.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had half a mind to stay and see the cart packed with the remaining wines and provisions, knowing that they would deceive and defraud Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But, suddenly feeling vexed with himself, he turned away with a curse and went to the tavern to play billiards.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’s a fool, though he’s a good fellow,” he muttered as he went.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve heard of that officer, Grushenka’s former flame. Well, if he has turned up.... Ech, those pistols! Damn it all! I’m not his nurse! Let them do what they like! Besides, it’ll all come to nothing. They’re a set of brawlers, that’s all. They’ll drink and fight, fight and make friends again. They are not men who do anything real. What does he mean by ‘I’m stepping aside, I’m punishing myself? It’ll come to nothing! He’s shouted such phrases a thousand times, drunk, in the taverns. But now he’s not drunk. ‘Drunk in spirit’—they’re fond of fine phrases, the villains. Am I his nurse? He must have been fighting, his face was all over blood. With whom? I shall find out at the ‘Metropolis. And his handkerchief was soaked in blood.... It’s still lying on my floor.... Hang it!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He reached the tavern in a bad humor and at once made up a game.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The game cheered him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He played a second game, and suddenly began telling one of his partners that Dmitri Karamazov had come in for some cash again—something like three thousand roubles, and had gone to Mokroe again to spend it with Grushenka....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This news roused singular interest in his listeners.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They all spoke of it, not laughing, but with a strange gravity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They left off playing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Three thousand? But where can he have got three thousand?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Questions were asked.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The story of Madame Hohlakov’s present was received with skepticism.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Hasn’t he robbed his old father?—that’s the question.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Three thousand! There’s something odd about it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He boasted aloud that he would kill his father; we all heard him, here. And it was three thousand he talked about ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Pyotr Ilyitch listened.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All at once he became short and dry in his answers.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He said not a word about the blood on Mitya’s face and hands, though he had meant to speak of it at first.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They began a third game, and by degrees the talk about Mitya died away.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But by the end of the third game, Pyotr Ilyitch felt no more desire for billiards; he laid down the cue, and without having supper as he had intended, he walked out of the tavern.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: When he reached the market-place he stood still in perplexity, wondering at himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He realized that what he wanted was to go to Fyodor Pavlovitch’s and find out if anything had happened there.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “On account of some stupid nonsense—as it’s sure to turn out—am I going to wake up the household and make a scandal? Fooh! damn it, is it my business to look after them?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In a very bad humor he went straight home, and suddenly remembered Fenya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Damn it all! I ought to have questioned her just now,” he thought with vexation, “I should have heard everything.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And the desire to speak to her, and so find out, became so pressing and importunate that when he was half-way home he turned abruptly and went towards the house where Grushenka lodged.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Going up to the gate he knocked.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The sound of the knock in the silence of the night sobered him and made him feel annoyed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And no one answered him; every one in the house was asleep.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And I shall be making a fuss!” he thought, with a feeling of positive discomfort.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But instead of going away altogether, he fell to knocking again with all his might, filling the street with clamor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not coming? Well, I will knock them up, I will!” he muttered at each knock, fuming at himself, but at the same time he redoubled his knocks on the gate.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Dmitri Fyodorovitch was speeding along the road.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was a little more than twenty versts to Mokroe, but Andrey’s three horses galloped at such a pace that the distance might be covered in an hour and a quarter.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The swift motion revived Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The air was fresh and cool, there were big stars shining in the sky.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was the very night, and perhaps the very hour, in which Alyosha fell on the earth, and rapturously swore to love it for ever and ever.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All was confusion, confusion, in Mitya’s soul, but although many things were goading his heart, at that moment his whole being was yearning for her, his queen, to whom he was flying to look on her for the last time.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: One thing I can say for certain; his heart did not waver for one instant.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I shall perhaps not be believed when I say that this jealous lover felt not the slightest jealousy of this new rival, who seemed to have sprung out of the earth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If any other had appeared on the scene, he would have been jealous at once, and would perhaps have stained his fierce hands with blood again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But as he flew through the night, he felt no envy, no hostility even, for the man who had been her first lover....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It is true he had not yet seen him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Here there was no room for dispute: it was her right and his; this was her first love which, after five years, she had not forgotten; so she had loved him only for those five years, and I, how do I come in? What right have I? Step aside, Mitya, and make way! What am I now? Now everything is over apart from the officer—even if he had not appeared, everything would be over ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: These words would roughly have expressed his feelings, if he had been capable of reasoning.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But he could not reason at that moment.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His present plan of action had arisen without reasoning.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At Fenya’s first words, it had sprung from feeling, and been adopted in a flash, with all its consequences.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And yet, in spite of his resolution, there was confusion in his soul, an agonizing confusion: his resolution did not give him peace.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was so much behind that tortured him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And it seemed strange to him, at moments, to think that he had written his own sentence of death with pen and paper: “I punish myself,” and the paper was lying there in his pocket, ready; the pistol was loaded; he had already resolved how, next morning, he would meet the first warm ray of “golden-haired Phœbus.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And yet he could not be quit of the past, of all that he had left behind and that tortured him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He felt that miserably, and the thought of it sank into his heart with despair.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was one moment when he felt an impulse to stop Andrey, to jump out of the cart, to pull out his loaded pistol, and to make an end of everything without waiting for the dawn.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But that moment flew by like a spark.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The horses galloped on, “devouring space,” and as he drew near his goal, again the thought of her, of her alone, took more and more complete possession of his soul, chasing away the fearful images that had been haunting it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh, how he longed to look upon her, if only for a moment, if only from a distance!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “She’s now with him,” he thought, “now I shall see what she looks like with him, her first love, and that’s all I want. Never had this woman, who was such a fateful influence in his life, aroused such love in his breast, such new and unknown feeling, surprising even to himself, a feeling tender to devoutness, to self-effacement before her! “I will efface myself!” he said, in a rush of almost hysterical ecstasy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They had been galloping nearly an hour.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya was silent, and though Andrey was, as a rule, a talkative peasant, he did not utter a word, either.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He seemed afraid to talk, he only whipped up smartly his three lean, but mettlesome, bay horses.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Suddenly Mitya cried out in horrible anxiety:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Andrey! What if they’re asleep?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This thought fell upon him like a blow.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It had not occurred to him before.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It may well be that they’re gone to bed, by now, Dmitri Fyodorovitch.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya frowned as though in pain.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yes, indeed ... he was rushing there ... with such feelings ... while they were asleep ... she was asleep, perhaps, there too....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: An angry feeling surged up in his heart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Drive on, Andrey! Whip them up! Look alive!” he cried, beside himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But maybe they’re not in bed! Andrey went on after a pause. “Timofey said they were a lot of them there—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “At the station?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not at the posting-station, but at Plastunov’s, at the inn, where they let out horses, too.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I know. So you say there are a lot of them? How’s that? Who are they?” cried Mitya, greatly dismayed at this unexpected news.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, Timofey was saying they’re all gentlefolk. Two from our town—who they are I can’t say—and there are two others, strangers, maybe more besides. I didn’t ask particularly. They’ve set to playing cards, so Timofey said.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Cards?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So, maybe they’re not in bed if they’re at cards. It’s most likely not more than eleven.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Quicker, Andrey!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Quicker!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya cried again, nervously.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “May I ask you something, sir?” said Andrey, after a pause.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Only I’m afraid of angering you, sir.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What is it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, Fenya threw herself at your feet just now, and begged you not to harm her mistress, and some one else, too ... so you see, sir— It’s I am taking you there ... forgive me, sir, it’s my conscience ... maybe it’s stupid of me to speak of it—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya suddenly seized him by the shoulders from behind.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Are you a driver?” he asked frantically.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, sir.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Then you know that one has to make way. What would you say to a driver who wouldn’t make way for any one, but would just drive on and crush people? No, a driver mustn’t run over people. One can’t run over a man. One can’t spoil people’s lives. And if you have spoilt a life—punish yourself.... If only you’ve spoilt, if only you’ve ruined any one’s life—punish yourself and go away.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: These phrases burst from Mitya almost hysterically.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though Andrey was surprised at him, he kept up the conversation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s right, Dmitri Fyodorovitch, you’re quite right, one mustn’t crush or torment a man, or any kind of creature, for every creature is created by God. Take a horse, for instance, for some folks, even among us drivers, drive anyhow. Nothing will restrain them, they just force it along.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “To hell? Mitya interrupted, and went off into his abrupt, short laugh. “Andrey, simple soul,” he seized him by the shoulders again, “tell me, will Dmitri Fyodorovitch Karamazov go to hell, or not, what do you think?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t know, darling, it depends on you, for you are ... you see, sir, when the Son of God was nailed on the Cross and died, He went straight down to hell from the Cross, and set free all sinners that were in agony. And the devil groaned, because he thought that he would get no more sinners in hell. And God said to him, then, ‘Don’t groan, for you shall have all the mighty of the earth, the rulers, the chief judges, and the rich men, and shall be filled up as you have been in all the ages till I come again. Those were His very words ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “A peasant legend! Capital! Whip up the left, Andrey!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So you see, sir, who it is hell’s for,” said Andrey, whipping up the left horse, “but you’re like a little child ... that’s how we look on you ... and though you’re hasty-tempered, sir, yet God will forgive you for your kind heart.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And you, do you forgive me, Andrey?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What should I forgive you for, sir? You’ve never done me any harm.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, for every one, for every one, you here alone, on the road, will you forgive me for every one? Speak, simple peasant heart!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, sir! I feel afraid of driving you, your talk is so strange.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Mitya did not hear.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was frantically praying and muttering to himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Lord, receive me, with all my lawlessness, and do not condemn me. Let me pass by Thy judgment ... do not condemn me, for I have condemned myself, do not condemn me, for I love Thee, O Lord. I am a wretch, but I love Thee. If Thou sendest me to hell, I shall love Thee there, and from there I shall cry out that I love Thee for ever and ever.... But let me love to the end.... Here and now for just five hours ... till the first light of Thy day ... for I love the queen of my soul ... I love her and I cannot help loving her. Thou seest my whole heart.... I shall gallop up, I shall fall before her and say, ‘You are right to pass on and leave me. Farewell and forget your victim ... never fret yourself about me!’”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mokroe!” cried Andrey, pointing ahead with his whip.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Through the pale darkness of the night loomed a solid black mass of buildings, flung down, as it were, in the vast plain.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The village of Mokroe numbered two thousand inhabitants, but at that hour all were asleep, and only here and there a few lights still twinkled.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Drive on, Andrey, I come!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya exclaimed, feverishly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “They’re not asleep,” said Andrey again, pointing with his whip to the Plastunovs’ inn, which was at the entrance to the village.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The six windows, looking on the street, were all brightly lighted up.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “They’re not asleep,” Mitya repeated joyously.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Quicker, Andrey! Gallop! Drive up with a dash! Set the bells ringing! Let all know that I have come. I’m coming! I’m coming, too!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Andrey lashed his exhausted team into a gallop, drove with a dash and pulled up his steaming, panting horses at the high flight of steps.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya jumped out of the cart just as the innkeeper, on his way to bed, peeped out from the steps curious to see who had arrived.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Trifon Borissovitch, is that you?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The innkeeper bent down, looked intently, ran down the steps, and rushed up to the guest with obsequious delight.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Dmitri Fyodorovitch, your honor! Do I see you again?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Trifon Borissovitch was a thick-set, healthy peasant, of middle height, with a rather fat face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His expression was severe and uncompromising, especially with the peasants of Mokroe, but he had the power of assuming the most obsequious countenance, when he had an inkling that it was to his interest.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He dressed in Russian style, with a shirt buttoning down on one side, and a full-skirted coat.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had saved a good sum of money, but was for ever dreaming of improving his position.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: More than half the peasants were in his clutches, every one in the neighborhood was in debt to him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: From the neighboring landowners he bought and rented lands which were worked by the peasants, in payment of debts which they could never shake off.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was a widower, with four grown-up daughters.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: One of them was already a widow and lived in the inn with her two children, his grandchildren, and worked for him like a charwoman.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Another of his daughters was married to a petty official, and in one of the rooms of the inn, on the wall could be seen, among the family photographs, a miniature photograph of this official in uniform and official epaulettes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The two younger daughters used to wear fashionable blue or green dresses, fitting tight at the back, and with trains a yard long, on Church holidays or when they went to pay visits.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But next morning they would get up at dawn, as usual, sweep out the rooms with a birch-broom, empty the slops, and clean up after lodgers.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In spite of the thousands of roubles he had saved, Trifon Borissovitch was very fond of emptying the pockets of a drunken guest, and remembering that not a month ago he had, in twenty-four hours, made two if not three hundred roubles out of Dmitri, when he had come on his escapade with Grushenka, he met him now with eager welcome, scenting his prey the moment Mitya drove up to the steps.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Dmitri Fyodorovitch, dear sir, we see you once more!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Stay, Trifon Borissovitch,” began Mitya, “first and foremost, where is she?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Agrafena Alexandrovna? The inn-keeper understood at once, looking sharply into Mitya’s face. “She’s here, too ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “With whom? With whom?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Some strangers. One is an official gentleman, a Pole, to judge from his speech. He sent the horses for her from here; and there’s another with him, a friend of his, or a fellow traveler, there’s no telling. They’re dressed like civilians.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, are they feasting? Have they money?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Poor sort of a feast! Nothing to boast of, Dmitri Fyodorovitch.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nothing to boast of? And who are the others?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “They’re two gentlemen from the town.... They’ve come back from Tcherny, and are putting up here. One’s quite a young gentleman, a relative of Mr. Miüsov, he must be, but I’ve forgotten his name ... and I expect you know the other, too, a gentleman called Maximov. He’s been on a pilgrimage, so he says, to the monastery in the town. He’s traveling with this young relation of Mr. Miüsov.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Is that all?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Stay, listen, Trifon Borissovitch. Tell me the chief thing: What of her? How is she?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, she’s only just come. She’s sitting with them.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Is she cheerful? Is she laughing?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, I think she’s not laughing much. She’s sitting quite dull. She’s combing the young gentleman’s hair.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The Pole—the officer?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’s not young, and he’s not an officer, either. Not him, sir. It’s the young gentleman that’s Mr. Miüsov’s relation ... I’ve forgotten his name.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Kalganov.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s it, Kalganov!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “All right. I’ll see for myself. Are they playing cards?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “They have been playing, but they’ve left off. They’ve been drinking tea, the official gentleman asked for liqueurs.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Stay, Trifon Borissovitch, stay, my good soul, I’ll see for myself. Now answer one more question: are the gypsies here?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You can’t have the gypsies now, Dmitri Fyodorovitch. The authorities have sent them away. But we’ve Jews that play the cymbals and the fiddle in the village, so one might send for them. They’d come.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Send for them. Certainly send for them!” cried Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And you can get the girls together as you did then, Marya especially, Stepanida, too, and Arina. Two hundred roubles for a chorus!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, for a sum like that I can get all the village together, though by now they’re asleep. Are the peasants here worth such kindness, Dmitri Fyodorovitch, or the girls either? To spend a sum like that on such coarseness and rudeness! What’s the good of giving a peasant a cigar to smoke, the stinking ruffian! And the girls are all lousy. Besides, I’ll get my daughters up for nothing, let alone a sum like that. They’ve only just gone to bed, I’ll give them a kick and set them singing for you. You gave the peasants champagne to drink the other day, e—ech!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For all his pretended compassion for Mitya, Trifon Borissovitch had hidden half a dozen bottles of champagne on that last occasion, and had picked up a hundred-rouble note under the table, and it had remained in his clutches.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Trifon Borissovitch, I sent more than one thousand flying last time I was here. Do you remember?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You did send it flying. I may well remember. You must have left three thousand behind you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, I’ve come to do the same again, do you see?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And he pulled out his roll of notes, and held them up before the innkeeper’s nose.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Now, listen and remember. In an hour’s time the wine will arrive, savories, pies, and sweets—bring them all up at once. That box Andrey has got is to be brought up at once, too. Open it, and hand champagne immediately. And the girls, we must have the girls, Marya especially.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He turned to the cart and pulled out the box of pistols.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Here, Andrey, let’s settle. Here’s fifteen roubles for the drive, and fifty for vodka ... for your readiness, for your love.... Remember Karamazov!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’m afraid, sir,” faltered Andrey.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Give me five roubles extra, but more I won’t take. Trifon Borissovitch, bear witness. Forgive my foolish words ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What are you afraid of?” asked Mitya, scanning him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, go to the devil, if that’s it!” he cried, flinging him five roubles.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Now, Trifon Borissovitch, take me up quietly and let me first get a look at them, so that they don’t see me. Where are they? In the blue room?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Trifon Borissovitch looked apprehensively at Mitya, but at once obediently did his bidding.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Leading him into the passage, he went himself into the first large room, adjoining that in which the visitors were sitting, and took the light away.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Then he stealthily led Mitya in, and put him in a corner in the dark, whence he could freely watch the company without being seen.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Mitya did not look long, and, indeed, he could not see them, he saw her, his heart throbbed violently, and all was dark before his eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

text: “No, no, c’est fini, don’t trouble yourselves. It’s not worth while soiling one’s hands. I have soiled myself enough through you as it is. You’re not worth it—no one is ... Enough, gentlemen. I’m not going on.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This was said too peremptorily.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch did not insist further, but from Ippolit Kirillovitch’s eyes he saw that he had not given up hope.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Can you not, at least, tell us what sum you had in your hands when you went into Mr. Perhotin’s—how many roubles exactly?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I can’t tell you that.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You spoke to Mr. Perhotin, I believe, of having received three thousand from Madame Hohlakov.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Perhaps I did. Enough, gentlemen. I won’t say how much I had.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Will you be so good then as to tell us how you came here and what you have done since you arrived?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh! you might ask the people here about that. But I’ll tell you if you like.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He proceeded to do so, but we won’t repeat his story.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He told it dryly and curtly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Of the raptures of his love he said nothing, but told them that he abandoned his determination to shoot himself, owing to “new factors in the case.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He told the story without going into motives or details.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And this time the lawyers did not worry him much.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was obvious that there was no essential point of interest to them here.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We shall verify all that. We will come back to it during the examination of the witnesses, which will, of course, take place in your presence,” said Nikolay Parfenovitch in conclusion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And now allow me to request you to lay on the table everything in your possession, especially all the money you still have about you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “My money, gentlemen? Certainly. I understand that that is necessary. I’m surprised, indeed, that you haven’t inquired about it before. It’s true I couldn’t get away anywhere. I’m sitting here where I can be seen. But here’s my money—count it—take it. That’s all, I think.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He turned it all out of his pockets; even the small change—two pieces of twenty copecks—he pulled out of his waistcoat pocket.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They counted the money, which amounted to eight hundred and thirty-six roubles, and forty copecks.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And is that all?” asked the investigating lawyer.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You stated just now in your evidence that you spent three hundred roubles at Plotnikovs’. You gave Perhotin ten, your driver twenty, here you lost two hundred, then....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch reckoned it all up.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya helped him readily.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They recollected every farthing and included it in the reckoning.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch hurriedly added up the total.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “With this eight hundred you must have had about fifteen hundred at first?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I suppose so,” snapped Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How is it they all assert there was much more?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Let them assert it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But you asserted it yourself.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, I did, too.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We will compare all this with the evidence of other persons not yet examined. Don’t be anxious about your money. It will be properly taken care of and be at your disposal at the conclusion of ... what is beginning ... if it appears, or, so to speak, is proved that you have undisputed right to it. Well, and now....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch suddenly got up, and informed Mitya firmly that it was his duty and obligation to conduct a minute and thorough search “of your clothes and everything else....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “By all means, gentlemen. I’ll turn out all my pockets, if you like.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And he did, in fact, begin turning out his pockets.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It will be necessary to take off your clothes, too.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What! Undress? Ugh! Damn it! Won’t you search me as I am! Can’t you?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s utterly impossible, Dmitri Fyodorovitch. You must take off your clothes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “As you like,” Mitya submitted gloomily; “only, please, not here, but behind the curtains. Who will search them?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Behind the curtains, of course.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch bent his head in assent.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His small face wore an expression of peculiar solemnity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Something utterly unexpected and amazing to Mitya followed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He could never, even a minute before, have conceived that any one could behave like that to him, Mitya Karamazov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What was worst of all, there was something humiliating in it, and on their side something “supercilious and scornful. It was nothing to take off his coat, but he was asked to undress further, or rather not asked but “commanded,” he quite understood that.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: From pride and contempt he submitted without a word.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Several peasants accompanied the lawyers and remained on the same side of the curtain.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “To be ready if force is required,” thought Mitya, “and perhaps for some other reason, too.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, must I take off my shirt, too?” he asked sharply, but Nikolay Parfenovitch did not answer.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was busily engaged with the prosecutor in examining the coat, the trousers, the waistcoat and the cap; and it was evident that they were both much interested in the scrutiny.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “They make no bones about it,” thought Mitya, “they don’t keep up the most elementary politeness.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I ask you for the second time—need I take off my shirt or not?” he said, still more sharply and irritably.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t trouble yourself. We will tell you what to do,” Nikolay Parfenovitch said, and his voice was positively peremptory, or so it seemed to Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Meantime a consultation was going on in undertones between the lawyers.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There turned out to be on the coat, especially on the left side at the back, a huge patch of blood, dry, and still stiff.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There were bloodstains on the trousers, too.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch, moreover, in the presence of the peasant witnesses, passed his fingers along the collar, the cuffs, and all the seams of the coat and trousers, obviously looking for something—money, of course.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He didn’t even hide from Mitya his suspicion that he was capable of sewing money up in his clothes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He treats me not as an officer but as a thief,” Mitya muttered to himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They communicated their ideas to one another with amazing frankness.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The secretary, for instance, who was also behind the curtain, fussing about and listening, called Nikolay Parfenovitch’s attention to the cap, which they were also fingering.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You remember Gridyenko, the copying-clerk,” observed the secretary.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Last summer he received the wages of the whole office, and pretended to have lost the money when he was drunk. And where was it found? Why, in just such pipings in his cap. The hundred-rouble notes were screwed up in little rolls and sewed in the piping.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Both the lawyers remembered Gridyenko’s case perfectly, and so laid aside Mitya’s cap, and decided that all his clothes must be more thoroughly examined later.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Excuse me,” cried Nikolay Parfenovitch, suddenly, noticing that the right cuff of Mitya’s shirt was turned in, and covered with blood, “excuse me, what’s that, blood?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes,” Mitya jerked out.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That is, what blood? ... and why is the cuff turned in?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya told him how he had got the sleeve stained with blood looking after Grigory, and had turned it inside when he was washing his hands at Perhotin’s.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You must take off your shirt, too. That’s very important as material evidence.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya flushed red and flew into a rage.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What, am I to stay naked?” he shouted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t disturb yourself. We will arrange something. And meanwhile take off your socks.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’re not joking?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Is that really necessary?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya’s eyes flashed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We are in no mood for joking,” answered Nikolay Parfenovitch sternly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, if I must—” muttered Mitya, and sitting down on the bed, he took off his socks.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He felt unbearably awkward.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All were clothed, while he was naked, and strange to say, when he was undressed he felt somehow guilty in their presence, and was almost ready to believe himself that he was inferior to them, and that now they had a perfect right to despise him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “When all are undressed, one is somehow not ashamed, but when one’s the only one undressed and everybody is looking, it’s degrading,” he kept repeating to himself, again and again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s like a dream, I’ve sometimes dreamed of being in such degrading positions.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was a misery to him to take off his socks.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They were very dirty, and so were his underclothes, and now every one could see it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And what was worse, he disliked his feet.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All his life he had thought both his big toes hideous.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He particularly loathed the coarse, flat, crooked nail on the right one, and now they would all see it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Feeling intolerably ashamed made him, at once and intentionally, rougher.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He pulled off his shirt, himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Would you like to look anywhere else if you’re not ashamed to?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, there’s no need to, at present.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, am I to stay naked like this?” he added savagely.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, that can’t be helped for the time.... Kindly sit down here for a while. You can wrap yourself in a quilt from the bed, and I ... I’ll see to all this.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All the things were shown to the witnesses.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The report of the search was drawn up, and at last Nikolay Parfenovitch went out, and the clothes were carried out after him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ippolit Kirillovitch went out, too.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya was left alone with the peasants, who stood in silence, never taking their eyes off him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya wrapped himself up in the quilt.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He felt cold.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His bare feet stuck out, and he couldn’t pull the quilt over so as to cover them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch seemed to be gone a long time, “an insufferable time. “He thinks of me as a puppy,” thought Mitya, gnashing his teeth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That rotten prosecutor has gone, too, contemptuous no doubt, it disgusts him to see me naked!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya imagined, however, that his clothes would be examined and returned to him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But what was his indignation when Nikolay Parfenovitch came back with quite different clothes, brought in behind him by a peasant.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Here are clothes for you,” he observed airily, seeming well satisfied with the success of his mission.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mr. Kalganov has kindly provided these for this unusual emergency, as well as a clean shirt. Luckily he had them all in his trunk. You can keep your own socks and underclothes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya flew into a passion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I won’t have other people’s clothes!” he shouted menacingly, “give me my own!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s impossible!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Give me my own. Damn Kalganov and his clothes, too!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was a long time before they could persuade him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But they succeeded somehow in quieting him down.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They impressed upon him that his clothes, being stained with blood, must be “included with the other material evidence,” and that they “had not even the right to let him have them now ... taking into consideration the possible outcome of the case. Mitya at last understood this. He subsided into gloomy silence and hurriedly dressed himself. He merely observed, as he put them on, that the clothes were much better than his old ones, and that he disliked “gaining by the change. The coat was, besides, “ridiculously tight. Am I to be dressed up like a fool ... for your amusement?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They urged upon him again that he was exaggerating, that Kalganov was only a little taller, so that only the trousers might be a little too long.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the coat turned out to be really tight in the shoulders.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Damn it all! I can hardly button it,” Mitya grumbled.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Be so good as to tell Mr. Kalganov from me that I didn’t ask for his clothes, and it’s not my doing that they’ve dressed me up like a clown.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He understands that, and is sorry ... I mean, not sorry to lend you his clothes, but sorry about all this business,” mumbled Nikolay Parfenovitch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Confound his sorrow! Well, where now? Am I to go on sitting here?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was asked to go back to the “other room. Mitya went in, scowling with anger, and trying to avoid looking at any one. Dressed in another man’s clothes he felt himself disgraced, even in the eyes of the peasants, and of Trifon Borissovitch, whose face appeared, for some reason, in the doorway, and vanished immediately. “He’s come to look at me dressed up,” thought Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He sat down on the same chair as before.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had an absurd nightmarish feeling, as though he were out of his mind.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, what now? Are you going to flog me? That’s all that’s left for you,” he said, clenching his teeth and addressing the prosecutor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He would not turn to Nikolay Parfenovitch, as though he disdained to speak to him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He looked too closely at my socks, and turned them inside out on purpose to show every one how dirty they were—the scoundrel!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, now we must proceed to the examination of witnesses,” observed Nikolay Parfenovitch, as though in reply to Mitya’s question.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes,” said the prosecutor thoughtfully, as though reflecting on something.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We’ve done what we could in your interest, Dmitri Fyodorovitch,” Nikolay Parfenovitch went on, “but having received from you such an uncompromising refusal to explain to us the source from which you obtained the money found upon you, we are, at the present moment—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What is the stone in your ring?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya interrupted suddenly, as though awakening from a reverie.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He pointed to one of the three large rings adorning Nikolay Parfenovitch’s right hand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ring?” repeated Nikolay Parfenovitch with surprise.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, that one ... on your middle finger, with the little veins in it, what stone is that?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya persisted, like a peevish child.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s a smoky topaz,” said Nikolay Parfenovitch, smiling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Would you like to look at it? I’ll take it off ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, don’t take it off,” cried Mitya furiously, suddenly waking up, and angry with himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t take it off ... there’s no need.... Damn it!... Gentlemen, you’ve sullied my heart! Can you suppose that I would conceal it from you, if I had really killed my father, that I would shuffle, lie, and hide myself? No, that’s not like Dmitri Karamazov, that he couldn’t do, and if I were guilty, I swear I shouldn’t have waited for your coming, or for the sunrise as I meant at first, but should have killed myself before this, without waiting for the dawn! I know that about myself now. I couldn’t have learnt so much in twenty years as I’ve found out in this accursed night!... And should I have been like this on this night, and at this moment, sitting with you, could I have talked like this, could I have moved like this, could I have looked at you and at the world like this, if I had really been the murderer of my father, when the very thought of having accidentally killed Grigory gave me no peace all night—not from fear—oh, not simply from fear of your punishment! The disgrace of it! And you expect me to be open with such scoffers as you, who see nothing and believe in nothing, blind moles and scoffers, and to tell you another nasty thing I’ve done, another disgrace, even if that would save me from your accusation! No, better Siberia! The man who opened the door to my father and went in at that door, he killed him, he robbed him. Who was he? I’m racking my brains and can’t think who. But I can tell you it was not Dmitri Karamazov, and that’s all I can tell you, and that’s enough, enough, leave me alone.... Exile me, punish me, but don’t bother me any more. I’ll say no more. Call your witnesses!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya uttered his sudden monologue as though he were determined to be absolutely silent for the future.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The prosecutor watched him the whole time and only when he had ceased speaking, observed, as though it were the most ordinary thing, with the most frigid and composed air:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, about the open door of which you spoke just now, we may as well inform you, by the way, now, of a very interesting piece of evidence of the greatest importance both to you and to us, that has been given us by Grigory, the old man you wounded. On his recovery, he clearly and emphatically stated, in reply to our questions, that when, on coming out to the steps, and hearing a noise in the garden, he made up his mind to go into it through the little gate which stood open, before he noticed you running, as you have told us already, in the dark from the open window where you saw your father, he, Grigory, glanced to the left, and, while noticing the open window, observed at the same time, much nearer to him, the door, standing wide open—that door which you have stated to have been shut the whole time you were in the garden. I will not conceal from you that Grigory himself confidently affirms and bears witness that you must have run from that door, though, of course, he did not see you do so with his own eyes, since he only noticed you first some distance away in the garden, running towards the fence.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya had leapt up from his chair half-way through this speech.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nonsense!” he yelled, in a sudden frenzy, “it’s a barefaced lie. He couldn’t have seen the door open because it was shut. He’s lying!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I consider it my duty to repeat that he is firm in his statement. He does not waver. He adheres to it. We’ve cross-examined him several times.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Precisely. I have cross-examined him several times,” Nikolay Parfenovitch confirmed warmly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s false, false! It’s either an attempt to slander me, or the hallucination of a madman,” Mitya still shouted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’s simply raving, from loss of blood, from the wound. He must have fancied it when he came to.... He’s raving.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, but he noticed the open door, not when he came to after his injuries, but before that, as soon as he went into the garden from the lodge.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But it’s false, it’s false! It can’t be so! He’s slandering me from spite.... He couldn’t have seen it ... I didn’t come from the door,” gasped Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The prosecutor turned to Nikolay Parfenovitch and said to him impressively:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Confront him with it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do you recognize this object?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch laid upon the table a large and thick official envelope, on which three seals still remained intact.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The envelope was empty, and slit open at one end.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya stared at it with open eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It ... it must be that envelope of my father’s, the envelope that contained the three thousand roubles ... and if there’s inscribed on it, allow me, ‘For my little chicken’ ... yes—three thousand!” he shouted, “do you see, three thousand, do you see?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Of course, we see. But we didn’t find the money in it. It was empty, and lying on the floor by the bed, behind the screen.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For some seconds Mitya stood as though thunderstruck.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Gentlemen, it’s Smerdyakov!” he shouted suddenly, at the top of his voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s he who’s murdered him! He’s robbed him! No one else knew where the old man hid the envelope. It’s Smerdyakov, that’s clear, now!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But you, too, knew of the envelope and that it was under the pillow.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I never knew it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I’ve never seen it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This is the first time I’ve looked at it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I’d only heard of it from Smerdyakov....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was the only one who knew where the old man kept it hidden, I didn’t know ...

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya was completely breathless.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But you told us yourself that the envelope was under your deceased father’s pillow. You especially stated that it was under the pillow, so you must have known it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We’ve got it written down,” confirmed Nikolay Parfenovitch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nonsense! It’s absurd! I’d no idea it was under the pillow. And perhaps it wasn’t under the pillow at all.... It was just a chance guess that it was under the pillow. What does Smerdyakov say? Have you asked him where it was? What does Smerdyakov say? that’s the chief point.... And I went out of my way to tell lies against myself.... I told you without thinking that it was under the pillow, and now you— Oh, you know how one says the wrong thing, without meaning it. No one knew but Smerdyakov, only Smerdyakov, and no one else.... He didn’t even tell me where it was! But it’s his doing, his doing; there’s no doubt about it, he murdered him, that’s as clear as daylight now,” Mitya exclaimed more and more frantically, repeating himself incoherently, and growing more and more exasperated and excited.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You must understand that, and arrest him at once.... He must have killed him while I was running away and while Grigory was unconscious, that’s clear now.... He gave the signal and father opened to him ... for no one but he knew the signal, and without the signal father would never have opened the door....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But you’re again forgetting the circumstance,” the prosecutor observed, still speaking with the same restraint, though with a note of triumph, “that there was no need to give the signal if the door already stood open when you were there, while you were in the garden....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The door, the door,” muttered Mitya, and he stared speechless at the prosecutor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He sank back helpless in his chair.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All were silent.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, the door!... It’s a nightmare! God is against me!” he exclaimed, staring before him in complete stupefaction.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Come, you see,” the prosecutor went on with dignity, “and you can judge for yourself, Dmitri Fyodorovitch. On the one hand we have the evidence of the open door from which you ran out, a fact which overwhelms you and us. On the other side your incomprehensible, persistent, and, so to speak, obdurate silence with regard to the source from which you obtained the money which was so suddenly seen in your hands, when only three hours earlier, on your own showing, you pledged your pistols for the sake of ten roubles! In view of all these facts, judge for yourself. What are we to believe, and what can we depend upon? And don’t accuse us of being ‘frigid, cynical, scoffing people,’ who are incapable of believing in the generous impulses of your heart.... Try to enter into our position ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya was indescribably agitated.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He turned pale.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Very well!” he exclaimed suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I will tell you my secret. I’ll tell you where I got the money!... I’ll reveal my shame, that I may not have to blame myself or you hereafter.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And believe me, Dmitri Fyodorovitch,” put in Nikolay Parfenovitch, in a voice of almost pathetic delight, “that every sincere and complete confession on your part at this moment may, later on, have an immense influence in your favor, and may, indeed, moreover—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the prosecutor gave him a slight shove under the table, and he checked himself in time.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya, it is true, had not heard him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Gentlemen,” he began, still in the same agitation, “I want to make a full confession: that money was my own.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The lawyers’ faces lengthened.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That was not at all what they expected.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How do you mean?” faltered Nikolay Parfenovitch, “when at five o’clock on the same day, from your own confession—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Damn five o’clock on the same day and my own confession! That’s nothing to do with it now! That money was my own, my own, that is, stolen by me ... not mine, I mean, but stolen by me, and it was fifteen hundred roubles, and I had it on me all the time, all the time ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But where did you get it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I took it off my neck, gentlemen, off this very neck ... it was here, round my neck, sewn up in a rag, and I’d had it round my neck a long time, it’s a month since I put it round my neck ... to my shame and disgrace!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And from whom did you ... appropriate it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You mean, ‘steal it’? Speak out plainly now. Yes, I consider that I practically stole it, but, if you prefer, I ‘appropriated it. I consider I stole it. And last night I stole it finally.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Last night? But you said that it’s a month since you ... obtained it?...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes. But not from my father. Not from my father, don’t be uneasy. I didn’t steal it from my father, but from her. Let me tell you without interrupting. It’s hard to do, you know. You see, a month ago, I was sent for by Katerina Ivanovna, formerly my betrothed. Do you know her?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, of course.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I know you know her. She’s a noble creature, noblest of the noble. But she has hated me ever so long, oh, ever so long ... and hated me with good reason, good reason!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Katerina Ivanovna!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch exclaimed with wonder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The prosecutor, too, stared.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, don’t take her name in vain! I’m a scoundrel to bring her into it. Yes, I’ve seen that she hated me ... a long while.... From the very first, even that evening at my lodging ... but enough, enough. You’re unworthy even to know of that. No need of that at all.... I need only tell you that she sent for me a month ago, gave me three thousand roubles to send off to her sister and another relation in Moscow (as though she couldn’t have sent it off herself!) and I ... it was just at that fatal moment in my life when I ... well, in fact, when I’d just come to love another, her, she’s sitting down below now, Grushenka. I carried her off here to Mokroe then, and wasted here in two days half that damned three thousand, but the other half I kept on me. Well, I’ve kept that other half, that fifteen hundred, like a locket round my neck, but yesterday I undid it, and spent it. What’s left of it, eight hundred roubles, is in your hands now, Nikolay Parfenovitch. That’s the change out of the fifteen hundred I had yesterday.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Excuse me. How’s that? Why, when you were here a month ago you spent three thousand, not fifteen hundred, everybody knows that.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Who knows it? Who counted the money? Did I let any one count it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, you told every one yourself that you’d spent exactly three thousand.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s true, I did. I told the whole town so, and the whole town said so. And here, at Mokroe, too, every one reckoned it was three thousand. Yet I didn’t spend three thousand, but fifteen hundred. And the other fifteen hundred I sewed into a little bag. That’s how it was, gentlemen. That’s where I got that money yesterday....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “This is almost miraculous,” murmured Nikolay Parfenovitch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Allow me to inquire,” observed the prosecutor at last, “have you informed any one whatever of this circumstance before, I mean that you had fifteen hundred left about you a month ago?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I told no one.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s strange. Do you mean absolutely no one?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Absolutely no one. No one and nobody.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What was your reason for this reticence? What was your motive for making such a secret of it? To be more precise: You have told us at last your secret, in your words, so ‘disgraceful,’ though in reality—that is, of course, comparatively speaking—this action, that is, the appropriation of three thousand roubles belonging to some one else, and, of course, only for a time is, in my view at least, only an act of the greatest recklessness and not so disgraceful, when one takes into consideration your character.... Even admitting that it was an action in the highest degree discreditable, still, discreditable is not ‘disgraceful.’... Many people have already guessed, during this last month, about the three thousand of Katerina Ivanovna’s, that you have spent, and I heard the legend myself, apart from your confession.... Mihail Makarovitch, for instance, had heard it, too, so that indeed, it was scarcely a legend, but the gossip of the whole town. There are indications, too, if I am not mistaken, that you confessed this yourself to some one, I mean that the money was Katerina Ivanovna’s, and so, it’s extremely surprising to me that hitherto, that is, up to the present moment, you have made such an extraordinary secret of the fifteen hundred you say you put by, apparently connecting a feeling of positive horror with that secret.... It’s not easy to believe that it could cost you such distress to confess such a secret.... You cried out, just now, that Siberia would be better than confessing it ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The prosecutor ceased speaking.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was provoked.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He did not conceal his vexation, which was almost anger, and gave vent to all his accumulated spleen, disconnectedly and incoherently, without choosing words.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s not the fifteen hundred that’s the disgrace, but that I put it apart from the rest of the three thousand,” said Mitya firmly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why?” smiled the prosecutor irritably.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What is there disgraceful, to your thinking, in your having set aside half of the three thousand you had discreditably, if you prefer, ‘disgracefully,’ appropriated? Your taking the three thousand is more important than what you did with it. And by the way, why did you do that—why did you set apart that half, for what purpose, for what object did you do it? Can you explain that to us?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, gentlemen, the purpose is the whole point!” cried Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I put it aside because I was vile, that is, because I was calculating, and to be calculating in such a case is vile ... and that vileness has been going on a whole month.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s incomprehensible.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I wonder at you. But I’ll make it clearer. Perhaps it really is incomprehensible. You see, attend to what I say. I appropriate three thousand entrusted to my honor, I spend it on a spree, say I spend it all, and next morning I go to her and say, ‘Katya, I’ve done wrong, I’ve squandered your three thousand,’ well, is that right? No, it’s not right—it’s dishonest and cowardly, I’m a beast, with no more self-control than a beast, that’s so, isn’t it? But still I’m not a thief? Not a downright thief, you’ll admit! I squandered it, but I didn’t steal it. Now a second, rather more favorable alternative: follow me carefully, or I may get confused again—my head’s going round—and so, for the second alternative: I spend here only fifteen hundred out of the three thousand, that is, only half. Next day I go and take that half to her: ‘Katya, take this fifteen hundred from me, I’m a low beast, and an untrustworthy scoundrel, for I’ve wasted half the money, and I shall waste this, too, so keep me from temptation! Well, what of that alternative? I should be a beast and a scoundrel, and whatever you like; but not a thief, not altogether a thief, or I should not have brought back what was left, but have kept that, too. She would see at once that since I brought back half, I should pay back what I’d spent, that I should never give up trying to, that I should work to get it and pay it back. So in that case I should be a scoundrel, but not a thief, you may say what you like, not a thief!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I admit that there is a certain distinction,” said the prosecutor, with a cold smile.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But it’s strange that you see such a vital difference.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, I see a vital difference! Every man may be a scoundrel, and perhaps every man is a scoundrel, but not every one can be a thief, it takes an arch-scoundrel to be that. Oh, of course, I don’t know how to make these fine distinctions ... but a thief is lower than a scoundrel, that’s my conviction. Listen, I carry the money about me a whole month, I may make up my mind to give it back to-morrow, and I’m a scoundrel no longer, but I cannot make up my mind, you see, though I’m making up my mind every day, and every day spurring myself on to do it, and yet for a whole month I can’t bring myself to it, you see. Is that right to your thinking, is that right?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Certainly, that’s not right, that I can quite understand, and that I don’t dispute,” answered the prosecutor with reserve.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And let us give up all discussion of these subtleties and distinctions, and, if you will be so kind, get back to the point. And the point is, that you have still not told us, altogether we’ve asked you, why, in the first place, you halved the money, squandering one half and hiding the other? For what purpose exactly did you hide it, what did you mean to do with that fifteen hundred? I insist upon that question, Dmitri Fyodorovitch.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, of course!” cried Mitya, striking himself on the forehead; “forgive me, I’m worrying you, and am not explaining the chief point, or you’d understand in a minute, for it’s just the motive of it that’s the disgrace! You see, it was all to do with the old man, my dead father. He was always pestering Agrafena Alexandrovna, and I was jealous; I thought then that she was hesitating between me and him. So I kept thinking every day, suppose she were to make up her mind all of a sudden, suppose she were to leave off tormenting me, and were suddenly to say to me, ‘I love you, not him; take me to the other end of the world. And I’d only forty copecks; how could I take her away, what could I do? Why, I’d be lost. You see, I didn’t know her then, I didn’t understand her, I thought she wanted money, and that she wouldn’t forgive my poverty. And so I fiendishly counted out the half of that three thousand, sewed it up, calculating on it, sewed it up before I was drunk, and after I had sewn it up, I went off to get drunk on the rest. Yes, that was base. Do you understand now?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Both the lawyers laughed aloud.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I should have called it sensible and moral on your part not to have squandered it all,” chuckled Nikolay Parfenovitch, “for after all what does it amount to?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, that I stole it, that’s what it amounts to! Oh, God, you horrify me by not understanding! Every day that I had that fifteen hundred sewn up round my neck, every day and every hour I said to myself, ‘You’re a thief! you’re a thief! Yes, that’s why I’ve been so savage all this month, that’s why I fought in the tavern, that’s why I attacked my father, it was because I felt I was a thief. I couldn’t make up my mind, I didn’t dare even to tell Alyosha, my brother, about that fifteen hundred: I felt I was such a scoundrel and such a pickpocket. But, do you know, while I carried it I said to myself at the same time every hour: ‘No, Dmitri Fyodorovitch, you may yet not be a thief. Why? Because I might go next day and pay back that fifteen hundred to Katya. And only yesterday I made up my mind to tear my amulet off my neck, on my way from Fenya’s to Perhotin. I hadn’t been able till that moment to bring myself to it. And it was only when I tore it off that I became a downright thief, a thief and a dishonest man for the rest of my life. Why? Because, with that I destroyed, too, my dream of going to Katya and saying, ‘I’m a scoundrel, but not a thief! Do you understand now? Do you understand?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What was it made you decide to do it yesterday?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch interrupted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why? It’s absurd to ask. Because I had condemned myself to die at five o’clock this morning, here, at dawn. I thought it made no difference whether I died a thief or a man of honor. But I see it’s not so, it turns out that it does make a difference. Believe me, gentlemen, what has tortured me most during this night has not been the thought that I’d killed the old servant, and that I was in danger of Siberia just when my love was being rewarded, and Heaven was open to me again. Oh, that did torture me, but not in the same way: not so much as the damned consciousness that I had torn that damned money off my breast at last and spent it, and had become a downright thief! Oh, gentlemen, I tell you again, with a bleeding heart, I have learnt a great deal this night. I have learnt that it’s not only impossible to live a scoundrel, but impossible to die a scoundrel.... No, gentlemen, one must die honest....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya was pale.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His face had a haggard and exhausted look, in spite of his being intensely excited.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I am beginning to understand you, Dmitri Fyodorovitch,” the prosecutor said slowly, in a soft and almost compassionate tone.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
