text: “But all this, if you’ll excuse my saying so, is a matter of nerves, in my opinion ... your overwrought nerves, that’s what it is. And why, for instance, should you not have saved yourself such misery for almost a month, by going and returning that fifteen hundred to the lady who had entrusted it to you? And why could you not have explained things to her, and in view of your position, which you describe as being so awful, why could you not have had recourse to the plan which would so naturally have occurred to one’s mind, that is, after honorably confessing your errors to her, why could you not have asked her to lend you the sum needed for your expenses, which, with her generous heart, she would certainly not have refused you in your distress, especially if it had been with some guarantee, or even on the security you offered to the merchant Samsonov, and to Madame Hohlakov? I suppose you still regard that security as of value?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya suddenly crimsoned.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Surely you don’t think me such an out and out scoundrel as that? You can’t be speaking in earnest?” he said, with indignation, looking the prosecutor straight in the face, and seeming unable to believe his ears.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I assure you I’m in earnest....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why do you imagine I’m not serious?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was the prosecutor’s turn to be surprised.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, how base that would have been! Gentlemen, do you know, you are torturing me! Let me tell you everything, so be it. I’ll confess all my infernal wickedness, but to put you to shame, and you’ll be surprised yourselves at the depth of ignominy to which a medley of human passions can sink. You must know that I already had that plan myself, that plan you spoke of, just now, prosecutor! Yes, gentlemen, I, too, have had that thought in my mind all this current month, so that I was on the point of deciding to go to Katya—I was mean enough for that. But to go to her, to tell her of my treachery, and for that very treachery, to carry it out, for the expenses of that treachery, to beg for money from her, Katya (to beg, do you hear, to beg), and go straight from her to run away with the other, the rival, who hated and insulted her—to think of it! You must be mad, prosecutor!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mad I am not, but I did speak in haste, without thinking ... of that feminine jealousy ... if there could be jealousy in this case, as you assert ... yes, perhaps there is something of the kind,” said the prosecutor, smiling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But that would have been so infamous! Mitya brought his fist down on the table fiercely. “That would have been filthy beyond everything! Yes, do you know that she might have given me that money, yes, and she would have given it, too; she’d have been certain to give it, to be revenged on me, she’d have given it to satisfy her vengeance, to show her contempt for me, for hers is an infernal nature, too, and she’s a woman of great wrath. I’d have taken the money, too, oh, I should have taken it; I should have taken it, and then, for the rest of my life ... oh, God! Forgive me, gentlemen, I’m making such an outcry because I’ve had that thought in my mind so lately, only the day before yesterday, that night when I was having all that bother with Lyagavy, and afterwards yesterday, all day yesterday, I remember, till that happened ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Till what happened?” put in Nikolay Parfenovitch inquisitively, but Mitya did not hear it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I have made you an awful confession,” Mitya said gloomily in conclusion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You must appreciate it, and what’s more, you must respect it, for if not, if that leaves your souls untouched, then you’ve simply no respect for me, gentlemen, I tell you that, and I shall die of shame at having confessed it to men like you! Oh, I shall shoot myself! Yes, I see, I see already that you don’t believe me. What, you want to write that down, too?” he cried in dismay.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, what you said just now,” said Nikolay Parfenovitch, looking at him in surprise, “that is, that up to the last hour you were still contemplating going to Katerina Ivanovna to beg that sum from her.... I assure you, that’s a very important piece of evidence for us, Dmitri Fyodorovitch, I mean for the whole case ... and particularly for you, particularly important for you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Have mercy, gentlemen! Mitya flung up his hands. “Don’t write that, anyway; have some shame. Here I’ve torn my heart asunder before you, and you seize the opportunity and are fingering the wounds in both halves.... Oh, my God!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In despair he hid his face in his hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t worry yourself so, Dmitri Fyodorovitch,” observed the prosecutor, “everything that is written down will be read over to you afterwards, and what you don’t agree to we’ll alter as you like. But now I’ll ask you one little question for the second time. Has no one, absolutely no one, heard from you of that money you sewed up? That, I must tell you, is almost impossible to believe.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No one, no one, I told you so before, or you’ve not understood anything! Let me alone!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Very well, this matter is bound to be explained, and there’s plenty of time for it, but meantime, consider; we have perhaps a dozen witnesses that you yourself spread it abroad, and even shouted almost everywhere about the three thousand you’d spent here; three thousand, not fifteen hundred. And now, too, when you got hold of the money you had yesterday, you gave many people to understand that you had brought three thousand with you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’ve got not dozens, but hundreds of witnesses, two hundred witnesses, two hundred have heard it, thousands have heard it!” cried Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, you see, all bear witness to it. And the word all means something.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It means nothing. I talked rot, and every one began repeating it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But what need had you to ‘talk rot,’ as you call it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The devil knows. From bravado perhaps ... at having wasted so much money.... To try and forget that money I had sewn up, perhaps ... yes, that was why ... damn it ... how often will you ask me that question? Well, I told a fib, and that was the end of it, once I’d said it, I didn’t care to correct it. What does a man tell lies for sometimes?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s very difficult to decide, Dmitri Fyodorovitch, what makes a man tell lies,” observed the prosecutor impressively.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Tell me, though, was that ‘amulet,’ as you call it, on your neck, a big thing?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, not big.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How big, for instance?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “If you fold a hundred-rouble note in half, that would be the size.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’d better show us the remains of it. You must have them somewhere.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Damnation, what nonsense! I don’t know where they are.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But excuse me: where and when did you take it off your neck? According to your own evidence you didn’t go home.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “When I was going from Fenya’s to Perhotin’s, on the way I tore it off my neck and took out the money.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “In the dark?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What should I want a light for? I did it with my fingers in one minute.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Without scissors, in the street?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “In the market-place I think it was. Why scissors? It was an old rag. It was torn in a minute.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Where did you put it afterwards?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I dropped it there.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Where was it, exactly?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “In the market-place, in the market-place! The devil knows whereabouts. What do you want to know for?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s extremely important, Dmitri Fyodorovitch. It would be material evidence in your favor. How is it you don’t understand that? Who helped you to sew it up a month ago?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No one helped me. I did it myself.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Can you sew?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “A soldier has to know how to sew. No knowledge was needed to do that.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Where did you get the material, that is, the rag in which you sewed the money?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Are you laughing at me?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not at all. And we are in no mood for laughing, Dmitri Fyodorovitch.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t know where I got the rag from—somewhere, I suppose.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I should have thought you couldn’t have forgotten it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Upon my word, I don’t remember. I might have torn a bit off my linen.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s very interesting. We might find in your lodgings to-morrow the shirt or whatever it is from which you tore the rag. What sort of rag was it, cloth or linen?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Goodness only knows what it was. Wait a bit.... I believe I didn’t tear it off anything. It was a bit of calico.... I believe I sewed it up in a cap of my landlady’s.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “In your landlady’s cap?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes. I took it from her.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How did you get it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You see, I remember once taking a cap for a rag, perhaps to wipe my pen on. I took it without asking, because it was a worthless rag. I tore it up, and I took the notes and sewed them up in it. I believe it was in that very rag I sewed them. An old piece of calico, washed a thousand times.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And you remember that for certain now?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t know whether for certain. I think it was in the cap. But, hang it, what does it matter?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “In that case your landlady will remember that the thing was lost?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, she won’t, she didn’t miss it. It was an old rag, I tell you, an old rag not worth a farthing.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And where did you get the needle and thread?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ll stop now. I won’t say any more. Enough of it!” said Mitya, losing his temper at last.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s strange that you should have so completely forgotten where you threw the pieces in the market-place.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Give orders for the market-place to be swept to-morrow, and perhaps you’ll find it,” said Mitya, sneering.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Enough, gentlemen, enough!” he decided, in an exhausted voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I see you don’t believe me! Not for a moment! It’s my fault, not yours. I ought not to have been so ready. Why, why did I degrade myself by confessing my secret to you? It’s a joke to you. I see that from your eyes. You led me on to it, prosecutor? Sing a hymn of triumph if you can.... Damn you, you torturers!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He bent his head, and hid his face in his hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The lawyers were silent.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A minute later he raised his head and looked at them almost vacantly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His face now expressed complete, hopeless despair, and he sat mute and passive as though hardly conscious of what was happening.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In the meantime they had to finish what they were about.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They had immediately to begin examining the witnesses.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was by now eight o’clock in the morning.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The lights had been extinguished long ago.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mihail Makarovitch and Kalganov, who had been continually in and out of the room all the while the interrogation had been going on, had now both gone out again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The lawyers, too, looked very tired.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was a wretched morning, the whole sky was overcast, and the rain streamed down in bucketfuls.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya gazed blankly out of the window.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “May I look out of the window?” he asked Nikolay Parfenovitch, suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, as much as you like,” the latter replied.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya got up and went to the window....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The rain lashed against its little greenish panes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He could see the muddy road just below the house, and farther away, in the rain and mist, a row of poor, black, dismal huts, looking even blacker and poorer in the rain.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya thought of “Phœbus the golden-haired,” and how he had meant to shoot himself at his first ray.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Perhaps it would be even better on a morning like this,” he thought with a smile, and suddenly, flinging his hand downwards, he turned to his “torturers.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Gentlemen,” he cried, “I see that I am lost! But she? Tell me about her, I beseech you. Surely she need not be ruined with me? She’s innocent, you know, she was out of her mind when she cried last night ‘It’s all my fault! She’s done nothing, nothing! I’ve been grieving over her all night as I sat with you.... Can’t you, won’t you tell me what you are going to do with her now?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You can set your mind quite at rest on that score, Dmitri Fyodorovitch,” the prosecutor answered at once, with evident alacrity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We have, so far, no grounds for interfering with the lady in whom you are so interested. I trust that it may be the same in the later development of the case.... On the contrary, we’ll do everything that lies in our power in that matter. Set your mind completely at rest.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Gentlemen, I thank you. I knew that you were honest, straight-forward people in spite of everything. You’ve taken a load off my heart.... Well, what are we to do now? I’m ready.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, we ought to make haste. We must pass to examining the witnesses without delay. That must be done in your presence and therefore—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Shouldn’t we have some tea first?” interposed Nikolay Parfenovitch, “I think we’ve deserved it!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They decided that if tea were ready downstairs (Mihail Makarovitch had, no doubt, gone down to get some) they would have a glass and then “go on and on,” putting off their proper breakfast until a more favorable opportunity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Tea really was ready below, and was soon brought up.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya at first refused the glass that Nikolay Parfenovitch politely offered him, but afterwards he asked for it himself and drank it greedily.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He looked surprisingly exhausted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It might have been supposed from his Herculean strength that one night of carousing, even accompanied by the most violent emotions, could have had little effect on him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But he felt that he could hardly hold his head up, and from time to time all the objects about him seemed heaving and dancing before his eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “A little more and I shall begin raving,” he said to himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The examination of the witnesses began.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But we will not continue our story in such detail as before.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And so we will not dwell on how Nikolay Parfenovitch impressed on every witness called that he must give his evidence in accordance with truth and conscience, and that he would afterwards have to repeat his evidence on oath, how every witness was called upon to sign the protocol of his evidence, and so on.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: We will only note that the point principally insisted upon in the examination was the question of the three thousand roubles, that is, was the sum spent here, at Mokroe, by Mitya on the first occasion, a month before, three thousand or fifteen hundred?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And again had he spent three thousand or fifteen hundred yesterday?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alas, all the evidence given by every one turned out to be against Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was not one in his favor, and some witnesses introduced new, almost crushing facts, in contradiction of his, Mitya’s, story.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The first witness examined was Trifon Borissovitch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was not in the least abashed as he stood before the lawyers.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had, on the contrary, an air of stern and severe indignation with the accused, which gave him an appearance of truthfulness and personal dignity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He spoke little, and with reserve, waited to be questioned, answered precisely and deliberately.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Firmly and unhesitatingly he bore witness that the sum spent a month before could not have been less than three thousand, that all the peasants about here would testify that they had heard the sum of three thousand mentioned by Dmitri Fyodorovitch himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What a lot of money he flung away on the gypsy girls alone! He wasted a thousand, I daresay, on them alone.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t believe I gave them five hundred,” was Mitya’s gloomy comment on this.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s a pity I didn’t count the money at the time, but I was drunk....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya was sitting sideways with his back to the curtains.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He listened gloomily, with a melancholy and exhausted air, as though he would say:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, say what you like. It makes no difference now.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “More than a thousand went on them, Dmitri Fyodorovitch,” retorted Trifon Borissovitch firmly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You flung it about at random and they picked it up. They were a rascally, thievish lot, horse-stealers, they’ve been driven away from here, or maybe they’d bear witness themselves how much they got from you. I saw the sum in your hands, myself—count it I didn’t, you didn’t let me, that’s true enough—but by the look of it I should say it was far more than fifteen hundred ... fifteen hundred, indeed! We’ve seen money too. We can judge of amounts....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As for the sum spent yesterday he asserted that Dmitri Fyodorovitch had told him, as soon as he arrived, that he had brought three thousand with him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Come now, is that so, Trifon Borissovitch?” replied Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Surely I didn’t declare so positively that I’d brought three thousand?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You did say so, Dmitri Fyodorovitch. You said it before Andrey. Andrey himself is still here. Send for him. And in the hall, when you were treating the chorus, you shouted straight out that you would leave your sixth thousand here—that is with what you spent before, we must understand. Stepan and Semyon heard it, and Pyotr Fomitch Kalganov, too, was standing beside you at the time. Maybe he’d remember it....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The evidence as to the “sixth” thousand made an extraordinary impression on the two lawyers.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They were delighted with this new mode of reckoning; three and three made six, three thousand then and three now made six, that was clear.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They questioned all the peasants suggested by Trifon Borissovitch, Stepan and Semyon, the driver Andrey, and Kalganov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The peasants and the driver unhesitatingly confirmed Trifon Borissovitch’s evidence.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They noted down, with particular care, Andrey’s account of the conversation he had had with Mitya on the road: “‘Where,’ says he, ‘am I, Dmitri Fyodorovitch, going, to heaven or to hell, and shall I be forgiven in the next world or not?’”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The psychological Ippolit Kirillovitch heard this with a subtle smile, and ended by recommending that these remarks as to where Dmitri Fyodorovitch would go should be “included in the case.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kalganov, when called, came in reluctantly, frowning and ill-humored, and he spoke to the lawyers as though he had never met them before in his life, though they were acquaintances whom he had been meeting every day for a long time past.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He began by saying that “he knew nothing about it and didn’t want to. But it appeared that he had heard of the “sixth” thousand, and he admitted that he had been standing close by at the moment.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As far as he could see he “didn’t know” how much money Mitya had in his hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He affirmed that the Poles had cheated at cards.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In reply to reiterated questions he stated that, after the Poles had been turned out, Mitya’s position with Agrafena Alexandrovna had certainly improved, and that she had said that she loved him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He spoke of Agrafena Alexandrovna with reserve and respect, as though she had been a lady of the best society, and did not once allow himself to call her Grushenka.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In spite of the young man’s obvious repugnance at giving evidence, Ippolit Kirillovitch examined him at great length, and only from him learnt all the details of what made up Mitya’s “romance,” so to say, on that night.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya did not once pull Kalganov up.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At last they let the young man go, and he left the room with unconcealed indignation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The Poles, too, were examined.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though they had gone to bed in their room, they had not slept all night, and on the arrival of the police officers they hastily dressed and got ready, realizing that they would certainly be sent for.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They gave their evidence with dignity, though not without some uneasiness.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The little Pole turned out to be a retired official of the twelfth class, who had served in Siberia as a veterinary surgeon.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His name was Mussyalovitch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Pan Vrublevsky turned out to be an uncertificated dentist.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Although Nikolay Parfenovitch asked them questions on entering the room they both addressed their answers to Mihail Makarovitch, who was standing on one side, taking him in their ignorance for the most important person and in command, and addressed him at every word as “Pan Colonel. Only after several reproofs from Mihail Makarovitch himself, they grasped that they had to address their answers to Nikolay Parfenovitch only. It turned out that they could speak Russian quite correctly except for their accent in some words. Of his relations with Grushenka, past and present, Pan Mussyalovitch spoke proudly and warmly, so that Mitya was roused at once and declared that he would not allow the “scoundrel” to speak like that in his presence!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Pan Mussyalovitch at once called attention to the word “scoundrel” and begged that it should be put down in the protocol.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya fumed with rage.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’s a scoundrel! A scoundrel! You can put that down. And put down, too, that, in spite of the protocol I still declare that he’s a scoundrel!” he cried.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though Nikolay Parfenovitch did insert this in the protocol, he showed the most praiseworthy tact and management.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: After sternly reprimanding Mitya, he cut short all further inquiry into the romantic aspect of the case, and hastened to pass to what was essential.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: One piece of evidence given by the Poles roused special interest in the lawyers: that was how, in that very room, Mitya had tried to buy off Pan Mussyalovitch, and had offered him three thousand roubles to resign his claims, seven hundred roubles down, and the remaining two thousand three hundred “to be paid next day in the town.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had sworn at the time that he had not the whole sum with him at Mokroe, but that his money was in the town.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya observed hotly that he had not said that he would be sure to pay him the remainder next day in the town.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Pan Vrublevsky confirmed the statement, and Mitya, after thinking for a moment admitted, frowning, that it must have been as the Poles stated, that he had been excited at the time, and might indeed have said so.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The prosecutor positively pounced on this piece of evidence.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It seemed to establish for the prosecution (and they did, in fact, base this deduction on it) that half, or a part of, the three thousand that had come into Mitya’s hands might really have been left somewhere hidden in the town, or even, perhaps, somewhere here, in Mokroe.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This would explain the circumstance, so baffling for the prosecution, that only eight hundred roubles were to be found in Mitya’s hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This circumstance had been the one piece of evidence which, insignificant as it was, had hitherto told, to some extent, in Mitya’s favor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Now this one piece of evidence in his favor had broken down.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In answer to the prosecutor’s inquiry, where he would have got the remaining two thousand three hundred roubles, since he himself had denied having more than fifteen hundred, Mitya confidently replied that he had meant to offer the “little chap,” not money, but a formal deed of conveyance of his rights to the village of Tchermashnya, those rights which he had already offered to Samsonov and Madame Hohlakov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The prosecutor positively smiled at the “innocence of this subterfuge.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And you imagine he would have accepted such a deed as a substitute for two thousand three hundred roubles in cash?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He certainly would have accepted it,” Mitya declared warmly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, look here, he might have grabbed not two thousand, but four or six, for it. He would have put his lawyers, Poles and Jews, on to the job, and might have got, not three thousand, but the whole property out of the old man.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The evidence of Pan Mussyalovitch was, of course, entered in the protocol in the fullest detail.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Then they let the Poles go.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The incident of the cheating at cards was hardly touched upon.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch was too well pleased with them, as it was, and did not want to worry them with trifles, moreover, it was nothing but a foolish, drunken quarrel over cards.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There had been drinking and disorder enough, that night....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: So the two hundred roubles remained in the pockets of the Poles.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Then old Maximov was summoned.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He came in timidly, approached with little steps, looking very disheveled and depressed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had, all this time, taken refuge below with Grushenka, sitting dumbly beside her, and “now and then he’d begin blubbering over her and wiping his eyes with a blue check handkerchief,” as Mihail Makarovitch described afterwards.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: So that she herself began trying to pacify and comfort him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The old man at once confessed that he had done wrong, that he had borrowed “ten roubles in my poverty,” from Dmitri Fyodorovitch, and that he was ready to pay it back.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: To Nikolay Parfenovitch’s direct question, had he noticed how much money Dmitri Fyodorovitch held in his hand, as he must have been able to see the sum better than any one when he took the note from him, Maximov, in the most positive manner, declared that there was twenty thousand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Have you ever seen so much as twenty thousand before, then?” inquired Nikolay Parfenovitch, with a smile.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “To be sure I have, not twenty, but seven, when my wife mortgaged my little property. She’d only let me look at it from a distance, boasting of it to me. It was a very thick bundle, all rainbow-colored notes. And Dmitri Fyodorovitch’s were all rainbow-colored....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was not kept long.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At last it was Grushenka’s turn.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch was obviously apprehensive of the effect her appearance might have on Mitya, and he muttered a few words of admonition to him, but Mitya bowed his head in silence, giving him to understand “that he would not make a scene. Mihail Makarovitch himself led Grushenka in. She entered with a stern and gloomy face, that looked almost composed and sat down quietly on the chair offered her by Nikolay Parfenovitch. She was very pale, she seemed to be cold, and wrapped herself closely in her magnificent black shawl. She was suffering from a slight feverish chill—the first symptom of the long illness which followed that night. Her grave air, her direct earnest look and quiet manner made a very favorable impression on every one. Nikolay Parfenovitch was even a little bit “fascinated. He admitted himself, when talking about it afterwards, that only then had he seen “how handsome the woman was,” for, though he had seen her several times before, he had always looked upon her as something of a “provincial hetaira. “She has the manners of the best society,” he said enthusiastically, gossiping about her in a circle of ladies.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But this was received with positive indignation by the ladies, who immediately called him a “naughty man,” to his great satisfaction.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As she entered the room, Grushenka only glanced for an instant at Mitya, who looked at her uneasily.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But her face reassured him at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: After the first inevitable inquiries and warnings, Nikolay Parfenovitch asked her, hesitating a little, but preserving the most courteous manner, on what terms she was with the retired lieutenant, Dmitri Fyodorovitch Karamazov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: To this Grushenka firmly and quietly replied:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He was an acquaintance. He came to see me as an acquaintance during the last month. To further inquisitive questions she answered plainly and with complete frankness, that, though “at times” she had thought him attractive, she had not loved him, but had won his heart as well as his old father’s “in my nasty spite,” that she had seen that Mitya was very jealous of Fyodor Pavlovitch and every one else; but that had only amused her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She had never meant to go to Fyodor Pavlovitch, she had simply been laughing at him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I had no thoughts for either of them all this last month. I was expecting another man who had wronged me. But I think,” she said in conclusion, “that there’s no need for you to inquire about that, nor for me to answer you, for that’s my own affair.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch immediately acted upon this hint.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He again dismissed the “romantic” aspect of the case and passed to the serious one, that is, to the question of most importance, concerning the three thousand roubles.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka confirmed the statement that three thousand roubles had certainly been spent on the first carousal at Mokroe, and, though she had not counted the money herself, she had heard that it was three thousand from Dmitri Fyodorovitch’s own lips.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Did he tell you that alone, or before some one else, or did you only hear him speak of it to others in your presence?” the prosecutor inquired immediately.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: To which Grushenka replied that she had heard him say so before other people, and had heard him say so when they were alone.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Did he say it to you alone once, or several times?” inquired the prosecutor, and learned that he had told Grushenka so several times.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ippolit Kirillovitch was very well satisfied with this piece of evidence.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Further examination elicited that Grushenka knew, too, where that money had come from, and that Dmitri Fyodorovitch had got it from Katerina Ivanovna.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And did you never, once, hear that the money spent a month ago was not three thousand, but less, and that Dmitri Fyodorovitch had saved half that sum for his own use?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, I never heard that,” answered Grushenka.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was explained further that Mitya had, on the contrary, often told her that he hadn’t a farthing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He was always expecting to get some from his father,” said Grushenka in conclusion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Did he never say before you ... casually, or in a moment of irritation,” Nikolay Parfenovitch put in suddenly, “that he intended to make an attempt on his father’s life?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ach, he did say so,” sighed Grushenka.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Once or several times?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He mentioned it several times, always in anger.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And did you believe he would do it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, I never believed it,” she answered firmly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I had faith in his noble heart.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Gentlemen, allow me,” cried Mitya suddenly, “allow me to say one word to Agrafena Alexandrovna, in your presence.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You can speak,” Nikolay Parfenovitch assented.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Agrafena Alexandrovna! Mitya got up from his chair, “have faith in God and in me. I am not guilty of my father’s murder!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Having uttered these words Mitya sat down again on his chair.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka stood up and crossed herself devoutly before the ikon.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Thanks be to Thee, O Lord,” she said, in a voice thrilled with emotion, and still standing, she turned to Nikolay Parfenovitch and added:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “As he has spoken now, believe it! I know him. He’ll say anything as a joke or from obstinacy, but he’ll never deceive you against his conscience. He’s telling the whole truth, you may believe it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Thanks, Agrafena Alexandrovna, you’ve given me fresh courage,” Mitya responded in a quivering voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As to the money spent the previous day, she declared that she did not know what sum it was, but had heard him tell several people that he had three thousand with him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And to the question where he got the money, she said that he had told her that he had “stolen” it from Katerina Ivanovna, and that she had replied to that that he hadn’t stolen it, and that he must pay the money back next day.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: On the prosecutor’s asking her emphatically whether the money he said he had stolen from Katerina Ivanovna was what he had spent yesterday, or what he had squandered here a month ago, she declared that he meant the money spent a month ago, and that that was how she understood him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka was at last released, and Nikolay Parfenovitch informed her impulsively that she might at once return to the town and that if he could be of any assistance to her, with horses for example, or if she would care for an escort, he ... would be—

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I thank you sincerely,” said Grushenka, bowing to him, “I’m going with this old gentleman, I am driving him back to town with me, and meanwhile, if you’ll allow me, I’ll wait below to hear what you decide about Dmitri Fyodorovitch.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She went out.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya was calm, and even looked more cheerful, but only for a moment.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He felt more and more oppressed by a strange physical weakness.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His eyes were closing with fatigue.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The examination of the witnesses was, at last, over.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They proceeded to a final revision of the protocol.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya got up, moved from his chair to the corner by the curtain, lay down on a large chest covered with a rug, and instantly fell asleep.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had a strange dream, utterly out of keeping with the place and the time.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was driving somewhere in the steppes, where he had been stationed long ago, and a peasant was driving him in a cart with a pair of horses, through snow and sleet.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was cold, it was early in November, and the snow was falling in big wet flakes, melting as soon as it touched the earth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And the peasant drove him smartly, he had a fair, long beard.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was not an old man, somewhere about fifty, and he had on a gray peasant’s smock.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Not far off was a village, he could see the black huts, and half the huts were burnt down, there were only the charred beams sticking up.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And as they drove in, there were peasant women drawn up along the road, a lot of women, a whole row, all thin and wan, with their faces a sort of brownish color, especially one at the edge, a tall, bony woman, who looked forty, but might have been only twenty, with a long thin face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And in her arms was a little baby crying.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And her breasts seemed so dried up that there was not a drop of milk in them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And the child cried and cried, and held out its little bare arms, with its little fists blue from cold.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why are they crying?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why are they crying?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya asked, as they dashed gayly by.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s the babe,” answered the driver, “the babe weeping.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And Mitya was struck by his saying, in his peasant way, “the babe,” and he liked the peasant’s calling it a “babe.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There seemed more pity in it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But why is it weeping? Mitya persisted stupidly, “why are its little arms bare? Why don’t they wrap it up?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The babe’s cold, its little clothes are frozen and don’t warm it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But why is it? Why?” foolish Mitya still persisted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, they’re poor people, burnt out. They’ve no bread. They’re begging because they’ve been burnt out.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, no,” Mitya, as it were, still did not understand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Tell me why it is those poor mothers stand there? Why are people poor? Why is the babe poor? Why is the steppe barren? Why don’t they hug each other and kiss? Why don’t they sing songs of joy? Why are they so dark from black misery? Why don’t they feed the babe?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And he felt that, though his questions were unreasonable and senseless, yet he wanted to ask just that, and he had to ask it just in that way.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And he felt that a passion of pity, such as he had never known before, was rising in his heart, that he wanted to cry, that he wanted to do something for them all, so that the babe should weep no more, so that the dark-faced, dried-up mother should not weep, that no one should shed tears again from that moment, and he wanted to do it at once, at once, regardless of all obstacles, with all the recklessness of the Karamazovs.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And I’m coming with you. I won’t leave you now for the rest of my life, I’m coming with you,” he heard close beside him Grushenka’s tender voice, thrilling with emotion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And his heart glowed, and he struggled forward towards the light, and he longed to live, to live, to go on and on, towards the new, beckoning light, and to hasten, hasten, now, at once!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What! Where?” he exclaimed opening his eyes, and sitting up on the chest, as though he had revived from a swoon, smiling brightly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch was standing over him, suggesting that he should hear the protocol read aloud and sign it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya guessed that he had been asleep an hour or more, but he did not hear Nikolay Parfenovitch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was suddenly struck by the fact that there was a pillow under his head, which hadn’t been there when he had leant back, exhausted, on the chest.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Who put that pillow under my head? Who was so kind?” he cried, with a sort of ecstatic gratitude, and tears in his voice, as though some great kindness had been shown him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He never found out who this kind man was; perhaps one of the peasant witnesses, or Nikolay Parfenovitch’s little secretary, had compassionately thought to put a pillow under his head; but his whole soul was quivering with tears.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He went to the table and said that he would sign whatever they liked.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve had a good dream, gentlemen,” he said in a strange voice, with a new light, as of joy, in his face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: When the protocol had been signed, Nikolay Parfenovitch turned solemnly to the prisoner and read him the “Committal,” setting forth, that in such a year, on such a day, in such a place, the investigating lawyer of such-and-such a district court, having examined so-and-so (to wit, Mitya) accused of this and of that (all the charges were carefully written out) and having considered that the accused, not pleading guilty to the charges made against him, had brought forward nothing in his defense, while the witnesses, so-and-so, and so-and-so, and the circumstances such-and-such testify against him, acting in accordance with such-and-such articles of the Statute Book, and so on, has ruled, that, in order to preclude so-and-so (Mitya) from all means of evading pursuit and judgment he be detained in such-and-such a prison, which he hereby notifies to the accused and communicates a copy of this same “Committal” to the deputy prosecutor, and so on, and so on.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

text: Krassotkin could, of course, have provided more diverting entertainment for them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He could have made them stand side by side and played soldiers with them, or sent them hiding all over the house.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had done so more than once before and was not above doing it, so much so that a report once spread at school that Krassotkin played horses with the little lodgers at home, prancing with his head on one side like a trace-horse.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Krassotkin haughtily parried this thrust, pointing out that to play horses with boys of one’s own age, boys of thirteen, would certainly be disgraceful “at this date,” but that he did it for the sake of “the kids” because he liked them, and no one had a right to call him to account for his feelings.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The two “kids” adored him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But on this occasion he was in no mood for games.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had very important business of his own before him, something almost mysterious.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Meanwhile time was passing and Agafya, with whom he could have left the children, would not come back from market.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had several times already crossed the passage, opened the door of the lodgers’ room and looked anxiously at “the kids” who were sitting over the book, as he had bidden them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Every time he opened the door they grinned at him, hoping he would come in and would do something delightful and amusing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Kolya was bothered and did not go in.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At last it struck eleven and he made up his mind, once for all, that if that “damned” Agafya did not come back within ten minutes he should go out without waiting for her, making “the kids” promise, of course, to be brave when he was away, not to be naughty, not to cry from fright.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: With this idea he put on his wadded winter overcoat with its catskin fur collar, slung his satchel round his shoulder, and, regardless of his mother’s constantly reiterated entreaties that he would always put on goloshes in such cold weather, he looked at them contemptuously as he crossed the hall and went out with only his boots on.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Perezvon, seeing him in his outdoor clothes, began tapping nervously, yet vigorously, on the floor with his tail.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Twitching all over, he even uttered a plaintive whine.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Kolya, seeing his dog’s passionate excitement, decided that it was a breach of discipline, kept him for another minute under the bench, and only when he had opened the door into the passage, whistled for him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The dog leapt up like a mad creature and rushed bounding before him rapturously.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya opened the door to peep at “the kids. They were both sitting as before at the table, not reading but warmly disputing about something. The children often argued together about various exciting problems of life, and Nastya, being the elder, always got the best of it. If Kostya did not agree with her, he almost always appealed to Kolya Krassotkin, and his verdict was regarded as infallible by both of them. This time the “kids’” discussion rather interested Krassotkin, and he stood still in the passage to listen.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The children saw he was listening and that made them dispute with even greater energy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I shall never, never believe,” Nastya prattled, “that the old women find babies among the cabbages in the kitchen-garden. It’s winter now and there are no cabbages, and so the old woman couldn’t have taken Katerina a daughter.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya whistled to himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Or perhaps they do bring babies from somewhere, but only to those who are married.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kostya stared at Nastya and listened, pondering profoundly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nastya, how silly you are!” he said at last, firmly and calmly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How can Katerina have a baby when she isn’t married?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nastya was exasperated.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You know nothing about it,” she snapped irritably.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Perhaps she has a husband, only he is in prison, so now she’s got a baby.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But is her husband in prison?” the matter-of-fact Kostya inquired gravely.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Or, I tell you what,” Nastya interrupted impulsively, completely rejecting and forgetting her first hypothesis.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “She hasn’t a husband, you are right there, but she wants to be married, and so she’s been thinking of getting married, and thinking and thinking of it till now she’s got it, that is, not a husband but a baby.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, perhaps so,” Kostya agreed, entirely vanquished.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But you didn’t say so before. So how could I tell?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Come, kiddies,” said Kolya, stepping into the room.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’re terrible people, I see.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And Perezvon with you!” grinned Kostya, and began snapping his fingers and calling Perezvon.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I am in a difficulty, kids,” Krassotkin began solemnly, “and you must help me. Agafya must have broken her leg, since she has not turned up till now, that’s certain. I must go out. Will you let me go?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The children looked anxiously at one another.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Their smiling faces showed signs of uneasiness, but they did not yet fully grasp what was expected of them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You won’t be naughty while I am gone? You won’t climb on the cupboard and break your legs? You won’t be frightened alone and cry?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A look of profound despondency came into the children’s faces.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And I could show you something as a reward, a little copper cannon which can be fired with real gunpowder.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The children’s faces instantly brightened.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Show us the cannon,” said Kostya, beaming all over.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Krassotkin put his hand in his satchel, and pulling out a little bronze cannon stood it on the table.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah, you are bound to ask that! Look, it’s on wheels. He rolled the toy on along the table. “And it can be fired off, too. It can be loaded with shot and fired off.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And it could kill any one?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It can kill any one; you’ve only got to aim at anybody,” and Krassotkin explained where the powder had to be put, where the shot should be rolled in, showing a tiny hole like a touch-hole, and told them that it kicked when it was fired.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The children listened with intense interest.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What particularly struck their imagination was that the cannon kicked.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And have you got any powder?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nastya inquired.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Show us the powder, too,” she drawled with a smile of entreaty.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Krassotkin dived again into his satchel and pulled out a small flask containing a little real gunpowder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had some shot, too, in a screw of paper.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He even uncorked the flask and shook a little powder into the palm of his hand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “One has to be careful there’s no fire about, or it would blow up and kill us all,” Krassotkin warned them sensationally.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The children gazed at the powder with an awe-stricken alarm that only intensified their enjoyment.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Kostya liked the shot better.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And does the shot burn?” he inquired.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, it doesn’t.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Give me a little shot,” he asked in an imploring voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ll give you a little shot; here, take it, but don’t show it to your mother till I come back, or she’ll be sure to think it’s gunpowder, and will die of fright and give you a thrashing.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mother never does whip us,” Nastya observed at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I know, I only said it to finish the sentence. And don’t you ever deceive your mother except just this once, until I come back. And so, kiddies, can I go out? You won’t be frightened and cry when I’m gone?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We sha—all cry,” drawled Kostya, on the verge of tears already.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We shall cry, we shall be sure to cry,” Nastya chimed in with timid haste.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, children, children, how fraught with peril are your years! There’s no help for it, chickens, I shall have to stay with you I don’t know how long. And time is passing, time is passing, oogh!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Tell Perezvon to pretend to be dead!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kostya begged.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There’s no help for it, we must have recourse to Perezvon.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ici, Perezvon.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And Kolya began giving orders to the dog, who performed all his tricks.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was a rough-haired dog, of medium size, with a coat of a sort of lilac-gray color.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was blind in his right eye, and his left ear was torn.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He whined and jumped, stood and walked on his hind legs, lay on his back with his paws in the air, rigid as though he were dead.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: While this last performance was going on, the door opened and Agafya, Madame Krassotkin’s servant, a stout woman of forty, marked with small-pox, appeared in the doorway.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She had come back from market and had a bag full of provisions in her hand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Holding up the bag of provisions in her left hand she stood still to watch the dog.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though Kolya had been so anxious for her return, he did not cut short the performance, and after keeping Perezvon dead for the usual time, at last he whistled to him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The dog jumped up and began bounding about in his joy at having done his duty.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Only think, a dog!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Agafya observed sententiously.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why are you late, female?” asked Krassotkin sternly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Female, indeed! Go on with you, you brat.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Brat?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, a brat. What is it to you if I’m late; if I’m late, you may be sure I have good reason,” muttered Agafya, busying herself about the stove, without a trace of anger or displeasure in her voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She seemed quite pleased, in fact, to enjoy a skirmish with her merry young master.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Listen, you frivolous young woman,” Krassotkin began, getting up from the sofa, “can you swear by all you hold sacred in the world and something else besides, that you will watch vigilantly over the kids in my absence? I am going out.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And what am I going to swear for?” laughed Agafya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I shall look after them without that.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, you must swear on your eternal salvation. Else I shan’t go.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, don’t then. What does it matter to me? It’s cold out; stay at home.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Kids,” Kolya turned to the children, “this woman will stay with you till I come back or till your mother comes, for she ought to have been back long ago. She will give you some lunch, too. You’ll give them something, Agafya, won’t you?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That I can do.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Good-by, chickens, I go with my heart at rest. And you, granny,” he added gravely, in an undertone, as he passed Agafya, “I hope you’ll spare their tender years and not tell them any of your old woman’s nonsense about Katerina. Ici, Perezvon!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Get along with you!” retorted Agafya, really angry this time.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ridiculous boy! You want a whipping for saying such things, that’s what you want!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Kolya did not hear her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At last he could go out.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As he went out at the gate he looked round him, shrugged up his shoulders, and saying “It is freezing,” went straight along the street and turned off to the right towards the market-place.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: When he reached the last house but one before the market-place he stopped at the gate, pulled a whistle out of his pocket, and whistled with all his might as though giving a signal.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had not to wait more than a minute before a rosy-cheeked boy of about eleven, wearing a warm, neat and even stylish coat, darted out to meet him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This was Smurov, a boy in the preparatory class (two classes below Kolya Krassotkin), son of a well-to-do official.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Apparently he was forbidden by his parents to associate with Krassotkin, who was well known to be a desperately naughty boy, so Smurov was obviously slipping out on the sly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was—if the reader has not forgotten—one of the group of boys who two months before had thrown stones at Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was the one who told Alyosha Karamazov about Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve been waiting for you for the last hour, Krassotkin,” said Smurov stolidly, and the boys strode towards the market-place.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I am late,” answered Krassotkin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I was detained by circumstances. You won’t be thrashed for coming with me?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Come, I say, I’m never thrashed! And you’ve got Perezvon with you?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’re taking him, too?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah! if it were only Zhutchka!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s impossible. Zhutchka’s non-existent. Zhutchka is lost in the mists of obscurity.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah! couldn’t we do this? Smurov suddenly stood still. “You see Ilusha says that Zhutchka was a shaggy, grayish, smoky-looking dog like Perezvon. Couldn’t you tell him this is Zhutchka, and he might believe you?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Boy, shun a lie, that’s one thing; even with a good object—that’s another. Above all, I hope you’ve not told them anything about my coming.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Heaven forbid! I know what I am about. But you won’t comfort him with Perezvon,” said Smurov, with a sigh.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You know his father, the captain, ‘the wisp of tow,’ told us that he was going to bring him a real mastiff pup, with a black nose, to-day. He thinks that would comfort Ilusha; but I doubt it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And how is Ilusha?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah, he is bad, very bad! I believe he’s in consumption: he is quite conscious, but his breathing! His breathing’s gone wrong. The other day he asked to have his boots on to be led round the room. He tried to walk, but he couldn’t stand. ‘Ah, I told you before, father,’ he said, ‘that those boots were no good. I could never walk properly in them. He fancied it was his boots that made him stagger, but it was simply weakness, really. He won’t live another week. Herzenstube is looking after him. Now they are rich again—they’ve got heaps of money.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “They are rogues.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Who are rogues?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Doctors and the whole crew of quacks collectively, and also, of course, individually. I don’t believe in medicine. It’s a useless institution. I mean to go into all that. But what’s that sentimentality you’ve got up there? The whole class seems to be there every day.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not the whole class: it’s only ten of our fellows who go to see him every day. There’s nothing in that.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What I don’t understand in all this is the part that Alexey Karamazov is taking in it. His brother’s going to be tried to-morrow or next day for such a crime, and yet he has so much time to spend on sentimentality with boys.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There’s no sentimentality about it. You are going yourself now to make it up with Ilusha.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Make it up with him? What an absurd expression! But I allow no one to analyze my actions.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And how pleased Ilusha will be to see you!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He has no idea that you are coming.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why was it, why was it you wouldn’t come all this time?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Smurov cried with sudden warmth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “My dear boy, that’s my business, not yours. I am going of myself because I choose to, but you’ve all been hauled there by Alexey Karamazov—there’s a difference, you know. And how do you know? I may not be going to make it up at all. It’s a stupid expression.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s not Karamazov at all; it’s not his doing. Our fellows began going there of themselves. Of course, they went with Karamazov at first. And there’s been nothing of that sort—no silliness. First one went, and then another. His father was awfully pleased to see us. You know he will simply go out of his mind if Ilusha dies. He sees that Ilusha’s dying. And he seems so glad we’ve made it up with Ilusha. Ilusha asked after you, that was all. He just asks and says no more. His father will go out of his mind or hang himself. He behaved like a madman before. You know he is a very decent man. We made a mistake then. It’s all the fault of that murderer who beat him then.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Karamazov’s a riddle to me all the same. I might have made his acquaintance long ago, but I like to have a proper pride in some cases. Besides, I have a theory about him which I must work out and verify.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya subsided into dignified silence.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Smurov, too, was silent.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Smurov, of course, worshiped Krassotkin and never dreamed of putting himself on a level with him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Now he was tremendously interested at Kolya’s saying that he was “going of himself” to see Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He felt that there must be some mystery in Kolya’s suddenly taking it into his head to go to him that day.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They crossed the market-place, in which at that hour were many loaded wagons from the country and a great number of live fowls.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The market women were selling rolls, cottons and threads, etc., in their booths.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: These Sunday markets were naïvely called “fairs” in the town, and there were many such fairs in the year.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Perezvon ran about in the wildest spirits, sniffing about first one side, then the other.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: When he met other dogs they zealously smelt each other over according to the rules of canine etiquette.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I like to watch such realistic scenes, Smurov,” said Kolya suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Have you noticed how dogs sniff at one another when they meet? It seems to be a law of their nature.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes; it’s a funny habit.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, it’s not funny; you are wrong there. There’s nothing funny in nature, however funny it may seem to man with his prejudices. If dogs could reason and criticize us they’d be sure to find just as much that would be funny to them, if not far more, in the social relations of men, their masters—far more, indeed. I repeat that, because I am convinced that there is far more foolishness among us. That’s Rakitin’s idea—a remarkable idea. I am a Socialist, Smurov.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And what is a Socialist?” asked Smurov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s when all are equal and all have property in common, there are no marriages, and every one has any religion and laws he likes best, and all the rest of it. You are not old enough to understand that yet. It’s cold, though.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, twelve degrees of frost. Father looked at the thermometer just now.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Have you noticed, Smurov, that in the middle of winter we don’t feel so cold even when there are fifteen or eighteen degrees of frost as we do now, in the beginning of winter, when there is a sudden frost of twelve degrees, especially when there is not much snow. It’s because people are not used to it. Everything is habit with men, everything even in their social and political relations. Habit is the great motive-power. What a funny-looking peasant!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya pointed to a tall peasant, with a good-natured countenance in a long sheepskin coat, who was standing by his wagon, clapping together his hands, in their shapeless leather gloves, to warm them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His long fair beard was all white with frost.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That peasant’s beard’s frozen,” Kolya cried in a loud provocative voice as he passed him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Lots of people’s beards are frozen,” the peasant replied, calmly and sententiously.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t provoke him,” observed Smurov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s all right; he won’t be cross; he’s a nice fellow. Good-by, Matvey.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Good-by.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Is your name Matvey?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes. Didn’t you know?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, I didn’t. It was a guess.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You don’t say so! You are a schoolboy, I suppose?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You get whipped, I expect?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nothing to speak of—sometimes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Does it hurt?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, yes, it does.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ech, what a life!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The peasant heaved a sigh from the bottom of his heart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Good-by, Matvey.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Good-by. You are a nice chap, that you are.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boys went on.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That was a nice peasant,” Kolya observed to Smurov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I like talking to the peasants, and am always glad to do them justice.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why did you tell a lie, pretending we are thrashed?” asked Smurov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I had to say that to please him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How do you mean?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You know, Smurov, I don’t like being asked the same thing twice. I like people to understand at the first word. Some things can’t be explained. According to a peasant’s notions, schoolboys are whipped, and must be whipped. What would a schoolboy be if he were not whipped? And if I were to tell him we are not, he’d be disappointed. But you don’t understand that. One has to know how to talk to the peasants.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Only don’t tease them, please, or you’ll get into another scrape as you did about that goose.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So you’re afraid?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t laugh, Kolya. Of course I’m afraid. My father would be awfully cross. I am strictly forbidden to go out with you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t be uneasy, nothing will happen this time. Hallo, Natasha!” he shouted to a market woman in one of the booths.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Call me Natasha! What next! My name is Marya,” the middle-aged market woman shouted at him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I am so glad it’s Marya. Good-by!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah, you young rascal! A brat like you to carry on so!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’m in a hurry.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I can’t stay now.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: You shall tell me next Sunday.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya waved his hand at her, as though she had attacked him and not he her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve nothing to tell you next Sunday. You set upon me, you impudent young monkey. I didn’t say anything,” bawled Marya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You want a whipping, that’s what you want, you saucy jackanapes!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was a roar of laughter among the other market women round her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Suddenly a man in a violent rage darted out from the arcade of shops close by.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was a young man, not a native of the town, with dark, curly hair and a long, pale face, marked with smallpox.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He wore a long blue coat and a peaked cap, and looked like a merchant’s clerk.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was in a state of stupid excitement and brandished his fist at Kolya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I know you!” he cried angrily, “I know you!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya stared at him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He could not recall when he could have had a row with the man.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But he had been in so many rows in the street that he could hardly remember them all.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do you?” he asked sarcastically.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I know you! I know you!” the man repeated idiotically.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So much the better for you. Well, it’s time I was going. Good-by!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are at your saucy pranks again?” cried the man.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are at your saucy pranks again? I know, you are at it again!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s not your business, brother, if I am at my saucy pranks again,” said Kolya, standing still and scanning him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not my business?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov
