title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I know you would all like it to be Zhutchka. I’ve heard all about it. Kolya smiled mysteriously. “Listen, Karamazov, I’ll tell you all about it. That’s what I came for; that’s what I asked you to come out here for, to explain the whole episode to you before we go in,” he began with animation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You see, Karamazov, Ilusha came into the preparatory class last spring. Well, you know what our preparatory class is—a lot of small boys. They began teasing Ilusha at once. I am two classes higher up, and, of course, I only look on at them from a distance. I saw the boy was weak and small, but he wouldn’t give in to them; he fought with them. I saw he was proud, and his eyes were full of fire. I like children like that. And they teased him all the more. The worst of it was he was horribly dressed at the time, his breeches were too small for him, and there were holes in his boots. They worried him about it; they jeered at him. That I can’t stand. I stood up for him at once, and gave it to them hot. I beat them, but they adore me, do you know, Karamazov? Kolya boasted impulsively; “but I am always fond of children. I’ve two chickens in my hands at home now—that’s what detained me to-day. So they left off beating Ilusha and I took him under my protection. I saw the boy was proud. I tell you that, the boy was proud; but in the end he became slavishly devoted to me: he did my slightest bidding, obeyed me as though I were God, tried to copy me. In the intervals between the classes he used to run to me at once, and I’d go about with him. On Sundays, too. They always laugh when an older boy makes friends with a younger one like that; but that’s a prejudice. If it’s my fancy, that’s enough. I am teaching him, developing him. Why shouldn’t I develop him if I like him? Here you, Karamazov, have taken up with all these nestlings. I see you want to influence the younger generation—to develop them, to be of use to them, and I assure you this trait in your character, which I knew by hearsay, attracted me more than anything. Let us get to the point, though. I noticed that there was a sort of softness and sentimentality coming over the boy, and you know I have a positive hatred of this sheepish sentimentality, and I have had it from a baby. There were contradictions in him, too: he was proud, but he was slavishly devoted to me, and yet all at once his eyes would flash and he’d refuse to agree with me; he’d argue, fly into a rage. I used sometimes to propound certain ideas; I could see that it was not so much that he disagreed with the ideas, but that he was simply rebelling against me, because I was cool in responding to his endearments. And so, in order to train him properly, the tenderer he was, the colder I became. I did it on purpose: that was my idea. My object was to form his character, to lick him into shape, to make a man of him ... and besides ... no doubt, you understand me at a word. Suddenly I noticed for three days in succession he was downcast and dejected, not because of my coldness, but for something else, something more important. I wondered what the tragedy was. I have pumped him and found out that he had somehow got to know Smerdyakov, who was footman to your late father—it was before his death, of course—and he taught the little fool a silly trick—that is, a brutal, nasty trick. He told him to take a piece of bread, to stick a pin in it, and throw it to one of those hungry dogs who snap up anything without biting it, and then to watch and see what would happen. So they prepared a piece of bread like that and threw it to Zhutchka, that shaggy dog there’s been such a fuss about. The people of the house it belonged to never fed it at all, though it barked all day. (Do you like that stupid barking, Karamazov? I can’t stand it.) So it rushed at the bread, swallowed it, and began to squeal; it turned round and round and ran away, squealing as it ran out of sight. That was Ilusha’s own account of it. He confessed it to me, and cried bitterly. He hugged me, shaking all over. He kept on repeating ‘He ran away squealing’: the sight of that haunted him. He was tormented by remorse, I could see that. I took it seriously. I determined to give him a lesson for other things as well. So I must confess I wasn’t quite straightforward, and pretended to be more indignant perhaps than I was. ‘You’ve done a nasty thing,’ I said, ‘you are a scoundrel. I won’t tell of it, of course, but I shall have nothing more to do with you for a time. I’ll think it over and let you know through Smurov’—that’s the boy who’s just come with me; he’s always ready to do anything for me—‘whether I will have anything to do with you in the future or whether I give you up for good as a scoundrel. He was tremendously upset. I must own I felt I’d gone too far as I spoke, but there was no help for it. I did what I thought best at the time. A day or two after, I sent Smurov to tell him that I would not speak to him again. That’s what we call it when two schoolfellows refuse to have anything more to do with one another. Secretly I only meant to send him to Coventry for a few days and then, if I saw signs of repentance, to hold out my hand to him again. That was my intention. But what do you think happened? He heard Smurov’s message, his eyes flashed. ‘Tell Krassotkin from me,’ he cried, ‘that I will throw bread with pins to all the dogs—all—all of them! ‘So he’s going in for a little temper. We must smoke it out of him. And I began to treat him with contempt; whenever I met him I turned away or smiled sarcastically. And just then that affair with his father happened. You remember? You must realize that he was fearfully worked up by what had happened already. The boys, seeing I’d given him up, set on him and taunted him, shouting, ‘Wisp of tow, wisp of tow! And he had soon regular skirmishes with them, which I am very sorry for. They seem to have given him one very bad beating. One day he flew at them all as they were coming out of school. I stood a few yards off, looking on. And, I swear, I don’t remember that I laughed; it was quite the other way, I felt awfully sorry for him, in another minute I would have run up to take his part. But he suddenly met my eyes. I don’t know what he fancied; but he pulled out a penknife, rushed at me, and struck at my thigh, here in my right leg. I didn’t move. I don’t mind owning I am plucky sometimes, Karamazov. I simply looked at him contemptuously, as though to say, ‘This is how you repay all my kindness! Do it again, if you like, I’m at your service. But he didn’t stab me again; he broke down, he was frightened at what he had done, he threw away the knife, burst out crying, and ran away. I did not sneak on him, of course, and I made them all keep quiet, so it shouldn’t come to the ears of the masters. I didn’t even tell my mother till it had healed up. And the wound was a mere scratch. And then I heard that the same day he’d been throwing stones and had bitten your finger—but you understand now what a state he was in! Well, it can’t be helped: it was stupid of me not to come and forgive him—that is, to make it up with him—when he was taken ill. I am sorry for it now. But I had a special reason. So now I’ve told you all about it ... but I’m afraid it was stupid of me.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, what a pity,” exclaimed Alyosha, with feeling, “that I didn’t know before what terms you were on with him, or I’d have come to you long ago to beg you to go to him with me. Would you believe it, when he was feverish he talked about you in delirium. I didn’t know how much you were to him! And you’ve really not succeeded in finding that dog? His father and the boys have been hunting all over the town for it. Would you believe it, since he’s been ill, I’ve three times heard him repeat with tears, ‘It’s because I killed Zhutchka, father, that I am ill now. God is punishing me for it. He can’t get that idea out of his head. And if the dog were found and proved to be alive, one might almost fancy the joy would cure him. We have all rested our hopes on you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Tell me, what made you hope that I should be the one to find him? Kolya asked, with great curiosity. “Why did you reckon on me rather than any one else?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There was a report that you were looking for the dog, and that you would bring it when you’d found it. Smurov said something of the sort. We’ve all been trying to persuade Ilusha that the dog is alive, that it’s been seen. The boys brought him a live hare; he just looked at it, with a faint smile, and asked them to set it free in the fields. And so we did. His father has just this moment come back, bringing him a mastiff pup, hoping to comfort him with that; but I think it only makes it worse.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Tell me, Karamazov, what sort of man is the father? I know him, but what do you make of him—a mountebank, a buffoon?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, no; there are people of deep feeling who have been somehow crushed. Buffoonery in them is a form of resentful irony against those to whom they daren’t speak the truth, from having been for years humiliated and intimidated by them. Believe me, Krassotkin, that sort of buffoonery is sometimes tragic in the extreme. His whole life now is centered in Ilusha, and if Ilusha dies, he will either go mad with grief or kill himself. I feel almost certain of that when I look at him now.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I understand you, Karamazov. I see you understand human nature,” Kolya added, with feeling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And as soon as I saw you with a dog, I thought it was Zhutchka you were bringing.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Wait a bit, Karamazov, perhaps we shall find it yet; but this is Perezvon. I’ll let him go in now and perhaps it will amuse Ilusha more than the mastiff pup. Wait a bit, Karamazov, you will know something in a minute. But, I say, I am keeping you here! Kolya cried suddenly. “You’ve no overcoat on in this bitter cold. You see what an egoist I am. Oh, we are all egoists, Karamazov!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t trouble; it is cold, but I don’t often catch cold. Let us go in, though, and, by the way, what is your name? I know you are called Kolya, but what else?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nikolay—Nikolay Ivanovitch Krassotkin, or, as they say in official documents, ‘Krassotkin son. Kolya laughed for some reason, but added suddenly, “Of course I hate my name Nikolay.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why so?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s so trivial, so ordinary.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are thirteen?” asked Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, fourteen—that is, I shall be fourteen very soon, in a fortnight. I’ll confess one weakness of mine, Karamazov, just to you, since it’s our first meeting, so that you may understand my character at once. I hate being asked my age, more than that ... and in fact ... there’s a libelous story going about me, that last week I played robbers with the preparatory boys. It’s a fact that I did play with them, but it’s a perfect libel to say I did it for my own amusement. I have reasons for believing that you’ve heard the story; but I wasn’t playing for my own amusement, it was for the sake of the children, because they couldn’t think of anything to do by themselves. But they’ve always got some silly tale. This is an awful town for gossip, I can tell you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But what if you had been playing for your own amusement, what’s the harm?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Come, I say, for my own amusement! You don’t play horses, do you?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But you must look at it like this,” said Alyosha, smiling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Grown-up people go to the theater and there the adventures of all sorts of heroes are represented—sometimes there are robbers and battles, too—and isn’t that just the same thing, in a different form, of course? And young people’s games of soldiers or robbers in their playtime are also art in its first stage. You know, they spring from the growing artistic instincts of the young. And sometimes these games are much better than performances in the theater, the only difference is that people go there to look at the actors, while in these games the young people are the actors themselves. But that’s only natural.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You think so? Is that your idea? Kolya looked at him intently. “Oh, you know, that’s rather an interesting view. When I go home, I’ll think it over. text: But when Smurov hinted to Krassotkin that Alyosha wanted to come and see him about something, the latter cut him short, bidding Smurov tell “Karamazov” at once that he knew best what to do, that he wanted no one’s advice, and that, if he went to see Ilusha, he would choose his own time for he had “his own reasons.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That was a fortnight before this Sunday.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That was why Alyosha had not been to see him, as he had meant to.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But though he waited, he sent Smurov to him twice again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Both times Krassotkin met him with a curt, impatient refusal, sending Alyosha a message not to bother him any more, that if he came himself, he, Krassotkin, would not go to Ilusha at all.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Up to the very last day, Smurov did not know that Kolya meant to go to Ilusha that morning, and only the evening before, as he parted from Smurov, Kolya abruptly told him to wait at home for him next morning, for he would go with him to the Snegiryovs’, but warned him on no account to say he was coming, as he wanted to drop in casually.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Smurov obeyed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Smurov’s fancy that Kolya would bring back the lost dog was based on the words Kolya had dropped that “they must be asses not to find the dog, if it was alive. When Smurov, waiting for an opportunity, timidly hinted at his guess about the dog, Krassotkin flew into a violent rage. “I’m not such an ass as to go hunting about the town for other people’s dogs when I’ve got a dog of my own! And how can you imagine a dog could be alive after swallowing a pin? Sheepish sentimentality, that’s what it is!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For the last fortnight Ilusha had not left his little bed under the ikons in the corner.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had not been to school since the day he met Alyosha and bit his finger.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was taken ill the same day, though for a month afterwards he was sometimes able to get up and walk about the room and passage.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But latterly he had become so weak that he could not move without help from his father.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His father was terribly concerned about him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He even gave up drinking and was almost crazy with terror that his boy would die.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And often, especially after leading him round the room on his arm and putting him back to bed, he would run to a dark corner in the passage and, leaning his head against the wall, he would break into paroxysms of violent weeping, stifling his sobs that they might not be heard by Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Returning to the room, he would usually begin doing something to amuse and comfort his precious boy; he would tell him stories, funny anecdotes, or would mimic comic people he had happened to meet, even imitate the howls and cries of animals.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Ilusha could not bear to see his father fooling and playing the buffoon.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though the boy tried not to show how he disliked it, he saw with an aching heart that his father was an object of contempt, and he was continually haunted by the memory of the “wisp of tow” and that “terrible day.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nina, Ilusha’s gentle, crippled sister, did not like her father’s buffoonery either (Varvara had been gone for some time past to Petersburg to study at the university).

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the half-imbecile mother was greatly diverted and laughed heartily when her husband began capering about or performing something.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was the only way she could be amused; all the rest of the time she was grumbling and complaining that now every one had forgotten her, that no one treated her with respect, that she was slighted, and so on.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But during the last few days she had completely changed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She began looking constantly at Ilusha’s bed in the corner and seemed lost in thought.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was more silent, quieter, and, if she cried, she cried quietly so as not to be heard.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain noticed the change in her with mournful perplexity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boys’ visits at first only angered her, but later on their merry shouts and stories began to divert her, and at last she liked them so much that, if the boys had given up coming, she would have felt dreary without them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: When the children told some story or played a game, she laughed and clapped her hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She called some of them to her and kissed them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was particularly fond of Smurov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As for the captain, the presence in his room of the children, who came to cheer up Ilusha, filled his heart from the first with ecstatic joy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He even hoped that Ilusha would now get over his depression, and that that would hasten his recovery.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In spite of his alarm about Ilusha, he had not, till lately, felt one minute’s doubt of his boy’s ultimate recovery.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He met his little visitors with homage, waited upon them hand and foot; he was ready to be their horse and even began letting them ride on his back, but Ilusha did not like the game and it was given up.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He began buying little things for them, gingerbread and nuts, gave them tea and cut them sandwiches.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It must be noted that all this time he had plenty of money.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had taken the two hundred roubles from Katerina Ivanovna just as Alyosha had predicted he would.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And afterwards Katerina Ivanovna, learning more about their circumstances and Ilusha’s illness, visited them herself, made the acquaintance of the family, and succeeded in fascinating the half-imbecile mother.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Since then she had been lavish in helping them, and the captain, terror-stricken at the thought that his boy might be dying, forgot his pride and humbly accepted her assistance.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All this time Doctor Herzenstube, who was called in by Katerina Ivanovna, came punctually every other day, but little was gained by his visits and he dosed the invalid mercilessly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But on that Sunday morning a new doctor was expected, who had come from Moscow, where he had a great reputation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Katerina Ivanovna had sent for him from Moscow at great expense, not expressly for Ilusha, but for another object of which more will be said in its place hereafter.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But, as he had come, she had asked him to see Ilusha as well, and the captain had been told to expect him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He hadn’t the slightest idea that Kolya Krassotkin was coming, though he had long wished for a visit from the boy for whom Ilusha was fretting.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At the moment when Krassotkin opened the door and came into the room, the captain and all the boys were round Ilusha’s bed, looking at a tiny mastiff pup, which had only been born the day before, though the captain had bespoken it a week ago to comfort and amuse Ilusha, who was still fretting over the lost and probably dead Zhutchka.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha, who had heard three days before that he was to be presented with a puppy, not an ordinary puppy, but a pedigree mastiff (a very important point, of course), tried from delicacy of feeling to pretend that he was pleased.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But his father and the boys could not help seeing that the puppy only served to recall to his little heart the thought of the unhappy dog he had killed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The puppy lay beside him feebly moving and he, smiling sadly, stroked it with his thin, pale, wasted hand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Clearly he liked the puppy, but ... it wasn’t Zhutchka; if he could have had Zhutchka and the puppy, too, then he would have been completely happy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Krassotkin!” cried one of the boys suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was the first to see him come in.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Krassotkin’s entrance made a general sensation; the boys moved away and stood on each side of the bed, so that he could get a full view of Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain ran eagerly to meet Kolya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Please come in ... you are welcome!” he said hurriedly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ilusha, Mr. Krassotkin has come to see you!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Krassotkin, shaking hands with him hurriedly, instantly showed his complete knowledge of the manners of good society.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He turned first to the captain’s wife sitting in her arm-chair, who was very ill-humored at the moment, and was grumbling that the boys stood between her and Ilusha’s bed and did not let her see the new puppy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: With the greatest courtesy he made her a bow, scraping his foot, and turning to Nina, he made her, as the only other lady present, a similar bow.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This polite behavior made an extremely favorable impression on the deranged lady.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There, you can see at once he is a young man that has been well brought up,” she commented aloud, throwing up her hands; “but as for our other visitors they come in one on the top of another.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How do you mean, mamma, one on the top of another, how is that?” muttered the captain affectionately, though a little anxious on her account.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s how they ride in. They get on each other’s shoulders in the passage and prance in like that on a respectable family. Strange sort of visitors!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But who’s come in like that, mamma?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, that boy came in riding on that one’s back and this one on that one’s.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya was already by Ilusha’s bedside.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The sick boy turned visibly paler.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He raised himself in the bed and looked intently at Kolya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya had not seen his little friend for two months, and he was overwhelmed at the sight of him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had never imagined that he would see such a wasted, yellow face, such enormous, feverishly glowing eyes and such thin little hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He saw, with grieved surprise, Ilusha’s rapid, hard breathing and dry lips.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He stepped close to him, held out his hand, and almost overwhelmed, he said:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, old man ... how are you?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But his voice failed him, he couldn’t achieve an appearance of ease; his face suddenly twitched and the corners of his mouth quivered.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha smiled a pitiful little smile, still unable to utter a word.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Something moved Kolya to raise his hand and pass it over Ilusha’s hair.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Never mind!” he murmured softly to him to cheer him up, or perhaps not knowing why he said it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For a minute they were silent again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Hallo, so you’ve got a new puppy?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya said suddenly, in a most callous voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ye—es,” answered Ilusha in a long whisper, gasping for breath.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “A black nose, that means he’ll be fierce, a good house-dog,” Kolya observed gravely and stolidly, as if the only thing he cared about was the puppy and its black nose.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But in reality he still had to do his utmost to control his feelings not to burst out crying like a child, and do what he would he could not control it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “When it grows up, you’ll have to keep it on the chain, I’m sure.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’ll be a huge dog!” cried one of the boys.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Of course he will,” “a mastiff,” “large,” “like this,” “as big as a calf,” shouted several voices.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “As big as a calf, as a real calf,” chimed in the captain.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I got one like that on purpose, one of the fiercest breed, and his parents are huge and very fierce, they stand as high as this from the floor.... Sit down here, on Ilusha’s bed, or here on the bench. You are welcome, we’ve been hoping to see you a long time.... You were so kind as to come with Alexey Fyodorovitch?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Krassotkin sat on the edge of the bed, at Ilusha’s feet.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though he had perhaps prepared a free-and-easy opening for the conversation on his way, now he completely lost the thread of it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No ... I came with Perezvon. I’ve got a dog now, called Perezvon. A Slavonic name. He’s out there ... if I whistle, he’ll run in. I’ve brought a dog, too,” he said, addressing Ilusha all at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do you remember Zhutchka, old man?” he suddenly fired the question at him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha’s little face quivered.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He looked with an agonized expression at Kolya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha, standing at the door, frowned and signed to Kolya not to speak of Zhutchka, but he did not or would not notice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Where ... is Zhutchka?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha asked in a broken voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, well, my boy, your Zhutchka’s lost and done for!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha did not speak, but he fixed an intent gaze once more on Kolya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha, catching Kolya’s eye, signed to him vigorously again, but he turned away his eyes pretending not to have noticed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It must have run away and died somewhere. It must have died after a meal like that,” Kolya pronounced pitilessly, though he seemed a little breathless.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But I’ve got a dog, Perezvon ... A Slavonic name.... I’ve brought him to show you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t want him!” said Ilusha suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, no, you really must see him ... it will amuse you.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I brought him on purpose....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He’s the same sort of shaggy dog....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: You allow me to call in my dog, madam?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He suddenly addressed Madame Snegiryov, with inexplicable excitement in his manner.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t want him, I don’t want him!” cried Ilusha, with a mournful break in his voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was a reproachful light in his eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’d better,” the captain started up from the chest by the wall on which he had just sat down, “you’d better ... another time,” he muttered, but Kolya could not be restrained.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He hurriedly shouted to Smurov, “Open the door,” and as soon as it was open, he blew his whistle.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Perezvon dashed headlong into the room.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Jump, Perezvon, beg! Beg!” shouted Kolya, jumping up, and the dog stood erect on its hind-legs by Ilusha’s bedside.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What followed was a surprise to every one: Ilusha started, lurched violently forward, bent over Perezvon and gazed at him, faint with suspense.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s ... Zhutchka!” he cried suddenly, in a voice breaking with joy and suffering.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And who did you think it was?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Krassotkin shouted with all his might, in a ringing, happy voice, and bending down he seized the dog and lifted him up to Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Look, old man, you see, blind of one eye and the left ear is torn, just the marks you described to me. It was by that I found him. I found him directly. He did not belong to any one!” he explained, turning quickly to the captain, to his wife, to Alyosha and then again to Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He used to live in the Fedotovs’ back-yard.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though he made his home there, they did not feed him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was a stray dog that had run away from the village ...

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I found him....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: You see, old man, he couldn’t have swallowed what you gave him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If he had, he must have died, he must have!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: So he must have spat it out, since he is alive.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: You did not see him do it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the pin pricked his tongue, that is why he squealed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He ran away squealing and you thought he’d swallowed it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He might well squeal, because the skin of dogs’ mouths is so tender ... tenderer than in men, much tenderer!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya cried impetuously, his face glowing and radiant with delight.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha could not speak.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: White as a sheet, he gazed open-mouthed at Kolya, with his great eyes almost starting out of his head.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And if Krassotkin, who had no suspicion of it, had known what a disastrous and fatal effect such a moment might have on the sick child’s health, nothing would have induced him to play such a trick on him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Alyosha was perhaps the only person in the room who realized it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As for the captain he behaved like a small child.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Zhutchka! It’s Zhutchka!” he cried in a blissful voice, “Ilusha, this is Zhutchka, your Zhutchka!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mamma, this is Zhutchka!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was almost weeping.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And I never guessed!” cried Smurov regretfully.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Bravo, Krassotkin! I said he’d find the dog and here he’s found him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Here he’s found him!” another boy repeated gleefully.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Krassotkin’s a brick!” cried a third voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’s a brick, he’s a brick!” cried the other boys, and they began clapping.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Wait, wait,” Krassotkin did his utmost to shout above them all.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ll tell you how it happened, that’s the whole point. I found him, I took him home and hid him at once. I kept him locked up at home and did not show him to any one till to-day. Only Smurov has known for the last fortnight, but I assured him this dog was called Perezvon and he did not guess. And meanwhile I taught the dog all sorts of tricks. You should only see all the things he can do! I trained him so as to bring you a well-trained dog, in good condition, old man, so as to be able to say to you, ‘See, old man, what a fine dog your Zhutchka is now! Haven’t you a bit of meat? He’ll show you a trick that will make you die with laughing. A piece of meat, haven’t you got any?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain ran across the passage to the landlady, where their cooking was done.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Not to lose precious time, Kolya, in desperate haste, shouted to Perezvon, “Dead! And the dog immediately turned round and lay on his back with its four paws in the air. The boys laughed. Ilusha looked on with the same suffering smile, but the person most delighted with the dog’s performance was “mamma. She laughed at the dog and began snapping her fingers and calling it, “Perezvon, Perezvon!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nothing will make him get up, nothing!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya cried triumphantly, proud of his success.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He won’t move for all the shouting in the world, but if I call to him, he’ll jump up in a minute.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ici, Perezvon!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The dog leapt up and bounded about, whining with delight.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain ran back with a piece of cooked beef.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Is it hot? Kolya inquired hurriedly, with a business-like air, taking the meat. “Dogs don’t like hot things. No, it’s all right. Look, everybody, look, Ilusha, look, old man; why aren’t you looking? He does not look at him, now I’ve brought him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The new trick consisted in making the dog stand motionless with his nose out and putting a tempting morsel of meat just on his nose.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The luckless dog had to stand without moving, with the meat on his nose, as long as his master chose to keep him, without a movement, perhaps for half an hour.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But he kept Perezvon only for a brief moment.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Paid for!” cried Kolya, and the meat passed in a flash from the dog’s nose to his mouth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The audience, of course, expressed enthusiasm and surprise.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Can you really have put off coming all this time simply to train the dog?” exclaimed Alyosha, with an involuntary note of reproach in his voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Simply for that!” answered Kolya, with perfect simplicity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I wanted to show him in all his glory.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Perezvon! Perezvon,” called Ilusha suddenly, snapping his thin fingers and beckoning to the dog.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What is it?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Let him jump up on the bed!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ici, Perezvon!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya slapped the bed and Perezvon darted up by Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boy threw both arms round his head and Perezvon instantly licked his cheek.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha crept close to him, stretched himself out in bed and hid his face in the dog’s shaggy coat.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Dear, dear!” kept exclaiming the captain.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya sat down again on the edge of the bed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ilusha, I can show you another trick. I’ve brought you a little cannon. You remember, I told you about it before and you said how much you’d like to see it. Well, here, I’ve brought it to you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And Kolya hurriedly pulled out of his satchel the little bronze cannon.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He hurried, because he was happy himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Another time he would have waited till the sensation made by Perezvon had passed off, now he hurried on regardless of all consideration.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are all happy now,” he felt, “so here’s something to make you happier!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was perfectly enchanted himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve been coveting this thing for a long while; it’s for you, old man, it’s for you. It belonged to Morozov, it was no use to him, he had it from his brother. I swopped a book from father’s book-case for it, A Kinsman of Mahomet or Salutary Folly, a scandalous book published in Moscow a hundred years ago, before they had any censorship. And Morozov has a taste for such things. He was grateful to me, too....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya held the cannon in his hand so that all could see and admire it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha raised himself, and, with his right arm still round the dog, he gazed enchanted at the toy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The sensation was even greater when Kolya announced that he had gunpowder too, and that it could be fired off at once “if it won’t alarm the ladies. “Mamma” immediately asked to look at the toy closer and her request was granted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was much pleased with the little bronze cannon on wheels and began rolling it to and fro on her lap.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She readily gave permission for the cannon to be fired, without any idea of what she had been asked.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya showed the powder and the shot.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain, as a military man, undertook to load it, putting in a minute quantity of powder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He asked that the shot might be put off till another time.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The cannon was put on the floor, aiming towards an empty part of the room, three grains of powder were thrust into the touch-hole and a match was put to it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A magnificent explosion followed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mamma was startled, but at once laughed with delight.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boys gazed in speechless triumph.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the captain, looking at Ilusha, was more enchanted than any of them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya picked up the cannon and immediately presented it to Ilusha, together with the powder and the shot.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I got it for you, for you! I’ve been keeping it for you a long time,” he repeated once more in his delight.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, give it to me! No, give me the cannon!” mamma began begging like a little child.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Her face showed a piteous fear that she would not get it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya was disconcerted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain fidgeted uneasily.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mamma, mamma,” he ran to her, “the cannon’s yours, of course, but let Ilusha have it, because it’s a present to him, but it’s just as good as yours. Ilusha will always let you play with it; it shall belong to both of you, both of you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, I don’t want it to belong to both of us, I want it to be mine altogether, not Ilusha’s,” persisted mamma, on the point of tears.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Take it, mother, here, keep it! Ilusha cried. “Krassotkin, may I give it to my mother?” he turned to Krassotkin with an imploring face, as though he were afraid he might be offended at his giving his present to some one else.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Of course you may,” Krassotkin assented heartily, and, taking the cannon from Ilusha, he handed it himself to mamma with a polite bow.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was so touched that she cried.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ilusha, darling, he’s the one who loves his mamma!” she said tenderly, and at once began wheeling the cannon to and fro on her lap again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mamma, let me kiss your hand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain darted up to her at once and did so.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

text: “That would have more effect on you than anything.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, how I regret and blame myself for not having come sooner!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya exclaimed, with bitter feeling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, it’s a great pity. You saw for yourself how delighted the poor child was to see you. And how he fretted for you to come!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t tell me! You make it worse! But it serves me right. What kept me from coming was my conceit, my egoistic vanity, and the beastly wilfullness, which I never can get rid of, though I’ve been struggling with it all my life. I see that now. I am a beast in lots of ways, Karamazov!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, you have a charming nature, though it’s been distorted, and I quite understand why you have had such an influence on this generous, morbidly sensitive boy,” Alyosha answered warmly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And you say that to me!” cried Kolya; “and would you believe it, I thought—I’ve thought several times since I’ve been here—that you despised me! If only you knew how I prize your opinion!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But are you really so sensitive? At your age! Would you believe it, just now, when you were telling your story, I thought, as I watched you, that you must be very sensitive!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You thought so? What an eye you’ve got, I say! I bet that was when I was talking about the goose. That was just when I was fancying you had a great contempt for me for being in such a hurry to show off, and for a moment I quite hated you for it, and began talking like a fool. Then I fancied—just now, here—when I said that if there were no God He would have to be invented, that I was in too great a hurry to display my knowledge, especially as I got that phrase out of a book. But I swear I wasn’t showing off out of vanity, though I really don’t know why. Because I was so pleased? Yes, I believe it was because I was so pleased ... though it’s perfectly disgraceful for any one to be gushing directly they are pleased, I know that. But I am convinced now that you don’t despise me; it was all my imagination. Oh, Karamazov, I am profoundly unhappy. I sometimes fancy all sorts of things, that every one is laughing at me, the whole world, and then I feel ready to overturn the whole order of things.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And you worry every one about you,” smiled Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, I worry every one about me, especially my mother. Karamazov, tell me, am I very ridiculous now?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t think about that, don’t think of it at all!” cried Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And what does ridiculous mean? Isn’t every one constantly being or seeming ridiculous? Besides, nearly all clever people now are fearfully afraid of being ridiculous, and that makes them unhappy. All I am surprised at is that you should be feeling that so early, though I’ve observed it for some time past, and not only in you. Nowadays the very children have begun to suffer from it. It’s almost a sort of insanity. The devil has taken the form of that vanity and entered into the whole generation; it’s simply the devil,” added Alyosha, without a trace of the smile that Kolya, staring at him, expected to see.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are like every one else,” said Alyosha, in conclusion, “that is, like very many others. Only you must not be like everybody else, that’s all.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Even if every one is like that?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, even if every one is like that. You be the only one not like it. You really are not like every one else, here you are not ashamed to confess to something bad and even ridiculous. And who will admit so much in these days? No one. And people have even ceased to feel the impulse to self-criticism. Don’t be like every one else, even if you are the only one.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Splendid! I was not mistaken in you. You know how to console one. Oh, how I have longed to know you, Karamazov! I’ve long been eager for this meeting. Can you really have thought about me, too? You said just now that you thought of me, too?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, I’d heard of you and had thought of you, too ... and if it’s partly vanity that makes you ask, it doesn’t matter.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do you know, Karamazov, our talk has been like a declaration of love,” said Kolya, in a bashful and melting voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s not ridiculous, is it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not at all ridiculous, and if it were, it wouldn’t matter, because it’s been a good thing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha smiled brightly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But do you know, Karamazov, you must admit that you are a little ashamed yourself, now....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I see it by your eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya smiled with a sort of sly happiness.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why ashamed?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, why are you blushing?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It was you made me blush,” laughed Alyosha, and he really did blush.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, well, I am a little, goodness knows why, I don’t know...” he muttered, almost embarrassed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His cheeks glowed, his eyes beamed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You know, Kolya, you will be very unhappy in your life,” something made Alyosha say suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I know, I know.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya agreed at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov

Do you know, all this last month, I’ve been saying to myself, ‘Either we shall be friends at once, for ever, or we shall part enemies to the grave!’”

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov

And I’ll bring Perezvon, but now I will take him with me, because he will begin to howl when I am away and bother you. Good-by!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And he ran out into the passage.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

text: “Kolya, you must be sure to keep your word and come, or he will be terribly disappointed,” Alyosha said emphatically.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov

text: He stood before the two and flung up his arms.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “If I forget thee, Jerusalem, may my tongue—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha went towards the cathedral square to the widow Morozov’s house to see Grushenka, who had sent Fenya to him early in the morning with an urgent message begging him to come.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Questioning Fenya, Alyosha learned that her mistress had been particularly distressed since the previous day.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: During the two months that had passed since Mitya’s arrest, Alyosha had called frequently at the widow Morozov’s house, both from his own inclination and to take messages for Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Three days after Mitya’s arrest, Grushenka was taken very ill and was ill for nearly five weeks.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For one whole week she was unconscious.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was very much changed—thinner and a little sallow, though she had for the past fortnight been well enough to go out.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But to Alyosha her face was even more attractive than before, and he liked to meet her eyes when he went in to her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A look of firmness and intelligent purpose had developed in her face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There were signs of a spiritual transformation in her, and a steadfast, fine and humble determination that nothing could shake could be discerned in her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was a small vertical line between her brows which gave her charming face a look of concentrated thought, almost austere at the first glance.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was scarcely a trace of her former frivolity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It seemed strange to Alyosha, too, that in spite of the calamity that had overtaken the poor girl, betrothed to a man who had been arrested for a terrible crime, almost at the instant of their betrothal, in spite of her illness and the almost inevitable sentence hanging over Mitya, Grushenka had not yet lost her youthful cheerfulness.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was a soft light in the once proud eyes, though at times they gleamed with the old vindictive fire when she was visited by one disturbing thought stronger than ever in her heart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The object of that uneasiness was the same as ever—Katerina Ivanovna, of whom Grushenka had even raved when she lay in delirium.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha knew that she was fearfully jealous of her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yet Katerina Ivanovna had not once visited Mitya in his prison, though she might have done it whenever she liked.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All this made a difficult problem for Alyosha, for he was the only person to whom Grushenka opened her heart and from whom she was continually asking advice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Sometimes he was unable to say anything.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov

I’ve been to see him also. And I shall send him some pies, too, on purpose. I hadn’t sent him any, but Mitya accused me of it, so now I shall send some! Ah, here’s Fenya with a letter! Yes, it’s from the Poles—begging again!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
