text: Indeed, when the witnesses à décharge, that is, called by the defense, began giving evidence, fortune seemed all at once markedly more favorable to Mitya, and what was particularly striking, this was a surprise even to the counsel for the defense.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But before Katerina Ivanovna was called, Alyosha was examined, and he recalled a fact which seemed to furnish positive evidence against one important point made by the prosecution.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It came quite as a surprise even to Alyosha himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was not required to take the oath, and I remember that both sides addressed him very gently and sympathetically.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was evident that his reputation for goodness had preceded him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha gave his evidence modestly and with restraint, but his warm sympathy for his unhappy brother was unmistakable.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In answer to one question, he sketched his brother’s character as that of a man, violent-tempered perhaps and carried away by his passions, but at the same time honorable, proud and generous, capable of self-sacrifice, if necessary.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He admitted, however, that, through his passion for Grushenka and his rivalry with his father, his brother had been of late in an intolerable position.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But he repelled with indignation the suggestion that his brother might have committed a murder for the sake of gain, though he recognized that the three thousand roubles had become almost an obsession with Mitya; that he looked upon them as part of the inheritance he had been cheated of by his father, and that, indifferent as he was to money as a rule, he could not even speak of that three thousand without fury.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As for the rivalry of the two “ladies,” as the prosecutor expressed it—that is, of Grushenka and Katya—he answered evasively and was even unwilling to answer one or two questions altogether.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Did your brother tell you, anyway, that he intended to kill your father?” asked the prosecutor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You can refuse to answer if you think necessary,” he added.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He did not tell me so directly,” answered Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How so? Did he indirectly?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He spoke to me once of his hatred for our father and his fear that at an extreme moment ... at a moment of fury, he might perhaps murder him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And you believed him?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I am afraid to say that I did. But I never doubted that some higher feeling would always save him at the fatal moment, as it has indeed saved him, for it was not he killed my father,” Alyosha said firmly, in a loud voice that was heard throughout the court.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The prosecutor started like a war-horse at the sound of a trumpet.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Let me assure you that I fully believe in the complete sincerity of your conviction and do not explain it by or identify it with your affection for your unhappy brother. Your peculiar view of the whole tragic episode is known to us already from the preliminary investigation. I won’t attempt to conceal from you that it is highly individual and contradicts all the other evidence collected by the prosecution. And so I think it essential to press you to tell me what facts have led you to this conviction of your brother’s innocence and of the guilt of another person against whom you gave evidence at the preliminary inquiry?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I only answered the questions asked me at the preliminary inquiry,” replied Alyosha, slowly and calmly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I made no accusation against Smerdyakov of myself.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yet you gave evidence against him?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I was led to do so by my brother Dmitri’s words. I was told what took place at his arrest and how he had pointed to Smerdyakov before I was examined. I believe absolutely that my brother is innocent, and if he didn’t commit the murder, then—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Then Smerdyakov? Why Smerdyakov? And why are you so completely persuaded of your brother’s innocence?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I cannot help believing my brother. I know he wouldn’t lie to me. I saw from his face he wasn’t lying.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Only from his face? Is that all the proof you have?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I have no other proof.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And of Smerdyakov’s guilt you have no proof whatever but your brother’s word and the expression of his face?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, I have no other proof.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The prosecutor dropped the examination at this point.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The impression left by Alyosha’s evidence on the public was most disappointing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There had been talk about Smerdyakov before the trial; some one had heard something, some one had pointed out something else, it was said that Alyosha had gathered together some extraordinary proofs of his brother’s innocence and Smerdyakov’s guilt, and after all there was nothing, no evidence except certain moral convictions so natural in a brother.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Fetyukovitch began his cross-examination.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: On his asking Alyosha when it was that the prisoner had told him of his hatred for his father and that he might kill him, and whether he had heard it, for instance, at their last meeting before the catastrophe, Alyosha started as he answered, as though only just recollecting and understanding something.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

It is true that after he had taken the final decision, he must have felt apprehensive that he had talked too much about his design beforehand, and that this might lead to his arrest and prosecution afterwards. But there was nothing for it; he could not take his words back, but his luck had served him before, it would serve him again. He believed in his star, you know! The elder of these brothers expressed his suspicions only to-day, when he was undoubtedly suffering from brain fever. But we know that for the last two months he has completely shared our conviction of his brother’s guilt and did not attempt to combat that idea. But of that later. He depicted him as a man of weak intellect, with a smattering of education, who had been thrown off his balance by philosophical ideas above his level and certain modern theories of duty, which he learnt in practice from the reckless life of his master, who was also perhaps his father—Fyodor Pavlovitch; and, theoretically, from various strange philosophical conversations with his master’s elder son, Ivan Fyodorovitch, who readily indulged in this diversion, probably feeling dull or wishing to amuse himself at the valet’s expense. “He spoke to me himself of his spiritual condition during the last few days at his father’s house,” Ippolit Kirillovitch explained; “but others too have borne witness to it—the prisoner himself, his brother, and the servant Grigory—that is, all who knew him well.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Moreover, Smerdyakov, whose health was shaken by his attacks of epilepsy, had not the courage of a chicken.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘He fell at my feet and kissed them,’ the prisoner himself has told us, before he realized how damaging such a statement was to himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

text: And the prisoner chose him for his confidant (we have his own word for it) and he frightened him into consenting at last to act as a spy for him.

text: In that capacity he deceived his master, revealing to the prisoner the existence of the envelope with the notes in it and the signals by means of which he could get into the house.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘He suspected me at every instant. In fear and trembling I hastened to tell him every secret to pacify him, that he might see that I had not deceived him and let me off alive. Those are his own words. I wrote them down and I remember them. ‘When he began shouting at me, I would fall on my knees.’

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: So it may be supposed that the poor fellow suffered pangs of remorse at having deceived his master, whom he loved as his benefactor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Persons severely afflicted with epilepsy are, so the most skillful doctors tell us, always prone to continual and morbid self-reproach.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They worry over their ‘wickedness,’ they are tormented by pangs of conscience, often entirely without cause; they exaggerate and often invent all sorts of faults and crimes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And here we have a man of that type who had really been driven to wrong-doing by terror and intimidation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: When Ivan Fyodorovitch was leaving for Moscow, just before the catastrophe, Smerdyakov besought him to remain, though he was too timid to tell him plainly what he feared.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He confined himself to hints, but his hints were not understood.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It must be observed that he looked on Ivan Fyodorovitch as a protector, whose presence in the house was a guarantee that no harm would come to pass.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Remember the phrase in Dmitri Karamazov’s drunken letter, ‘I shall kill the old man, if only Ivan goes away. So Ivan Fyodorovitch’s presence seemed to every one a guarantee of peace and order in the house.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But he went away, and within an hour of his young master’s departure Smerdyakov was taken with an epileptic fit.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Here I must mention that Smerdyakov, oppressed by terror and despair of a sort, had felt during those last few days that one of the fits from which he had suffered before at moments of strain, might be coming upon him again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The day and hour of such an attack cannot, of course, be foreseen, but every epileptic can feel beforehand that he is likely to have one.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: So the doctors tell us.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And so, as soon as Ivan Fyodorovitch had driven out of the yard, Smerdyakov, depressed by his lonely and unprotected position, went to the cellar.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He went down the stairs wondering if he would have a fit or not, and what if it were to come upon him at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And that very apprehension, that very wonder, brought on the spasm in his throat that always precedes such attacks, and he fell unconscious into the cellar.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And in this perfectly natural occurrence people try to detect a suspicion, a hint that he was shamming an attack on purpose.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But, if it were on purpose, the question arises at once, what was his motive?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What was he reckoning on?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What was he aiming at?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I say nothing about medicine: science, I am told, may go astray: the doctors were not able to discriminate between the counterfeit and the real.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That may be so, but answer me one question: what motive had he for such a counterfeit?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Could he, had he been plotting the murder, have desired to attract the attention of the household by having a fit just before?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You see, gentlemen of the jury, on the night of the murder, there were five persons in Fyodor Pavlovitch’s—Fyodor Pavlovitch himself (but he did not kill himself, that’s evident); then his servant, Grigory, but he was almost killed himself; the third person was Grigory’s wife, Marfa Ignatyevna, but it would be simply shameful to imagine her murdering her master.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Two persons are left—the prisoner and Smerdyakov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But, if we are to believe the prisoner’s statement that he is not the murderer, then Smerdyakov must have been, for there is no other alternative, no one else can be found.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That is what accounts for the artful, astounding accusation against the unhappy idiot who committed suicide yesterday.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Had a shadow of suspicion rested on any one else, had there been any sixth person, I am persuaded that even the prisoner would have been ashamed to accuse Smerdyakov, and would have accused that sixth person, for to charge Smerdyakov with that murder is perfectly absurd.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Gentlemen, let us lay aside psychology, let us lay aside medicine, let us even lay aside logic, let us turn only to the facts and see what the facts tell us.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If Smerdyakov killed him, how did he do it?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alone or with the assistance of the prisoner?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Let us consider the first alternative—that he did it alone.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If he had killed him it must have been with some object, for some advantage to himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But not having a shadow of the motive that the prisoner had for the murder—hatred, jealousy, and so on—Smerdyakov could only have murdered him for the sake of gain, in order to appropriate the three thousand roubles he had seen his master put in the envelope.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And yet he tells another person—and a person most closely interested, that is, the prisoner—everything about the money and the signals, where the envelope lay, what was written on it, what it was tied up with, and, above all, told him of those signals by which he could enter the house.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Did he do this simply to betray himself, or to invite to the same enterprise one who would be anxious to get that envelope for himself?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘Yes,’ I shall be told, ‘but he betrayed it from fear.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But how do you explain this?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A man who could conceive such an audacious, savage act, and carry it out, tells facts which are known to no one else in the world, and which, if he held his tongue, no one would ever have guessed!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, however cowardly he might be, if he had plotted such a crime, nothing would have induced him to tell any one about the envelope and the signals, for that was as good as betraying himself beforehand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He would have invented something, he would have told some lie if he had been forced to give information, but he would have been silent about that.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For, on the other hand, if he had said nothing about the money, but had committed the murder and stolen the money, no one in the world could have charged him with murder for the sake of robbery, since no one but he had seen the money, no one but he knew of its existence in the house.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Even if he had been accused of the murder, it could only have been thought that he had committed it from some other motive.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But since no one had observed any such motive in him beforehand, and every one saw, on the contrary, that his master was fond of him and honored him with his confidence, he would, of course, have been the last to be suspected.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: People would have suspected first the man who had a motive, a man who had himself declared he had such motives, who had made no secret of it; they would, in fact, have suspected the son of the murdered man, Dmitri Fyodorovitch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Had Smerdyakov killed and robbed him, and the son been accused of it, that would, of course, have suited Smerdyakov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yet are we to believe that, though plotting the murder, he told that son, Dmitri, about the money, the envelope, and the signals?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Is that logical?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Is that clear?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “When the day of the murder planned by Smerdyakov came, we have him falling downstairs in a feigned fit—with what object?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In the first place that Grigory, who had been intending to take his medicine, might put it off and remain on guard, seeing there was no one to look after the house, and, in the second place, I suppose, that his master seeing that there was no one to guard him, and in terror of a visit from his son, might redouble his vigilance and precaution.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And, most of all, I suppose that he, Smerdyakov, disabled by the fit, might be carried from the kitchen, where he always slept, apart from all the rest, and where he could go in and out as he liked, to Grigory’s room at the other end of the lodge, where he was always put, shut off by a screen three paces from their own bed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This was the immemorial custom established by his master and the kind-hearted Marfa Ignatyevna, whenever he had a fit.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There, lying behind the screen, he would most likely, to keep up the sham, have begun groaning, and so keeping them awake all night (as Grigory and his wife testified).

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And all this, we are to believe, that he might more conveniently get up and murder his master!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But I shall be told that he shammed illness on purpose that he might not be suspected and that he told the prisoner of the money and the signals to tempt him to commit the murder, and when he had murdered him and had gone away with the money, making a noise, most likely, and waking people, Smerdyakov got up, am I to believe, and went in—what for?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: To murder his master a second time and carry off the money that had already been stolen?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Gentlemen, are you laughing?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I am ashamed to put forward such suggestions, but, incredible as it seems, that’s just what the prisoner alleges.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: When he had left the house, had knocked Grigory down and raised an alarm, he tells us Smerdyakov got up, went in and murdered his master and stole the money!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I won’t press the point that Smerdyakov could hardly have reckoned on this beforehand, and have foreseen that the furious and exasperated son would simply come to peep in respectfully, though he knew the signals, and beat a retreat, leaving Smerdyakov his booty.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Gentlemen of the jury, I put this question to you in earnest; when was the moment when Smerdyakov could have committed his crime?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Name that moment, or you can’t accuse him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But, perhaps, the fit was a real one, the sick man suddenly recovered, heard a shout, and went out.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Well—what then?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He looked about him and said, ‘Why not go and kill the master? And how did he know what had happened, since he had been lying unconscious till that moment? But there’s a limit to these flights of fancy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “‘Quite so,’ some astute people will tell me, ‘but what if they were in agreement?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What if they murdered him together and shared the money—what then?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A weighty question, truly!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And the facts to confirm it are astounding.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: One commits the murder and takes all the trouble while his accomplice lies on one side shamming a fit, apparently to arouse suspicion in every one, alarm in his master and alarm in Grigory.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It would be interesting to know what motives could have induced the two accomplices to form such an insane plan.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But as this attack of Smerdyakov’s was bound to throw the household into confusion, Dmitri Karamazov could never have agreed to such a plan.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I will waive that point however.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Supposing that he did agree, it would still follow that Dmitri Karamazov is the murderer and the instigator, and Smerdyakov is only a passive accomplice, and not even an accomplice, but merely acquiesced against his will through terror.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But what do we see?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As soon as he is arrested the prisoner instantly throws all the blame on Smerdyakov, not accusing him of being his accomplice, but of being himself the murderer.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘He did it alone,’ he says.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘He murdered and robbed him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was the work of his hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Strange sort of accomplices who begin to accuse one another at once!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And think of the risk for Karamazov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: After committing the murder while his accomplice lay in bed, he throws the blame on the invalid, who might well have resented it and in self-preservation might well have confessed the truth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For he might well have seen that the court would at once judge how far he was responsible, and so he might well have reckoned that if he were punished, it would be far less severely than the real murderer.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But in that case he would have been certain to make a confession, yet he has not done so.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Smerdyakov never hinted at their complicity, though the actual murderer persisted in accusing him and declaring that he had committed the crime alone.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What’s more, Smerdyakov at the inquiry volunteered the statement that it was he who had told the prisoner of the envelope of notes and of the signals, and that, but for him, he would have known nothing about them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If he had really been a guilty accomplice, would he so readily have made this statement at the inquiry?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: On the contrary, he would have tried to conceal it, to distort the facts or minimize them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But he was far from distorting or minimizing them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: No one but an innocent man, who had no fear of being charged with complicity, could have acted as he did.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And in a fit of melancholy arising from his disease and this catastrophe he hanged himself yesterday.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He left a note written in his peculiar language, ‘I destroy myself of my own will and inclination so as to throw no blame on any one. What would it have cost him to add: ‘I am the murderer, not Karamazov’?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But that he did not add.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Did his conscience lead him to suicide and not to avowing his guilt?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And what followed?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Notes for three thousand roubles were brought into the court just now, and we were told that they were the same that lay in the envelope now on the table before us, and that the witness had received them from Smerdyakov the day before.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But I need not recall the painful scene, though I will make one or two comments, selecting such trivial ones as might not be obvious at first sight to every one, and so may be overlooked.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In the first place, Smerdyakov must have given back the money and hanged himself yesterday from remorse.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And only yesterday he confessed his guilt to Ivan Karamazov, as the latter informs us.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If it were not so, indeed, why should Ivan Fyodorovitch have kept silence till now?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And so, if he has confessed, then why, I ask again, did he not avow the whole truth in the last letter he left behind, knowing that the innocent prisoner had to face this terrible ordeal the next day?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The money alone is no proof.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A week ago, quite by chance, the fact came to the knowledge of myself and two other persons in this court that Ivan Fyodorovitch had sent two five per cent.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: coupons of five thousand each—that is, ten thousand in all—to the chief town of the province to be changed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I only mention this to point out that any one may have money, and that it can’t be proved that these notes are the same as were in Fyodor Pavlovitch’s envelope.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ivan Karamazov, after receiving yesterday a communication of such importance from the real murderer, did not stir.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why didn’t he report it at once?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why did he put it all off till morning?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I think I have a right to conjecture why.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His health had been giving way for a week past: he had admitted to a doctor and to his most intimate friends that he was suffering from hallucinations and seeing phantoms of the dead: he was on the eve of the attack of brain fever by which he has been stricken down to-day.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In this condition he suddenly heard of Smerdyakov’s death, and at once reflected, ‘The man is dead, I can throw the blame on him and save my brother. I have money. I will take a roll of notes and say that Smerdyakov gave them me before his death. You will say that was dishonorable: it’s dishonorable to slander even the dead, and even to save a brother. True, but what if he slandered him unconsciously? What if, finally unhinged by the sudden news of the valet’s death, he imagined it really was so? You saw the recent scene: you have seen the witness’s condition.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was standing up and was speaking, but where was his mind?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Then followed the document, the prisoner’s letter written two days before the crime, and containing a complete program of the murder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why, then, are we looking for any other program?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The crime was committed precisely according to this program, and by no other than the writer of it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yes, gentlemen of the jury, it went off without a hitch!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He did not run respectfully and timidly away from his father’s window, though he was firmly convinced that the object of his affections was with him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: No, that is absurd and unlikely!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He went in and murdered him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Most likely he killed him in anger, burning with resentment, as soon as he looked on his hated rival.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But having killed him, probably with one blow of the brass pestle, and having convinced himself, after careful search, that she was not there, he did not, however, forget to put his hand under the pillow and take out the envelope, the torn cover of which lies now on the table before us.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I mention this fact that you may note one, to my thinking, very characteristic circumstance.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Had he been an experienced murderer and had he committed the murder for the sake of gain only, would he have left the torn envelope on the floor as it was found, beside the corpse?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Had it been Smerdyakov, for instance, murdering his master to rob him, he would have simply carried away the envelope with him, without troubling himself to open it over his victim’s corpse, for he would have known for certain that the notes were in the envelope—they had been put in and sealed up in his presence—and had he taken the envelope with him, no one would ever have known of the robbery.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I ask you, gentlemen, would Smerdyakov have behaved in that way?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Would he have left the envelope on the floor?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, this was the action of a frantic murderer, a murderer who was not a thief and had never stolen before that day, who snatched the notes from under the pillow, not like a thief stealing them, but as though seizing his own property from the thief who had stolen it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For that was the idea which had become almost an insane obsession in Dmitri Karamazov in regard to that money.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And pouncing upon the envelope, which he had never seen before, he tore it open to make sure whether the money was in it, and ran away with the money in his pocket, even forgetting to consider that he had left an astounding piece of evidence against himself in that torn envelope on the floor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All because it was Karamazov, not Smerdyakov, he didn’t think, he didn’t reflect, and how should he?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He ran away; he heard behind him the servant cry out; the old man caught him, stopped him and was felled to the ground by the brass pestle.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The prisoner, moved by pity, leapt down to look at him. Would you believe it, he tells us that he leapt down out of pity, out of compassion, to see whether he could do anything for him. Was that a moment to show compassion? No; he jumped down simply to make certain whether the only witness of his crime were dead or alive. Any other feeling, any other motive would be unnatural. Note that he took trouble over Grigory, wiped his head with his handkerchief and, convincing himself he was dead, he ran to the house of his mistress, dazed and covered with blood. How was it he never thought that he was covered with blood and would be at once detected? But the prisoner himself assures us that he did not even notice that he was covered with blood. That may be believed, that is very possible, that always happens at such moments with criminals. On one point they will show diabolical cunning, while another will escape them altogether. But he was thinking at that moment of one thing only—where was she? He wanted to find out at once where she was, so he ran to her lodging and learnt an unexpected and astounding piece of news—she had gone off to Mokroe to meet her first lover.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ippolit Kirillovitch had chosen the historical method of exposition, beloved by all nervous orators, who find in its limitation a check on their own eager rhetoric.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At this moment in his speech he went off into a dissertation on Grushenka’s “first lover,” and brought forward several interesting thoughts on this theme.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Karamazov, who had been frantically jealous of every one, collapsed, so to speak, and effaced himself at once before this first lover.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What makes it all the more strange is that he seems to have hardly thought of this formidable rival.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But he had looked upon him as a remote danger, and Karamazov always lives in the present.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Possibly he regarded him as a fiction.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But his wounded heart grasped instantly that the woman had been concealing this new rival and deceiving him, because he was anything but a fiction to her, because he was the one hope of her life.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grasping this instantly, he resigned himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Gentlemen of the jury, I cannot help dwelling on this unexpected trait in the prisoner’s character.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He suddenly evinces an irresistible desire for justice, a respect for woman and a recognition of her right to love.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And all this at the very moment when he had stained his hands with his father’s blood for her sake!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It is true that the blood he had shed was already crying out for vengeance, for, after having ruined his soul and his life in this world, he was forced to ask himself at that same instant what he was and what he could be now to her, to that being, dearer to him than his own soul, in comparison with that former lover who had returned penitent, with new love, to the woman he had once betrayed, with honorable offers, with the promise of a reformed and happy life.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And he, luckless man, what could he give her now, what could he offer her?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Karamazov felt all this, knew that all ways were barred to him by his crime and that he was a criminal under sentence, and not a man with life before him!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This thought crushed him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And so he instantly flew to one frantic plan, which, to a man of Karamazov’s character, must have appeared the one inevitable way out of his terrible position.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That way out was suicide.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He ran for the pistols he had left in pledge with his friend Perhotin and on the way, as he ran, he pulled out of his pocket the money, for the sake of which he had stained his hands with his father’s gore.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh, now he needed money more than ever.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Karamazov would die, Karamazov would shoot himself and it should be remembered!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: To be sure, he was a poet and had burnt the candle at both ends all his life.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘To her, to her! and there, oh, there I will give a feast to the whole world, such as never was before, that will be remembered and talked of long after! In the midst of shouts of wild merriment, reckless gypsy songs and dances I shall raise the glass and drink to the woman I adore and her new-found happiness! And then, on the spot, at her feet, I shall dash out my brains before her and punish myself! She will remember Mitya Karamazov sometimes, she will see how Mitya loved her, she will feel for Mitya!’

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Here we see in excess a love of effect, a romantic despair and sentimentality, and the wild recklessness of the Karamazovs. Yes, but there is something else, gentlemen of the jury, something that cries out in the soul, throbs incessantly in the mind, and poisons the heart unto death—that something is conscience, gentlemen of the jury, its judgment, its terrible torments! The pistol will settle everything, the pistol is the only way out! But beyond—I don’t know whether Karamazov wondered at that moment ‘What lies beyond,’ and whether Karamazov could, like Hamlet, wonder ‘What lies beyond. No, gentlemen of the jury, they have their Hamlets, but we still have our Karamazovs!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Here Ippolit Kirillovitch drew a minute picture of Mitya’s preparations, the scene at Perhotin’s, at the shop, with the drivers.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He quoted numerous words and actions, confirmed by witnesses, and the picture made a terrible impression on the audience.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The guilt of this harassed and desperate man stood out clear and convincing, when the facts were brought together.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

Our fatal troika dashes on in her headlong flight perhaps to destruction and in all Russia for long past men have stretched out imploring hands and called a halt to its furious reckless course. title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He went straight to the point, and began by saying that although he practiced in Petersburg, he had more than once visited provincial towns to defend prisoners, of whose innocence he had a conviction or at least a preconceived idea.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “From the very first accounts in the newspapers I was struck by something which strongly prepossessed me in the prisoner’s favor. What interested me most was a fact which often occurs in legal practice, but rarely, I think, in such an extreme and peculiar form as in the present case. I ought to formulate that peculiarity only at the end of my speech, but I will do so at the very beginning, for it is my weakness to go to work directly, not keeping my effects in reserve and economizing my material. That may be imprudent on my part, but at least it’s sincere. What I have in my mind is this: there is an overwhelming chain of evidence against the prisoner, and at the same time not one fact that will stand criticism, if it is examined separately. As I followed the case more closely in the papers my idea was more and more confirmed, and I suddenly received from the prisoner’s relatives a request to undertake his defense. I at once hurried here, and here I became completely convinced. It was to break down this terrible chain of facts, and to show that each piece of evidence taken separately was unproved and fantastic, that I undertook the case.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: So Fetyukovitch began.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Gentlemen of the jury,” he suddenly protested, “I am new to this district. I have no preconceived ideas. The prisoner, a man of turbulent and unbridled temper, has not insulted me. But he has insulted perhaps hundreds of persons in this town, and so prejudiced many people against him beforehand. Of course I recognize that the moral sentiment of local society is justly excited against him. The prisoner is of turbulent and violent temper. Yet he was received in society here; he was even welcome in the family of my talented friend, the prosecutor.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: (N.B. At these words there were two or three laughs in the audience, quickly suppressed, but noticed by all.
